description: The topbar QUEUE badge builds ConsoleStatus -> TaskQueueHealth#status on every HTML page render. status calls blocking_check_count which includes agent_done_without_proof_count (task_queue_health.rb:199-204): it loads EVERY done agent-sourced task ever created into memory (.to_a) and, per task, runs completion_proof_present? plus a separate task_events EXISTS query — one extra query per historical task, forever growing. It also parses every needs_approval task body through TaskNotes (lines 221-236). The same work repeats for the /api/v1/task_queue_health endpoint agents poll.
failure_or_value: Every page Brian opens (and every agent poll) pays a cost linear in total done-task history. With agents filing dozens of cards a day since the Google Tasks cutover, this is hundreds of rows + hundreds of queries per page render within months — a steadily degrading console, worst on phone over cellular. It is pure read-model work with no per-request freshness requirement.
fix_sketch: Two additive steps: (1) collapse agent_done_without_proof_count to one SQL query — done agent tasks WHERE NOT (jsonb proof keys present) AND NOT EXISTS (task_events with event_type IN ('completed','applied','sent','executed')) — expressing completion_proof_present? as a jsonb predicate; optionally bound it to completed_at >= 90.days.ago (older leaks are already surfaced/handled). (2) cache the whole TaskQueueHealth#as_json/status per organization in Rails.cache (Solid Cache) for 30-60s, keyed on org id + Task.maximum(:updated_at); the badge tolerates a minute of staleness. Keep the JSON shape identical for the polling agents.

verdict.reason: Verified on the real code path: layouts/application.html.erb renders _topbar/_sidebar_nav/_mobile_bottom_nav on every HTML page; the topbar calls shell_status.task_sync_label and queue_checks, which drive TaskQueueHealth#status -> blocking_check_count -> agent_done_without_proof_count. task_queue_health.rb:199-204 loads EVERY done agent-sourced task (full rows incl. body text and resolution_payload jsonb) via .to_a with no time bound, then evaluates completion_proof_present? per task in Ruby. One correction to the finding: the per-task task_events EXISTS query is short-circuited by the && and only fires for tasks lacking payload proof keys, so the N+1 is bounded by proof-less done tasks rather than all history — but the unbounded full-row materialization of all done agent tasks is real and grows forever. The same instance also loads and TaskNotes-parses every needs_approval task body (lines 221-236). rg confirms zero caching anywhere on the path (no Rails.cache, no fragment cache in the shell partials), and Api::V1::TaskQueueHealthController#show rebuilds it per agent poll. The proposed fix (single SQL count + 30-60s Solid Cache wrap, identical JSON shape) is feasible, additive, and does not already exist. High because it taxes every page Brian opens (heavily on phone) plus 24/7 agent polling, with cost growing linearly in done-task history since the Google Tasks cutover.
verdict.ship_risk: Low blast radius, no client email involved (touches_client_email=false), no API field changes if the cached as_json keeps the exact shape (agents poll /api/v1/task_queue_health and the queue-badge runbook names checks by key — keys/labels/counts must stay identical). Two real risks: (1) translating completion_proof_present? (especially the nested completion_proof hash 'any value present excluding type/completed_at' rule) into a jsonb predicate can drift from the Ruby logic; a silent divergence to zero would mask genuine done-without-proof leaks that the badge exists to catch — ship with a spec asserting SQL count equals the Ruby oracle across proof permutations. (2) Caching keyed on Task.maximum(:updated_at) misses bare task_events inserts, so rely on a short TTL (30-60s) as the primary invalidation; up to a minute of badge staleness is acceptable by design but should be stated in the PR. Prefer shipping the cache wrap first (near-zero risk), then the SQL collapse behind the equivalence spec.

title: The tasks board never live-updates — Brian's phone approval surface goes stale between manual reloads
description: The board only mutates via Brian's own drag/approve turbo_streams. Nothing broadcasts when the other actors touch the board: Kerri files new approval cards via the API, SendApprovedDraftsJob sends a parked card (or bounces it back held), the sweep stamps applied_at and archives. rg confirms no turbo_stream_from / broadcasts anywhere in tasks views or the Task model, despite Solid Cable being wired into the stack.
failure_or_value: Brian works the queue on his phone; a tab left open shows cards that were already sent (tapping through wastes time, and the stale 'Approved... pull it back' bar invites pulling back a card that's long gone) and misses new needs_approval cards until he pull-to-refreshes. A live board is the single biggest phone-UX win available in this subsystem and directly reduces acting-on-stale-state incidents.
fix_sketch: Use Rails 8 page-refresh broadcasts to stay silo-safe: (1) in Task, after_commit broadcast_refresh_later_to [organization, assignee, 'tasks'] (per-assignee stream, so no cross-lane leak; the refresh re-runs TasksController#index under current_user's own scope); (2) in index.html.erb add turbo_stream_from @organization, current_user, 'tasks' plus <meta name='turbo-refresh-method' content='morph'> so the morph preserves scroll/drag state; (3) same stream subscription on show.html.erb so the review page's action bar flips to the sent state when the sweep fires. Debounce via broadcast_refresh_later's built-in coalescing.

verdict.reason: Re-read confirms every claim: app/views/tasks/index.html.erb and show.html.erb have no turbo_stream_from/refresh/polling and app/models/task.rb has no broadcasts, while api/v1/tasks_controller.rb and send_approved_drafts_job.rb mutate the board from outside the browser session. show.html.erb:194 literally renders "Approved and queued... Pull it back" which stays on screen after the sweep sends. The proposed fix is feasible with existing infra: cable.yml uses solid_cable in production, turbo-rails 2.0.23 supports broadcast_refresh_later_to + morph, and Turbo::StreamsChannel broadcasts are already an established pattern in this codebase (ticket searches, deals, agents index). Silo-safety holds because TasksController#index scopes via visible_to(current_user) + brand_scoped, and page-refresh broadcasts carry no content. Genuine, high-value, not-already-existing upgrade to Brian's primary phone approval surface.
verdict.ship_risk: Low-to-medium, no client-email or API-compat exposure: touches_client_email=false (view/model change only, no mailers), and the fix is purely additive (a stream tag, a meta tag, an after_commit callback) with zero /api/v1 field or schema changes. Real risks: (1) morph refreshes can clobber an in-flight SortableJS drag in kanban_controller.js — mark drag containers data-turbo-permanent or pause refresh during drag; (2) after_commit broadcasts fire on bulk agent API writes — broadcast_refresh_later coalesces, but verify no job-queue noise and suppress in test env so the green suite stays green; (3) mobile Safari drops the websocket in background tabs, so the board updates on re-foreground rather than truly live — still strictly better than never; (4) stream key must include org (and ideally assignee) to avoid cross-org refresh chatter, though even a coarse key leaks no content since the refresh re-runs the viewer-scoped controller.

title: Vendor tracker master cards go permanently stale: rollup refreshes only when a child is linked, never when a child's status changes
description: Tasks::VendorCard.refresh_master! regenerates the master card's title count and per-vendor status rollup ('• Vendor X [awaiting approval]'), but its only caller is group_under_master! (vendor_card.rb:142-144), which runs at child-filing time. When Brian later approves a vendor card, it moves to done, or it flips to waiting_reply, the master card's body still says 'awaiting approval' forever. Bonus defect in the same function: line 166 derives the event name via title.split(':').first, which truncates any event name containing a colon.
failure_or_value: The whole point of the master tracker (PR #237's per-event-per-category grouping) is a one-glance status rollup for an event's vendors. Today that rollup is only correct at the instant of filing; a week into event prep every label is wrong (approved/answered vendors still show 'awaiting approval'), so Brian either opens every child card anyway or trusts wrong data during event logistics.
fix_sketch: In Task, add an after_commit (on update) hook: if saved_change_to_status? && linkable_type == 'Task', load the parent; if parent.body.to_s.include?(Tasks::VendorCard::MANAGED_MARKER), call Tasks::VendorCard.refresh_master!(parent) (rescue/log so a rollup failure never blocks the status change; no recursion risk since masters have no linkable and refresh only touches title/body). Fix the name derivation by storing event_name in the master's source_details at creation and reading it back in refresh_master!, falling back to the current split only for pre-existing masters.

verdict.reason: Re-read confirms both defects. refresh_master! (app/services/tasks/vendor_card.rb:164) has exactly one caller, group_under_master! at vendor_card.rb:143, and that is invoked only from the two child-CREATION paths (app/tools/tasks/create_task_tool.rb:129 and app/services/ask_savant/tool_executor.rb:3772, both inside create_task). No status-change path refreshes the master: TasksController#move/#approve/#skip/#pull_back (tasks_controller.rb:135/174/202/230), the API update/events path (api/v1/tasks_controller.rb:71/88), and Task#move_to_status! never touch VendorCard, and Task has no callback on linkable. Concrete repro: file a vendor card with event_slug+category in needs_approval (master body renders '[awaiting approval]' via STATUS_LABEL, vendor_card.rb:213-214), then approve it; child moves to agent_working/done but the master body and title count never change. The bonus colon defect is also real and fires today: master_title is '<event>: <Category> vendors (n)' (line 184) and refresh_master! recovers the name via title.split(':').first (line 166), so an event name containing a colon (e.g. 'SF Tech Week: 2026') is permanently truncated the moment a second child is linked. Severity stays medium: it is wrong-but-visible data on a tracker Brian uses for event logistics, not data loss or security, and the feature (PR #237) is the entire value proposition being broken a week into use.
verdict.ship_risk: Low. touches_client_email=false — the fix is a server-side Task after_commit hook plus VendorCard changes; nothing near SponsorPortalMailer/SponsorAssetReminderService and no email path. API-compat is safe: no fields renamed or removed; only the master card's title/body VALUES change (which agents already expect to regenerate). Storing event_name in the master's source_details is additive. Residual risks to manage: (1) the hook must rescue/log around refresh_master! because master.update! runs validations (including the brand-wall property check when BrandScope enforcement flips) and a rollup failure must never abort an approve/skip; (2) no recursion since refresh only writes title/body, never status, but the guard (linkable_type == 'Task' + MANAGED_MARKER in parent body) should stay to avoid rewriting non-tracker parents; (3) refresh clobbers any manual edits to the master body — already true today on child link, so not a regression; (4) one extra parent query per task status change with a Task linkable, negligible.

title: The sweep's resolved=pending poll can hand out a card the Rails send job is actively sending (cross-sender double-send window)
description: Two independent senders exist: SendApprovedDraftsJob (Rails, every ~2 min) and the brain-side agent sweep, which polls GET /api/v1/tasks?resolved=pending (api/v1/tasks_controller.rb:24-26: resolution NOT NULL AND applied_at IS NULL). The job's in-flight claim (resolution_payload.send_started_at) is invisible to that filter — a card mid-send by the job still matches resolved=pending, because applied_at is only stamped after the send completes (Drive fetch + network can take many seconds).
failure_or_value: If the sweep polls during the job's send window and decides to execute the same approved decision (the job's own header comment says it exists so sends don't 'depend on the agent's sweep parsing and sending it' — i.e. both know how), the sponsor gets the email twice: once from the job, once from the sweep, each stamping its own completion. The fix is additive and belongs in the API since the claim is Rails-internal state the sweep cannot otherwise see.
fix_sketch: Extend the resolved=pending filter to also exclude cards with a fresh in-flight claim: .where("(resolution_payload->>'send_started_at') IS NULL OR (resolution_payload->>'send_started_at')::timestamptz < ?", SendApprovedDraftsJob::UNCONFIRMED_SEND_GRACE.ago). Purely subtractive on the result set for a poll that exists to find un-executed decisions — no field renames, no schema change; stale claims still surface so the sweep/humans can escalate. Optionally also expose send_started_at in serialize_record (additive field) so agents can reason about it.

verdict.reason: Verified on the real code: tasks_controller.rb:24-26 filters resolved=pending on resolution NOT NULL + applied_at IS NULL only, while send_approved_drafts_job.rb commits its send_started_at claim (line 157-159) before slow post-commit work (Drive fetches lines 55-62, network send lines 64-70) and stamps applied_at only after the send (stamp_sent!, lines 339-346). A card mid-send therefore matches resolved=pending for the whole window, and up to 10 minutes if stamp_sent! fails after a successful send (rescue at lines 76-82). The cross-sender overlap is documented in the repo itself: the job header (lines 3-9) says the agent sweep parses/sends approved drafts and skips only on applied_at, and api_docs_helper.rb:89 tells agents to act on list_tasks?resolved=pending outcomes with no mention of send_started_at. Confirmed as an upgrade, not a demonstrated double-send bug: the current brain-side sweep is external to this repo so its exact send scope can't be verified, and S&W cards (the sweep's documented lane) never receive a send_started_at claim (resolve_mailbox returns nil at line 119 before the stamp). One correction: serialize_record (lines 246-258) already returns the full resolution_payload, so send_started_at is already API-visible; only the server-side filter is missing.
verdict.ship_risk: Low. Server-side, one WHERE clause on a single query param, no schema change, no field rename or removal (API stays additive-compatible; the param's result set narrows to match its documented "not executed yet" semantics). S&W/Superhuman cards are unaffected since the job never stamps them. Stale claims still surface because the job's own grace hold clears resolution and bounces to needs_approval. Client-email posture: the change reduces the chance of a sponsor receiving a duplicate email and enables no new sending; touches_client_email is correctly flagged only because it sits on the send path. Two cautions: (1) reuse SendApprovedDraftsJob::UNCONFIRMED_SEND_GRACE rather than a second constant so the filter and the job's hold logic can't drift; (2) any agent using resolved=pending for monitoring (not sending) will see mid-send cards disappear for a few seconds — point such uses at task_queue_health instead. Residual: the reverse race (sweep sends first, job claims later) is not closed by this and would require the external sweep to stamp its own claim.

title: update_status accepts 'done' for a sendable needs_approval card: the decision is silently dropped and on_complete fires with nothing sent
description: TasksController#update_status validates only that the status key exists in Task.statuses (line 126), so PATCH .../update_status with status=done is accepted for any card, including a sendable needs_approval draft. That archives the card with resolution nil: the sweep's resolved=pending poll (resolution NOT NULL) never sees a decision, so the draft is neither sent nor stood down — it just vanishes. Worse, Task#run_on_complete_action (task.rb:159-164) fires on done unless resolution == 'skipped', so a payload like create_deal executes even though the email that justified the deal never went out. The board renders no done column (ACTIVE_BOARD_COLUMNS excludes it), so this isn't reachable by a normal drag, but the endpoint responds to JSON and any scripted/stale client.
failure_or_value: Concrete: a card 'Send sponsorship proposal to Acme' with on_complete create_deal gets PATCHed to done (automation glue, a replayed request, or a future done drop-target). Result: no email sent, no skip recorded for the agent, and a phantom 'Acme sponsorship' deal appears in the pipeline — directly violating the no-phantom-pipeline rule and leaving Kerri's sync in a state it can't interpret.
fix_sketch: In update_status, before move_to_status!: if new_status == 'done' && @task.resolution.nil? && TaskNotes.parse(@task.body, title: @task.title).sendable?, reject with 422 and message 'Use Approve or Skip on sendable cards' (turbo_stream + json branches already exist for the invalid-status case, reuse them). Non-sendable cards keep the current behavior. One guarded conditional, no route or param changes.

verdict.reason: Every cited mechanic verified on re-read: tasks_controller.rb:125-132 validates only Task.statuses.key? so an authenticated PATCH update_status with status=done on a needs_approval sendable card is accepted; task.rb:159-164 + task_completion_action.rb:86 then run on_complete (nil resolution only blocks on 'skipped'), creating e.g. a phantom deal; and the agent sweep's resolved=pending filter (api/v1/tasks_controller.rb:24-25) requires resolution NOT NULL, so the decision is invisible and the draft is neither sent nor stood down while open_board drops the card. The gap is real and inconsistent with the rest of the codebase: both the agent API (proof gate, PR #115) and the MCP update_task_tool (app/tools/tasks/update_task_tool.rb:45-46) block done-without-proof, making web update_status (plus the sibling TasksController#update, whose task_params at line 386 also permits :status) the only unguarded surfaces. Severity adjusted from medium to low because the endpoint sits behind Devise+Pundit+CSRF and no current client ever sends done to it (ACTIVE_BOARD_COLUMNS excludes done so no drop target exists), and TaskQueueHealth's agent_done_without_proof check would surface it after the fact — it is a latent missing guard with deterministic bad consequences but no producer today. Worth fixing as cheap defense-in-depth; the fix should cover both update_status and update.
verdict.ship_risk: Low blast radius. The fix only adds a 422 rejection on a web endpoint no current client calls with status=done, so nothing legitimate breaks; the sanctioned paths (approve/skip, API with proof, MCP tool with proof) are untouched. No client email involvement — the guard prevents unsent drafts from being silently archived, it does not enable any send (touches_client_email=false is correct). No /api/v1 field changes, no schema changes, so agent polling compat is unaffected. Two cautions: (1) guard only unresolved sendable cards as sketched, so non-sendable manual cards keep their current mark-done behavior; (2) also patch TasksController#update (task_params permits :status) or the same hole remains one endpoint over — and add a request spec for both so the green suite stays green.

title: Stage moves never emit the proposal_sent/contract_sent engagement signals DealBrief and DealHealth are built to track
description: Crm::DealBrief's flagship feature is the sent->opened artifact pair (ARTIFACTS maps 'proposal' to AccountSignal types proposal_sent/proposal_viewed) and its to_advance line 'Proposal sent N days ago, not yet opened'. But no producer in the codebase ever writes a proposal_sent signal: moving a deal to the proposal_sent stage records an Activity with action 'stage_changed', and AccountSignalRecorder#activity_signal_type maps that to signal_type 'stage_changed', which is not in ENGAGEMENT_SIGNAL_TYPES. Same for a board move to contract_sent when no Contract record exists (the contract_sent signal only comes from a Contract row's status). So engagement.proposal is always null in every deal_brief unless an agent manually POSTs an account_signal, and recent_engagement_signals? in DealHealth never credits a proposal send.
failure_or_value: Concrete value: the deal_brief payload is what Kerri/Vaughn draft advancing follow-ups from. Today its proposal tracking is dead weight -- Brian drags a deal to 'Proposal sent' on his phone and the brief still says nothing was sent. Wiring the stage move to the engagement signal makes 'proposal sent 12 days ago, not yet opened' fire from real board moves, which is exactly the nudge the pipeline worklist and agents need on the $1M push.
fix_sketch: In Crm::AccountSignalRecorder#from_activity (or activity_signal_type), when record.action == 'stage_changed' and record.metadata['to'] == 'proposal_sent', return signal_type 'proposal_sent' (strength 1); when metadata['to'] == 'contract_sent', return 'contract_sent'. The unique index on (org, source_record, signal_type) keeps it idempotent per activity row. Purely additive -- no API field or schema changes; run Crm::AccountSignalBackfill to light up historical stage moves.

verdict.reason: Re-read confirms every claim. Deal#record_stage_activity (deal.rb:288-299) emits Activity action "stage_changed" with metadata {from, to}; AccountSignalRecorder#activity_signal_type (account_signal_recorder.rb:174-182) maps it to signal_type "stage_changed", which is absent from AccountSignal::ENGAGEMENT_SIGNAL_TYPES (account_signal.rb:28-40). A full grep shows no producer of "proposal_sent" anywhere (and, stronger than claimed, no producer of "proposal_viewed" either) — the only path is a manual POST /api/v1/account_signals. So moving a deal to the proposal_sent stage on the board or via update_deal_stage_tool yields engagement.proposal => nil in DealBrief (deal_brief.rb:133-152), no "Proposal sent N days ago, not yet opened" line in to_advance (deal_brief.rb:190-211), and no recent_engagement_signals? credit in DealHealth (deal_health.rb:156-158). Same holds for a contract_sent stage move with no Contract row (from_contract requires a Contract record, recorder lines 87-106). deals_helper.rb:15,31 confirms stage_changed signals are deliberately hidden in the UI, so today a board move contributes nothing to the engagement machinery built around it. The fix (branch on record.metadata["to"] for stage_changed activities) is small, idempotent via the (org, source_record, signal_type) find_or_initialize_by, and AccountSignalBackfill already iterates Activity, so historical moves light up.
verdict.ship_risk: Low. Purely additive: signal types already exist in SIGNAL_TYPES/ENGAGEMENT_SIGNAL_TYPES, no schema change, no API field rename, no client email anywhere (touches_client_email=false). Three real but minor risks: (1) proposal_viewed has no producer at all, so every proposal-stage deal will show "Proposal sent N days ago, not yet opened" indefinitely — agents drafting from deal_brief may nudge repeatedly until an open-tracking producer exists; (2) a deal that both moves to contract_sent and has a Contract row marked sent gets two contract_sent signals (different source_records), slightly inflating engagement_signal_count and the DealHealth +5 engagement bonus; (3) re-running the backfill leaves old stage_changed signal rows alongside new proposal_sent rows for the same historical activities — harmless since stage_changed is hidden in the UI, but worth an optional cleanup. Health scores will shift upward for proposal/contract-stage deals (new +5 bonus and a "Recent buyer engagement" positive), which is the intended behavior but changes numbers agents already read.

title: Quick-add create_sponsor can regress an advanced deal back to qualified and double its package value
description: In DealsController#create_sponsor, when params[:deal_id] is present the deal is loaded with @event.deals.sponsorship.find(params[:deal_id]) -- NOT scoped to stage lead (the companion search_sponsors endpoint filters .by_stage(:lead), but the id is client-supplied). It then unconditionally runs create_sponsorship_selections! (which appends selections without clearing existing ones), recalculate_value!, and move_to_stage!(:qualified). Every other promotion path (promote_to_lead line 306, bulk_promote_to_lead line 334, mark_outreach_sent) guards with deal.lead?; this one does not.
failure_or_value: Concrete failure: Brian opens the board quick-add modal, picks a sponsor from a stale search result (or the deal was advanced by an agent/another tab between search and submit), submits -- a deal sitting in negotiation or even closed_won is silently regressed to 'qualified', stage_changed_at resets (corrupting days_in_stage and the stage-change activity trail), and re-selected sponsorship options are appended so recalculate_value! doubles the deal value. Both pipeline totals and the phantom-pipeline discipline are corrupted through a normal UI flow.
fix_sketch: Scope the lookup to leads (@event.deals.sponsorship.by_stage(:lead).find(...)) or add the same guard the other actions use: unless @deal.lead? -> redirect with 'already on the pipeline board' notice and skip selections/stage move. One conditional, mirrors promote_to_lead lines 306-309.

verdict.reason: The stage-regression half is confirmed against the real code: deals_controller.rb:402 loads the deal with no stage scope and line 424 calls move_to_stage!(:qualified) unconditionally (deal.rb:112-116 has no guard), while every sibling promotion path (promote_to_lead:306-309, bulk_promote_to_lead:334, mark_lead_qualified! deal.rb:240-245) guards on lead?. Concrete input: POST create_sponsor with the deal_id of a negotiation or closed_won sponsorship deal and no selections -> stage regresses to qualified, stage_changed_at resets (deal.rb:272-277), and for closed_won deals set_closed_at (deal.rb:279-286) additionally wipes closed_at and closed_reason, silently removing the deal from booked-revenue (won) totals — worse than the finding stated. However, the value-doubling half is REFUTED: SponsorshipSelection validates sponsorship_option_id uniqueness scoped to deal_id, so re-selecting existing options raises RecordInvalid, caught by the rescue at controller line 435, rolling back the whole transaction. Severity adjusted high->medium: doubling can't happen, and the UI trigger window is narrow (search_sponsors returns only leads, so it takes a race between search and submit, or a replayed POST) — but the closed_won data destruction keeps it above low.
verdict.ship_risk: Very low. The fix is one guard clause in a web-only controller action (mirror promote_to_lead lines 306-309: unless @deal.lead? -> redirect with 'already on the pipeline board'), or scoping the find to by_stage(:lead) — the guard is preferred since a scoped find would 404 on a stale id instead of showing a friendly notice. No client email involved (touches_client_email=false; this is board CRM plumbing, nowhere near sponsor sends). No /api/v1 surface touched — create_sponsor is an HTML/turbo_stream controller action, so agent pollers are unaffected; no schema change. Only behavior change: a non-lead deal_id now redirects with a notice instead of silently regressing, which is exactly the intent. Add a request spec for the non-lead case; existing green suite should be unaffected since no current spec can legitimately depend on regressing an advanced deal through quick-add.

title: GET /api/v1/renewals fires 2-4 extra queries per deal (fulfillment N+1) and is unpaginated
description: The API renewals index preloads :company, :primary_contact, :contracts, :case_file_entries, :account_signals -- but renewal_json calls deal.fulfillment_summary, which needs newsletter_placements (with :sponsor_commitment and :newsletter_issue, both touched by committed?/ran? per placement) and contract_deliverables. Neither is preloaded, so fulfillment_summary's fallback branch (deal.rb:195-200) fires a fresh placements query plus a contract_deliverables query per deal, and each placement's sponsor_commitment/newsletter_issue lookups compound. The response is also rendered without paginate(), unlike every other list endpoint, so the whole renewal book (which includes every ended contract forever, by design) is serialized in one request. Contrast: the web RenewalsController preloads exactly these associations (renewals_controller.rb:23-25).
failure_or_value: Agents poll this endpoint around the clock for Renewal Command. With N won deals carrying contract_end_dates and M placements each, every poll costs roughly N*(2 + M) queries instead of ~8; as the renewal book grows through the $1M push this endpoint gets linearly slower and heavier on the prod Postgres.
fix_sketch: Add :contract_deliverables and newsletter_placements: [:sponsor_commitment, :newsletter_issue] to the includes at api/v1/renewals_controller.rb:34-35 (copy the web controller's list). Optionally add opt-in pagination via the existing paginate() helper with a high default per_page so existing agent consumers see identical output (meta additions are additive).

verdict.reason: Re-read confirms both claims on the real code path. api/v1/renewals_controller.rb:34-35 omits :contract_deliverables and newsletter_placements from includes, so renewal_json's fulfillment_summary call (line 57) always hits the fallback branch at deal.rb:195-200 (newsletter_placements not loaded) firing 1-3 queries per deal for placements + their sponsor_commitment/newsletter_issue preloads, plus 1 per-deal contract_deliverables query at deal.rb:205. Concrete input: any GET /api/v1/renewals with N won deals carrying contract_end_date <= cutoff produces ~8 + N*(2-4) queries. The web RenewalsController (renewals_controller.rb:23-25) preloads exactly the missing associations, proving the fix list. The response is also rendered without the existing paginate() helper (base_controller.rb:125) and the cutoff filter keeps every ever-ended won deal in the set forever, so payload and query count grow monotonically on an endpoint agents poll around the clock. One overstatement in the description: per-placement sponsor_commitment/newsletter_issue lookups do NOT compound (the fallback branch batches them via .includes); it is 2-4 extra queries per deal, as the title says. Severity stays medium: correct behavior, small dataset today, but unbounded growth on a polled endpoint.
verdict.ship_risk: The includes fix is near-zero risk: identical JSON output, purely fewer queries; copy the web controller's list (add :contract_deliverables and newsletter_placements: [:sponsor_commitment, :newsletter_issue]; :placement_metrics not needed here). The pagination half carries real API-compat risk: agents poll this endpoint and read the full list, and the existing paginate() helper caps per_page at 100 and defaults to 25 — applying it unconditionally would silently truncate the renewal book for existing consumers and change meta shape. If pagination is added it must be strictly opt-in (only paginate when page/per_page params are present; unpaginated full response stays the default), keeping meta.within_days/meta.count intact and only adding fields. No client-email surface anywhere in this change.

title: No way to retire a dead renewal: ended contracts flag 'renewal needs action' and sit on the worklist forever
description: renewal_status returns 'ended' for any deal whose contract_end_date has passed, with no lower bound and no close-out state. Consequences: (1) DealHealth#renewal_needs_action? and HygieneScorer#renewal_needs_action? permanently penalize (14 pts) every won deal whose contract ended and won't renew -- and they don't gate on closed_won?, so an open or closed_lost deal carrying a contract_end_date also gets flagged; (2) the renewals worklist (contract_end_date <= cutoff, no floor) and /api/v1/renewals accumulate every expired contract since the beginning of time, so the screen Brian works renewals from fills with dead rows he can only clear by deleting contract_end_date, which destroys the historical record. Deal#renewal_attention? already bounds overdue at 30 days -- the health scorers and worklist disagree with it.
failure_or_value: Concrete value: keeps the renewal book workable as it grows -- today a sponsor who declined renewal in January still shows 'RENEWAL OVERDUE 150D' and drags a permanent 14-point health penalty in every agent brief and API payload, drowning the renewals that actually need action.
fix_sketch: Additive migration: renewal_closed_at (datetime) + renewal_outcome (string: renewed/churned/one_off) on deals. Add a 'Close out renewal' action on the deal page + renewals worklist row. Web worklist and the health/hygiene renewal_needs_action? checks skip deals with renewal_closed_at set (and gate on closed_won?). API keeps default output unchanged (agents poll it); add renewal_closed_at/renewal_outcome as new fields plus an ?include_closed param. No column drops or renames.

verdict.reason: Every claim survives re-reading. deal.rb:143-150 returns "ended" unbounded; deal_health.rb:142-146/109 and hygiene_scorer.rb:146-150/62 apply a permanent 14-pt penalty with no closed_won? gate and no overdue floor; the web renewals worklist (renewals_controller.rb:19-27) and GET /api/v1/renewals (api/v1/renewals_controller.rb:30-36, whose own comment says ended deals are "always included") have no lower bound so dead renewals accumulate forever; Deal#renewal_attention? (deal.rb:152-157) bounds overdue at 30 days and gates on closed_won?, so the badge and the worklist/scorers genuinely disagree. rg across app/ and db/schema.rb confirms NO close-out mechanism exists (no renewal_closed_at/renewal_outcome/churn state) — the deal.rb:171 attention message even tells the user to "close out the record", an action the product doesn't have. Only escapes are nulling contract_end_date (destroys history) or parking a fake future next_action_date (silences scorers only, not the worklist). Concrete failure: a won deal with contract_end_date = 2026-01-15 and blank next_action_date today shows in both renewals lists, carries renewal_at_risk (high, 14 pts) in hygiene and a 14-pt health penalty plus "Set a renewal follow-up date." as next_best_action in every API payload, indefinitely.
verdict.ship_risk: Low-to-medium. Zero client-email exposure (internal worklist + scorers + API only). Main compat risk is /api/v1/renewals and health/hygiene payload semantics: agents poll these around the clock, so closed-out renewals silently disappearing from default API output is a behavior change even though no field is renamed — safest is additive fields (renewal_closed_at, renewal_outcome) in the JSON plus an opt-in exclusion param for agents, while the WEB worklist and scorers filter closed-out immediately. Additive migration only, no column drops. Existing hygiene/health specs will need updating for the new closed_won? gate on renewal_needs_action?; gating it could also un-flag open/closed_lost deals that were previously (incorrectly) penalized, shifting some scores agents have already seen — acceptable but worth noting in the PR.

title: Brand-wall gaps: companies autocomplete search and deal form dropdowns are not brand-scoped
description: CompaniesController#index applies BrandScope.wall_companies (line 25), but CompaniesController#search (the JSON autocomplete) queries @organization.companies with no wall -- a brand-restricted member (Benji = HFYI-only) can enumerate every company name/website in the org by typing letters. Similarly DealsController#load_form_options loads @organization.companies, .events, and .people unwalled into the deal new/edit dropdowns, while the board itself and set_deal are carefully brand_scoped. These are exactly the side doors the brand-wall build (worktree PRs #255+, enforcement flipping in PR8) is meant to close.
failure_or_value: Concrete failure once enforcement flips: Benji opens the new-deal form or hits /organizations/:id/companies/search?q=a and sees Kinetic/S&W-adjacent companies, events, and people that the deals board correctly hides from him -- the wall leaks through autocomplete and form options.
fix_sketch: In companies#search, wrap the base scope with BrandScope.wall_companies(@organization.companies, current_user) to match index. In load_form_options, use brand_scoped(@organization.events, @organization) for events and the wall_companies/wall_people equivalents for companies and people. Both are drop-in replacements of the base relation; no schema or API change.

verdict.reason: Both cited gaps are real on main AND in the brand-wall worktree. companies_controller.rb:6-20 (#search) queries @organization.companies with only an org-membership check while #index directly below applies BrandScope.wall_companies with a 'Brand wall' comment; the route is live so any restricted member can enumerate every company via the JSON endpoint once enforcement flips (no UI caller found, but it is routed and reachable). deals_controller.rb:626-630 (load_form_options) loads unwalled companies/events/people that _form.html.erb renders into dropdowns (lines 40/46/93), while set_deal and DealPolicy::Scope in the same file are carefully walled; a brand-restricted admin (Membership allows restricted admins) reaches new/edit. Severity stays medium not high because BrandScope.restrictions_for returns {} while the brand_enforcement PlatformSetting is off (ships dark until PR8), so the leak is latent and the exposure is to an internal teammate, not the public. The fix sketch (wall_companies in search; wall_companies/brand_scoped-events/wall_people in load_form_options) is correct and drop-in.
verdict.ship_risk: Low. No client email involved (touches_client_email=false; nothing near SponsorPortalMailer/asset reminders). No /api/v1 surface touched — companies#search is an internal console JSON endpoint and the deal form is HTML; no field renames, no schema change. While the enforcement flag is off and for unrestricted users the wall helpers reduce to the original relation, so behavior today is provably unchanged (existing green suite should stay green). The one behavioral edge after enforcement flips: a restricted admin's deal form will hide companies/people not yet tagged with their brand — fail-closed by design per BrandScope's documented backfill rule, but worth a spec so an untagged-company gap surfaces as a test failure rather than a confused Benji. Fix should also land in the brand-wall worktree branch (same code there) to avoid the stacked PRs re-introducing it.

title: Pipeline board renders every deal ever created -- closed columns are unbounded
description: DealsController#index loads the full deals relation (no limit) and renders a kanban card for every closed_won and closed_lost deal since inception inside the collapsed closed column (_closed_column.html.erb iterates won_deals/lost_deals fully). Open columns are naturally bounded by pipeline discipline, but the closed set grows monotonically -- with ~$668K booked midyear and cold-outreach leads churning to closed_lost, this page (Brian's main phone surface) ships an ever-growing DOM and query payload on every visit and every turbo_stream refresh.
failure_or_value: Concrete value: board load time and phone scroll performance stay flat as the CRM grows instead of degrading a little every week. Today a year of closed deals means hundreds of hidden cards parsed, rendered, and shipped to a phone on each board visit.
fix_sketch: In #index, query open deals in full but restrict closed cards to a window (e.g. closed_at >= 90.days.ago) with a ?closed=all escape hatch link in the closed column header. Compute the header counts and won_total via SQL aggregates over the unrestricted scope (they're currently summed from the loaded arrays at _closed_column.html.erb:5 and index.html.erb:6, so keep those numbers full-history). Keep Revenue::PipelineSnapshot fed by the open scope it already effectively measures, or pass it the unrestricted relation explicitly. Web-only change; the API is untouched.

verdict.reason: Re-read confirms the claim on the real code path. DealsController#index (app/controllers/deals_controller.rb:28-30) loads the full brand-scoped deals relation with no limit and no pagination (verified: no limit/page/Pagy anywhere in the index path), then buckets every deal into @deals_by_stage including closed_won/closed_lost (line 43-44). _closed_column.html.erb:24-26 and 40-42 render a full ~70-line kanban_card partial for every closed deal ever created; the <details> disclosure only hides them visually, the DOM is still built and shipped on every board load and every filter submit (the filter form targets the "kanban-board" turbo_frame, index.html.erb:18, which re-renders the whole board). closed_at exists on Deal (set_closed_at, app/models/deal.rb:279-283), so the proposed 90-day window is directly implementable. The full-history numbers the fix must preserve are exactly where the finding says: won_total summed from the loaded array (_closed_column.html.erb:5), header counts from the arrays (index.html.erb:6), and Revenue::PipelineSnapshot#call consuming @deals.to_a for won_count/won_value. One nit: the finding's "every turbo_stream refresh" is slightly off (update_stage.turbo_stream.erb replaces only the moved card, and no index.turbo_stream.erb template exists), but the HTML/turbo_frame path carries the full cost, so the substance survives. This upgrade does not already exist, is web-only, and directly targets Brian's primary phone surface whose payload grows monotonically with closed_lost churn from cold outreach.
verdict.ship_risk: Low. touches_client_email=false: no mailer or sponsor-facing send is anywhere near this path. API compat is untouched: the web DealsController is separate from Api::V1::DealsController, and no /api/v1 field or DB column changes are needed (closed_at already exists; change is query-and-view only). Real risks to manage in the fix: (1) header counts, won_total, and PipelineSnapshot won_count/won_value must be computed from the unrestricted scope (SQL aggregates) or booked-revenue numbers on the board silently shrink to the window, which would be a data-integrity regression on the number Brian trusts most; (2) dragging an old closed deal back to open requires the ?closed=all escape hatch to still render its card in a drop container; (3) board request/system specs asserting closed-card presence or counts may need updating. All contained to the deals index views/controller, small blast radius.

title: Three uncoordinated company-matching paths create duplicate companies (case-sensitive name match, raw website string match, or no match at all)
description: Company dedup differs per entry point: (1) create_sponsor (board quick-add) unconditionally creates a new Company when a name is typed -- zero duplicate check; (2) import_csv matches find_by(name: name) which is case-sensitive and whitespace-exact ('Duro Labs' vs 'duro labs' duplicates); (3) find_or_create_company (deal create) matches only the exact website string, so 'https://duro.com', 'www.duro.com' and 'duro.com' are three different companies. None of them consult the normalized `domain` column that agents' Company.by_domain matching and the inbox sweep rely on.
failure_or_value: Concrete value: duplicate companies fragment CRM history -- deals, people, account signals, and sponsor commitments split across twins, and the agents' inbound-email-to-account matching (by_domain) picks whichever twin holds the domain. As the cold queue and CSV imports scale (MapYourShow exhibitor feed incoming), duplicates compound weekly. One shared matcher makes 'CRM of record' true.
fix_sketch: Add a Companies::Matcher service: derive a normalized domain from any website/email input (strip scheme/www, downcase), then match in order domain -> aliases -> case-insensitive trimmed name (LOWER(TRIM(name)) = ?); create only on miss, stamping the derived domain. Use it in create_sponsor, import_csv, and find_or_create_company. Additive behavior change at write time only; existing rows untouched (optionally a one-off rake to backfill domain from website).

verdict.reason: All three cited paths verified in deals_controller.rb: create_sponsor (403-407) creates a company unconditionally with no lookup; import_csv (491) uses case-sensitive exact find_by(name:); find_or_create_company (632-639) matches only the raw website string and creates blind when website is blank. Company (company.rb:39-46) has a normalized org-unique `domain` column plus a by_domain scope used by the API filter and GroundTruthGuard, but none of the write paths set or consult it, so the uniqueness validation never protects anything. No Companies::Matcher or equivalent exists; the problem is wider than cited — task_completion_action.rb:149 and ask_savant/tool_executor.rb:2934/3038/3220 and app/tools/companies/create_company_tool.rb:28 each use different (or no) matching rules, giving at least six creation paths with four inconsistent dedup behaviors. Concrete duplicate-producing inputs: CSV name 'duro labs' vs existing 'Duro Labs'; deal form website 'https://duro.com' vs existing 'duro.com'; any typed name in board quick-add.
verdict.ship_risk: Low-to-medium. Write-time-only change, additive, no API field renames or removals, and touches_client_email=false (no sponsor-facing sends anywhere near these paths). Real risks: (1) over-merge — case-insensitive name matching could wrongly unify two legitimately distinct companies sharing a name, silently attaching a deal to the wrong account; keep name-match as the last-resort tier and log matches. (2) Domain derivation from email input must blocklist freemail domains (gmail.com etc.) or one personal-email import glues unrelated companies together. (3) Stamping derived domain can collide with the org-scoped domain uniqueness validation when an existing twin already holds it — the matcher must match by domain before creating, and the backfill rake must handle conflicts (skip + report, never raise mid-batch). (4) Agents poll /api/v1 constantly: matcher must stay behind existing endpoints unchanged; if create endpoints start returning an existing company instead of a fresh one, callers that assume a new id still work (id is returned either way) but any agent logic that treats create as always-new should be checked. Existing rows untouched, so rollback is trivial.

title: Web update_stage error branch is dead code: move_to_stage! raises, so a validation failure 500s the kanban drag instead of showing the error
description: Deal#move_to_stage! ends with save!, which returns true or raises ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid -- it never returns false. DealsController#update_stage wraps it in `if @deal.move_to_stage!(...)` with an else branch that renders 'Could not update stage' with the deal's errors; that branch is unreachable. ApplicationController has no rescue_from RecordInvalid, so if the deal fails validation on save (e.g. a legacy row whose company/event drifted to another organization tripping associations_belong_to_organization, or an investor deal that acquired an event), a board drag or the inline stage selector returns a raw 500 and the card snaps back with no explanation. The API controller is fine (BaseController rescues RecordInvalid to 422).
failure_or_value: Concrete failure: dragging a card whose record is invalid for any pre-existing reason crashes with a 500 on Brian's phone instead of the friendly per-format error responses already written at lines 216-222; the carefully-built else branch never executes for anyone.
fix_sketch: Wrap the move in begin/rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid and route the rescue to the existing else-branch responses (the error messages are already on @deal.errors). Alternatively give Deal a non-bang move_to_stage returning save's boolean and call that here. Two-line change, no behavior change on the success path.

verdict.reason: Re-read confirms every load-bearing claim: Deal#move_to_stage! (deal.rb:112-116) ends in save!, which returns true or raises RecordInvalid and never returns false, so the else branch at deals_controller.rb:216-222 is dead code; ApplicationController (line 8) rescues only Pundit::NotAuthorizedError, so an invalid deal on a kanban drag or inline stage change 500s instead of rendering the already-written error responses. The API path is correctly excluded (api/v1/base_controller.rb:14 rescues RecordInvalid to 422). Concrete trigger: PATCH update_stage on any deal row failing associations_belong_to_organization (deal.rb:307-315) or event_only_for_sponsorship (deal.rb:301-305), e.g. a company reassigned to another organization. Caveat keeping it low: no in-app write path skips validations (no update_column/insert_all on deals found), so an invalid row requires data drift via console/migration/legacy data rather than a normal user flow; the dead branch itself is unconditional, the user-visible 500 is latent.
verdict.ship_risk: Very low. The fix (rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid in DealsController#update_stage and route to the existing else-branch responses) changes nothing on the success path, touches no /api/v1 fields or schema, and involves zero client email (touches_client_email=false). Two cautions: keep move_to_stage! bang semantics unchanged so the API controller's 422 rescue and app/tools/deals/update_deal_stage_tool.rb keep their current behavior; and note the rescue converts what would have been a loud 500 in error tracking into a quiet flash/422, so consider logging the caught RecordInvalid for observability.

title: Console and API sponsor-asset file uploads land on ephemeral Render disk and silently vanish on the next deploy
description: Production Active Storage is the :local Disk service (config/environments/production.rb:25) and the codebase itself documents that Render disks are ephemeral (SponsorAsset comment lines 4-8, SponsorPortalController lines 27-29). The sponsor-portal upload path was fixed to store bytes in Postgres via attach_stored_file, but the two internal upload paths were not: SponsorAssetsController#create (console form at sponsor_commitments/show.html.erb:159) and Api::V1::SponsorAssetsController#create (Kerri filing emailed creative) both permit :file and let it flow to has_one_attached :file, i.e. a blob file written to local disk.
failure_or_value: Kerri POSTs a sponsor logo to /api/v1/sponsor_commitments/:id/sponsor_assets (or Benji uploads via the console form). asset_content_present passes because file.attached?, the asset counts in submitted_asset_types, the chase card auto-closes as 'assets complete'. The next Render deploy wipes the disk: the asset row survives, the blob bytes are gone. On newsletter build day the download link 404s/streams nothing and the creative that closed the chase no longer exists — silent data loss with the reminder system reporting green.
fix_sketch: Extract the portal controller's upload handling (read bytes, enforce SponsorAsset::MAX_STORED_FILE_BYTES, call asset.attach_stored_file(name:, content_type:, bytes:)) into a shared helper (e.g. SponsorAsset.apply_upload(asset, upload) or a controller concern) and use it in SponsorAssetsController#create and Api::V1::SponsorAssetsController#create instead of permitting :file into mass assignment. Keep the :file param name so existing agent calls keep working (API response field file_attached can additively be complemented with stored_file). Return 422/alert with the over-limit message like the portal does. Add specs asserting file_data is populated and file.attached? is false for both paths. Optionally add a one-off backfill task that copies any existing disk-attached blobs (if still present) into file_data.

verdict.reason: Re-read every cited file. production.rb:25 uses the :local Disk service (storage.yml root Rails.root/storage) and render.yaml has NO persistent disk block on the kerrihq-rails web service, so the filesystem is genuinely ephemeral — the codebase says so itself in sponsor_asset.rb:4-8 and sponsor_portal_controller.rb:27-29. Both SponsorAssetsController#create (console form file_field at sponsor_commitments/show.html.erb:159, :file permitted at line 66) and Api::V1::SponsorAssetsController#create (:file permitted at line 50) mass-assign :file into has_one_attached, writing blob bytes to local disk. SponsorAsset has no callback that moves an attached blob into file_data; attach_stored_file is only called by the portal controller and the Ask Savant tool executor, confirming these two paths were simply missed in the portal fix. asset_content_present passes on file.attached? alone, the commitment counts the asset as submitted, and SponsorAssetReminderJob auto-closes the chase — then the next deploy deletes the bytes while the row survives, so download (rails_blob_path) and CompanyResource file_url dead-link. Concrete failing input: multipart POST /api/v1/sponsor_commitments/:id/sponsor_assets with sponsor_asset[file] (Kerri's documented email-filing flow), followed by any deploy. Aggravator: web and queue are separate Render services, so a web-written blob is invisible to the worker even pre-deploy. Critical because it is silent loss of sponsor creative in the core revenue workflow while the reminder system reports green, on a repo that deploys near-daily.
verdict.ship_risk: Low. The fix reuses the already-proven portal pattern (attach_stored_file into Postgres) on two internal write paths, keeps the :file param name so existing agent calls and the console form keep working unchanged, and touches no mailer — zero client-email exposure (SponsorAssetNotificationJob is an internal reviewer ping and is untouched). One API-compat trap to handle: the /api/v1 response field file_attached is computed as asset.file.attached? and would flip to false for new uploads after the fix; it must be redefined as (stored_file? || file.attached?) so polling agents keep seeing true, with a new additive stored_file field. Also CompanyResource#file_url only builds URLs for disk-attached blobs, so stored-file assets need the existing sponsor_assets download route added additively there. Size limit adds a new 422 path on the API for >15MB files where uploads previously succeeded (then silently died) — acceptable and should be documented in the agent-facing error message. Existing already-orphaned rows can't be recovered (bytes are gone); the optional backfill only helps blobs uploaded since the last deploy.

title: Newsletter inventory horizon is hardcoded to 2026 — 2027 slots can't be seen or sold from sell-through or the agent slots API
description: Three surfaces pin the inventory horizon at 2026-12-31: NewsletterSellThrough defaults year: 2026 and NewsletterInventoryController#sell_through passes no year (no UI to change it), NewsletterSlotSeeder defaults through: Date.new(2026,12,31), and the agent-facing /api/v1/newsletter_slots defaults both the index `to` and seed `through` to 2026-12-31.
failure_or_value: KMG's stated goal is $150K of 2027 revenue booked before EOY 2026, and 2027 goal-setting starts 2026-09-01 — selling 2027 slots is imminent. Today an agent asking the slots API for open inventory gets zero 2027 slots (none seeded, default window ends 2026-12-31), Brian's sell-through page can never show 2027, and on 2027-01-01 the page silently keeps rendering 2026 data. Fixing this now makes 2027 inventory sellable through the same agent + console surfaces with no schema change.
fix_sketch: NewsletterSellThrough: default year: Date.current.year. Controller: @sell_through = NewsletterSellThrough.new(organization: @organization, year: params[:year]&.to_i&.clamp(2024, 2100) || Date.current.year); add prev/next-year links in the sell_through view. NewsletterSlotSeeder: default through: (Date.current + 12.months).end_of_month. Slots API: default `to` and `through` to the same rolling 12-month horizon (explicit ?from/?to/?through params keep working, so this is additive for agents). Seed the 2027 Tue/Sat issues once via the existing seed endpoint after deploy.

verdict.reason: All five citations verified verbatim: NewsletterSellThrough defaults year: 2026 (app/services/newsletter_sell_through.rb:25); NewsletterInventoryController#sell_through passes no year and ignores params (lines 42-44), and a grep of sell_through.html.erb + routes confirms there is no year switcher anywhere, so the console page is hard-locked to 2026; NewsletterSlotSeeder defaults through: 2026-12-31 (line 14); the agent API defaults both index `to` and seed `through` to 2026-12-31 (api/v1/newsletter_slots_controller.rb:23,41). Minor overstatement: agents CAN pass explicit ?to/?through to reach 2027, so the API is not fully blind — but the default path is what agents use, and it degrades to a concrete failure: on 2027-01-01 a bare GET computes from=Date.current > to=2026-12-31, an inverted range returning zero slots, and default seeding becomes a permanent no-op (seeder clamps from to Date.current). With the stated business goal of $150K of 2027 revenue booked before EOY 2026 and 2027 planning starting 2026-09-01, selling 2027 inventory through these exact surfaces is imminent, making this a high-value, low-cost, schema-free upgrade that does not already exist.
verdict.ship_risk: Low. No client email surface is touched (touches_client_email=false; slots/sell-through are internal read surfaces and the seeder creates issue records only). API compat: changing the default `to`/`through` from a fixed 2026-12-31 to a rolling ~12-month horizon is additive in shape (no fields renamed/removed; explicit ?from/?to/?through keep working) but does change default-call response contents — an agent that sums the default window assuming it equals calendar-2026 could over/under count until re-prompted; mitigate by keeping meta.from/meta.to in the response (already present) so callers can see the window. Seeding 2027 adds ~104 idempotent newsletter_issue rows (unique index makes re-runs no-ops). The sell-through ?year param must be validated/clamped (as sketched) to avoid Date.new errors from junk input. Sell-through denominators for a new empty year are pure calendar arithmetic, so an unseeded 2027 view renders correctly as all-open-future rather than erroring.

title: Make the client-email ban executable: SponsorPortalMailer enforces internal-only recipients in code, not comments
description: The 2026-07-02 hard rule (no sponsor-facing asset mail) is enforced only by comments and the contact_email validation. SponsorPortalMailer's recipients are runtime arguments (asset_uploaded_notification mails whatever reviewer_for returns; reviewer_for falls back to organization.admins.first || owners.first), so a future code path, console change, or bad reviewer_for fallback could hand it an external address and the mail would go out. config/recurring.yml:91 still describes the reminder job as 'emails the client their portal link', which invites someone to re-add the send.
failure_or_value: Value: converts Brian's hard rule from prose into a tripwire. Any future regression that would email a sponsor (a re-added chase, a mis-resolved reviewer, an agent-driven mailer call) raises before delivery instead of leaking a client email. This explicitly keeps client email OFF — it adds no send path.
fix_sketch: In SponsorPortalMailer add an after_action (or override mail()) that collects to+cc+bcc and raises SponsorPortalMailer::ExternalRecipientError unless every address is on an internal allowlist (e.g. ENV-configurable INTERNAL_MAIL_DOMAINS defaulting to hardwarefyi.com + kerrihq.com, or membership emails of the commitment's organization). Tighten SponsorInventoryNotificationService.reviewer_for to only return active full-member staff. Fix the stale recurring.yml:91 comment to say the reminder is internal-only. Add a spec that asserts the mailer raises for a sponsor address — a permanent regression test for the ban.

verdict.reason: Re-read confirms every cited fact: SponsorPortalMailer (app/mailers/sponsor_portal_mailer.rb:3-8,20,37) enforces the 2026-07-02 client-email ban only in comments while taking recipients as runtime arguments; reviewer_for (app/services/sponsor_inventory_notification_service.rb:52-57) falls back to organization.admins.first || owners.first; no recipient guard exists anywhere in app/mailers or initializers; and config/recurring.yml:90-91 still says the reminder job "emails the client their portal link", contradicting the internal-only SponsorAssetReminderService and inviting re-addition of the banned send. The upgrade is real, does not already exist, and is feasible with a small after_action guard + spec. Severity adjusted from high to medium because no concrete input today produces a client email — all reachable recipients are org-member User records and internal_asset_reminder hardcodes benji@/brian@hardwarefyi.com — so this is a regression tripwire and doc fix, not a live hole.
verdict.ship_risk: Low and purely restrictive: touches_client_email=true only in the sense that it further blocks client email — it adds no send path and keeps client mail OFF by default, consistent with the hard rule. No /api/v1 fields or DB columns change. The one real risk is an over-narrow allowlist: if it only checks hardwarefyi.com/kerrihq.com domains and SPONSOR_ASSET_REVIEWER_EMAIL or a future staff member uses another domain, legitimate internal notifications would raise and fail in Solid Queue, silently dropping Benji's asset alerts. Mitigate by allowlisting the commitment's organization membership emails in addition to the domain list, making domains ENV-configurable, and adding both a raises-for-sponsor-address spec and a passes-for-org-member spec. The recurring.yml comment fix is zero-risk (comment only).

title: Newsletter import: the shared `status` row key crashes placement upserts and rolls back the whole import
description: upsert_commitment reads attrs[:status] as a SponsorCommitment status (active/fulfilled/cancelled/makegood) at line 63, and upsert_placement reuses the same attrs[:status] as a NewsletterPlacement status fallback at line 126 (reserved/needs_assets/.../cancelled). The two enums share almost no values, and enum assignment with an unknown value raises ArgumentError. The whole import runs in one transaction (line 18).
failure_or_value: An import row like { sponsor_name: "Quilter", status: "active", issue_date: "2026-07-14" } — a perfectly natural way for an agent to express commitment status — raises ArgumentError ("'active' is not a valid status") in upsert_placement and rolls back every row in the batch. Conversely a row with status: "cancelled" meant for the commitment silently cancels the placement too.
fix_sketch: In upsert_placement drop the attrs[:status] fallback: status: attrs[:placement_status].presence || "reserved". If back-compat with existing agent payloads matters, keep the fallback but only when the value is a valid NewsletterPlacement status (NewsletterPlacement.statuses.key?(value)), else default to reserved. Also wrap per-row enum assignment so a bad row reports which row failed instead of a bare ArgumentError. Add specs for a row carrying commitment-style status plus issue_date.

verdict.reason: Re-read confirms every element on the real code path. newsletter_inventory_import_service.rb:63 treats attrs[:status] as a SponsorCommitment status alias (active/fulfilled/cancelled/makegood) while line 126 reuses the same attrs[:status] as the NewsletterPlacement status fallback (reserved/needs_assets/.../cancelled); the two enums share only "cancelled". NewsletterPlacement's enum has no validate: true, so assignment of an unknown value raises ArgumentError. The input is reachable: :status is a permitted row key in Api::V1::NewsletterInventoryImportsController#permitted_row_keys (line 48) alongside :issue_date, and rows pass through unfiltered (also via lib/tasks/newsletter.rake). Concrete failing input: {sponsor_name: "Quilter", status: "active", issue_date: "2026-07-14"} — commitment saves, then upsert_placement raises ArgumentError ("'active' is not a valid status"), the single transaction at line 18 rolls back the entire batch, and the controller rescues only ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid so the caller gets a 500 with no row diagnostics. The secondary claim also holds: status: "cancelled" meant for the commitment silently cancels the placement (removing it from active_inventory). Severity stays medium, not high, because the endpoint is behind the trusted brain:import scope, the rollback is atomic (no partial corruption), and explicit placement_status payloads are unaffected — but it is a real reliability trap for agent-driven imports and the service spec has zero coverage of the status fallback.
verdict.ship_risk: Low. The guarded fix (honor attrs[:status] in upsert_placement only when NewsletterPlacement.statuses.key?(value), else default "reserved") is purely server-side interpretation of an input field: no API field renamed or removed, no DB schema change, and existing agent payloads that send valid placement statuses or explicit placement_status keep working, including status:"cancelled" cancelling both records if anyone relies on that. Rescuing ArgumentError in the controller as a 422 with the offending row index is additive. Only residual risk: any caller that (buggily) depended on the whole-batch 500 for a commitment-style status now gets a partial-success import with placement defaulted to reserved — that is the desired behavior, but worth a spec asserting it. No client-email surface is touched: this is the internal brain:import path, and contact_email is deliberately never imported (service line 61), so the client-email ban is unaffected.

title: Import money parsing is type-dependent: integer contract_value/price are read as cents, strings as dollars
description: cents() returns Integer input unchanged (line 183) but parses String input as dollars and multiplies by 100 (line 185). Both call sites feed it ambiguous keys: cents(attrs[:contract_value_cents] || attrs[:contract_value]) at line 64 and cents(attrs[:price]) at line 139. So the stored amount depends on the JSON type the agent happened to send, and a String passed under the _cents key gets multiplied by 100.
failure_or_value: Agent posts { contract_value: 5000 } (dollars) → stored as 5000 cents = $50.00; { contract_value: "5000" } → $5,000.00. Or { contract_value_cents: "500000" } (string cents) → 50,000,000 cents = $500,000 instead of $5,000. Revenue-of-record numbers on the CRM sell-through and owed ledgers become 100x wrong in either direction depending on serialization, with no error raised.
fix_sketch: Split the semantics: if attrs[:contract_value_cents].present?, use Integer(attrs[:contract_value_cents]) (accepting numeric strings); otherwise parse attrs[:contract_value] as dollars via a dollars_to_cents() that removes the `return value if value.is_a?(Integer)` short-circuit and always does BigDecimal * 100. Same for price: always dollars→cents. Field names keep their existing meaning (_cents = cents, others = dollars) so the change is additive/clarifying; add unit specs for integer, string, "$1,234.50" inputs on both keys.

verdict.reason: Re-read confirms every element. cents() at app/services/newsletter_inventory_import_service.rb:181-186 returns Integer input unchanged but parses String/Float as dollars and multiplies by 100; both call sites (line 64 for contract_value_cents||contract_value, line 139 for price) feed it type-ambiguous values. The API controller (api/v1/newsletter_inventory_imports_controller.rb:17) uses params.expect on a JSON body, which preserves JSON number vs string types, so {contract_value: 5000} stores $50 while {contract_value: "5000"} stores $5,000, and {contract_value_cents: "500000"} stores $500,000 — concrete, reachable inputs, not hypothetical. The rake path (lib/tasks/newsletter.rake:12, JSON.parse) has the same exposure. Decisive corroboration: the interactive NewsletterPlacementsController#cents (lines 106-110) has no Integer short-circuit and always treats contract_value as dollars, so the import service diverges from the UI for the same field whenever an Integer arrives. Result flows into contract_value_cents/price_cents, which drive paid-placement scopes (newsletter_placement.rb:54,98), issue revenue (newsletter_issue.rb:65), and the company API resource, with only a >=0 validation — 100x money errors land silently in the CRM of record. Severity stays medium: real silent money corruption, but the endpoint is gated behind the trusted brain:import scope with few known callers.
verdict.ship_risk: Low blast radius, no client email involved (touches_client_email=false; the import deliberately skips contact_email per the 2026-07-02 hard rule) and no API field renames — the fix only clarifies parsing semantics, which is additive-compatible. Two real risks to manage: (1) if any existing pusher (e.g., the ROWS_FILE producer for hwfyi_advertising_tracker) currently sends integer CENTS under the plain contract_value/price keys and depends on the pass-through, the fix would 100x its values — audit the producer script and a sample of stored contract_value_cents before deploy; since the importer is an idempotent upsert keyed on source_row_id, a corrected re-push repairs any bad stored data either way. (2) the sketched Integer(attrs[:contract_value_cents]) raises on decimal strings like "5000.50" — prefer BigDecimal(...).round.to_i or return a clear 422 rather than a 500. Add unit specs for Integer, String, and "$1,234.50" inputs on both keys, plus a request spec sending JSON numbers, and run the full suite (main is green) before shipping.

title: Sponsor portal contradicts itself: checklist says assets received while the Submitted assets panel says none submitted
description: The portal's per-type '✓ Received' badges and the 'Assets complete' banner use SponsorCommitment#submitted_asset_types, which (post-Quilter fix) counts assets held anywhere — including ones Kerri filed on the sponsor's company page. But the 'Submitted assets' panel renders @assets = @commitment.sponsor_assets (controller line 14), commitment-anchored rows only. The two views of the same question disagree on the page a sponsor actually looks at.
failure_or_value: A sponsor whose logo/copy were filed from email onto their company page (the normal agent path) opens their portal: the top says 'Assets complete' with four green checks, while the Submitted assets panel says 'No assets submitted yet.' That reads as a broken or untrustworthy portal — exactly the confusion the 2026-07-03 Quilter fix was meant to end. This is the asset hub Brian wants improved; it is a web page the sponsor already has the link to, no email involved.
fix_sketch: In SponsorPortalController#show set @assets to the union the checklist uses: @commitment.held_assets (submitted_or_approved, commitment OR matched-company anchored) merged with the commitment's own non-archived rows so pending/rejected uploads still show, ordered by created_at desc — e.g. SponsorAsset.where(id: @commitment.held_assets.select(:id)).or(SponsorAsset.where(sponsor_commitment_id: @commitment.id)).where.not(status: :archived).ordered. Keep the same partial; add a request spec covering a company-page-held asset appearing in the portal list.

verdict.reason: All cited lines check out on re-read. The checklist/banner path (show.html.erb:11,29,40-42,65-67,80-82) uses SponsorCommitment#submitted_asset_types -> held_assets (sponsor_commitment.rb:70-83), which counts commitment-anchored OR company-anchored submitted/approved assets. The Submitted assets panel uses @assets = @commitment.sponsor_assets (sponsor_portal_controller.rb:14), commitment-anchored only. The divergent population is real: AskSavant::ToolExecutor#save_company_asset (tool_executor.rb:3114-3125) creates SponsorAsset rows with company set and sponsor_commitment_id nil (status approved by default) — inside held_assets, outside @assets. Concrete repro: commitment with placements linked to company X; agent files all four asset types via save_company_asset with company_id=X; portal shows 'Assets complete' + four '✓ Received' while the panel renders 'No assets submitted yet' (show.html.erb:150-151). The fix sketch (union held_assets with the commitment's own non-archived rows) is feasible and small.
verdict.ship_risk: No client email is involved — the portal is an existing web page the sponsor already has a token link to, and the fix must not touch SponsorPortalMailer/SponsorAssetReminderService (both stay internal-only). No /api/v1 fields or DB columns change. The real ship risk is data exposure on a sponsor-facing page: widening @assets to held_assets surfaces agent-filed company assets to the sponsor, including type 'document' rows and rows matched via the exact sponsor-name company fallback (a mis-anchored or same-named company could leak another entity's creative). The current partial renders asset_type/status/filename/url/copy but not notes, limiting exposure; still, the implementer should consider restricting the union to required_asset_types plus portal-sourced rows, and should cover the union query (OR across sponsor_commitment_id/company_id plus the pending/rejected commitment rows) with a request spec, since a naive .or() on differently-structured relations raises ArgumentError in Rails.

title: Console/API asset creation accepts a newsletter_placement_id from any commitment in the org
description: The portal path validates that newsletter_placement_id belongs to the commitment (@commitment.newsletter_placements.find). The console and API create paths permit the raw id with no such scoping; SponsorAsset#records_share_organization only checks the organization, so a placement belonging to a different sponsor's commitment in the same org is accepted.
failure_or_value: Kerri (or a console user) files an asset with a stale/wrong placement id: the asset saves anchored to commitment A but placement belonging to commitment B. The asset then shows on sponsor B's placement in issue views and portal placement groupings while counting toward sponsor A's chase — cross-sponsor creative mix-up that nobody is validating.
fix_sketch: In both controllers, mirror the portal: if params include newsletter_placement_id, resolve it via @commitment.newsletter_placements.find_by(id: ...) and 422/alert when absent. Better: move it into the model — validate that newsletter_placement.sponsor_commitment_id matches sponsor_commitment_id when both are present (allow nil commitment for company-anchored assets). Additive validation; add specs for the mismatch case.

verdict.reason: Verified on the real code: api/v1/sponsor_assets_controller.rb:47-56 and sponsor_assets_controller.rb:62-72 both permit raw newsletter_placement_id with no commitment scoping, while sponsor_portal_controller.rb:69-72 validates via @commitment.newsletter_placements.find. SponsorAsset#records_share_organization (sponsor_asset.rb:97-103) only compares organization_id, and NewsletterPlacement has a required belongs_to :sponsor_commitment, so POST /api/v1/sponsor_commitments/A/sponsor_assets with a placement id from commitment B in the same org saves successfully and serializes the wrong placement back to agents — a concrete, reproducible cross-commitment data-integrity hole on the exact path Kerri uses (the API doc comment even shows newsletter_placement_id in its example). One caveat: the claimed visible impact is overstated — no current view renders placement.sponsor_assets (asset_status and assets_complete? derive from sponsor_commitment_id/company_id, not the placement FK), and the console form never exposes the field, so today it is latent DB/API corruption rather than a visible sponsor-B mix-up. The has_many plus the sponsor_assets eager-load on placements in sponsor_portal_controller.rb:12 mean it will surface silently when placement-grouped display lands. Severity low as filed.
verdict.ship_risk: Low blast radius. No client email involved (touches_client_email=false); the portal send path is untouched and the fix must not add any sponsor-facing mail. API compat: purely additive — no fields renamed/removed; the only behavior change is a 422 (or scoped-lookup 404) where an invalid cross-commitment placement id previously succeeded, which agents should never legitimately send; keep the error message explicit so Kerri can self-correct. Main ship risk is the model-level validation firing on UPDATE of any pre-existing mismatched rows (e.g. status flips from the console review buttons would start failing) — before deploying, run a one-off check for existing rows where newsletter_placement.sponsor_commitment_id != sponsor_assets.sponsor_commitment_id and repair or null the placement FK, or scope the validation to changes to the two ids. Controller-level scoping alone (mirroring the portal) carries essentially zero regression risk.

title: Manual 'send asset reminder' tells Brian a reminder went out when the service no-opped
description: SponsorAssetReminderService#call returns early (no task, no mail) when commitment.assets_complete?, but SponsorCommitmentsController#send_asset_reminder unconditionally flashes 'Internal reminder sent to Benji + Brian. Nothing goes to the client.' The controller has no way to know nothing happened.
failure_or_value: Brian taps the reminder button on a commitment whose assets are already complete (e.g. company-page assets satisfied the checklist): the console confirms a send that never occurred. For a non-technical operator who judges the system by its own reporting, that's a false 'done' — the exact class of trust failure the queue-health work exists to prevent.
fix_sketch: Have #call return a symbol (:sent vs :assets_complete) or a small Result. In the controller branch the flash: assets complete → notice: 'Assets are already complete for <sponsor> — no reminder needed.'; sent → the current message. One-line service change, two-line controller change, spec each branch.

verdict.reason: Verified on the real code path: SponsorAssetReminderService#call (app/services/sponsor_asset_reminder_service.rb:16) returns early with the same value (`commitment`) whether it sent or skipped, so SponsorCommitmentsController#send_asset_reminder (app/controllers/sponsor_commitments_controller.rb:44-47) has no signal and always flashes "Internal reminder sent to Benji + Brian." The trigger is reachable: the "Remind Benji + Brian" button in app/views/sponsor_commitments/show.html.erb:16 renders with no assets_complete? guard, directly under a badge that can read "assets complete" (line 11). Concrete input: any commitment whose missing_asset_types is empty (e.g., company-matched assets via held_assets, or empty required_asset_types) — tap the button, nothing is filed or mailed, benji_reminded_at is not set, yet the console reports a send. For a non-technical operator who trusts the system's own reporting, that is a real false-done, though internal-only and low impact, so severity stays low.
verdict.ship_risk: Very low. The fix is a return-value discriminator in the service plus a flash branch in the controller — no API /api/v1 surface, no schema change, no field renames.
