Critically it must NOT re-add any sponsor-facing send: the service header comments document the hard internal-only rule, and the sketched fix keeps SponsorPortalMailer usage untouched (internal_asset_reminder only), so touches_client_email stays false. Only care point: keep the service's return value backward-compatible for any other caller (rg shows the controller is the only caller today; a scheduled job comment references daily runs, so if a job invokes it, returning a Result object instead of the commitment should be checked against that call site) and spec both branches.

title: Unified outbound-mail ledger: no single record of what actually left the mailboxes
description: Outbound mail leaves through at least four paths (Ask Savant send_mail/reply_mail tools, SendApprovedDraftsJob, ActionMailer via MailboxMailDelivery, agent flows), but each records its send differently or not at all: the drafts job stamps a task's resolution_payload, outreach writes an OutboundEmail row, and tool/mailer sends leave only Rails.logger lines. There is no queryable ledger answering 'what did Savant send, from which mailbox, to whom, when, with what provider message id'.
failure_or_value: Concrete value: (1) audit-ready answers to Brian's most common question ('did that email actually go out?') without grepping Render logs; (2) a reliable data source for the 'check email before cold' warm/cold rule and duplicate-send forensics (e.g. after a send_unconfirmed hold, a human today has to open the mailbox's Sent folder — a ledger row with provider_message_id settles it instantly); (3) drift detection between what agents claim they sent and what the clients transmitted.
fix_sketch: Additive migration: outbound_mail_logs (provider, mailbox, kind[send/reply], to/cc/bcc jsonb, subject, provider_message_id, conversation_id, source tag, task_id/outbound_email_id nullable, sent_at, has_attachments). At the tail of GmailMailboxClient#send_message/#reply_message and MicrosoftGraphClient#send_message/#reply_message (after the API call succeeds, skipped when MailboxCapture.active?), write a row best-effort inside a rescue StandardError that only logs — a ledger bug must never fail a send. Source tag via an optional keyword or Current attribute. Expose read-only via an additive /api/v1 endpoint later if useful. No existing fields renamed, no schema drops.

verdict.reason: Re-read all five cited sites plus every caller. Confirmed: four distinct send paths record differently or not at all. MailboxMailDelivery#deliver! (mailbox_mail_delivery.rb:34-49) discards the client result, so every ActionMailer send persists nothing. MicrosoftGraphClient#send_message's plain sendMail path (microsoft_graph_client.rb:194-196) returns no provider message id at all, so even SendApprovedDraftsJob's resolution_payload stamp (send_approved_drafts_job.rb:343) records message_id=nil for Graph sends. OutboundEmail cannot serve as the ledger — it validates presence of a person or ticket_search_result (outbound_email.rb:62-66). schema.rb has no unified outbound table. The codebase documents the gap itself: the send_unconfirmed hold tells a human to 'check the mailbox's Sent folder' (send_approved_drafts_job.rb:268). One overstatement in the finding: Ask Savant send_mail/reply_mail DO persist an AgentRun audit row via audit! (tool_executor.rb:1901, 1981, 4786-4799), not just logger lines — but that is a generic JSON-blob run log, not a queryable mail ledger, so the upgrade stands. Fix is additive, feasible, and high-value for exactly the failure modes the code already escalates to humans.
verdict.ship_risk: Low if built as sketched. touches_client_email=false is correct: the ledger is passive recording after an already-authorized send; it enables no new sends and must not add any. API/schema risk is nil if the migration is purely additive (new outbound_mail_logs table, no renames/drops) and any /api/v1 exposure is a new endpoint. Two real risks to manage: (1) the ledger insert must be rescue StandardError + log-only and skipped when MailboxCapture.active?, or a DB hiccup could fail a send that already left the mailbox (the worst outcome — mail sent, caller told it failed, possible double-send on retry); write the row AFTER the provider call succeeds, never inside the SendApprovedDraftsJob row-lock transaction. (2) provider_message_id will be nil for Graph plain sendMail (the API returns nothing); either accept nil or switch Graph sends to the existing draft+send path — the latter changes the Graph send flow and should be a separate, tested step. Minor: the table duplicates recipients/subjects into a new store, so access should follow the existing brain permission model.

title: Ambiguous transport failures (ECONNRESET/EPIPE) clear the send claim and can double-send an approved email
description: record_send_failure! treats every client error as 'definitely not sent' and clears send_started_at for retry, exempting only Faraday::TimeoutError causes. But both clients wrap ALL Faraday errors into their Error class (microsoft_graph_client.rb:233, gmail_mailbox_client.rb:172), and Faraday's net_http adapter surfaces Errno::ECONNRESET / EPIPE / EOFError — connection dropped AFTER the request body was transmitted — as Faraday::ConnectionFailed, not TimeoutError. Those are exactly as ambiguous as a read timeout: Graph/Gmail may have accepted and sent the message while only the response was lost.
failure_or_value: Sequence: sweep N sends an approved sponsor email via Graph; the TLS connection resets after the POST /sendMail body is transmitted but before the 202 arrives; Faraday raises ConnectionFailed; record_send_failure! clears send_started_at (cause is not TimeoutError); sweep N+1 (2 minutes later, config/recurring.yml) re-claims and re-sends. The client receives the same email twice — the exact failure mode the send_started_at claim exists to prevent.
fix_sketch: Invert to a whitelist of provably-pre-send failures. In both clients, raise a distinct subclass for HTTP-status rejections (e.g. class RequestRejected < Error around the 'API error <status>' raise; keep AuthError). In record_send_failure!, only clear send_started_at when the error is a RequestRejected/AuthError (or when error.cause is nil); for any wrapped transport error (TimeoutError, ConnectionFailed, SSL errors) leave the claim in place so the existing UNCONFIRMED_SEND_GRACE hold escalates to a human. Additive classes, no API/schema change.

verdict.reason: Re-read all three cited files plus the vendored faraday-net_http 3.4.4 adapter. Confirmed: record_send_failure! (send_approved_drafts_job.rb:235) exempts only Faraday::TimeoutError causes before clearing the send_started_at claim (line 239); both mail clients wrap all Faraday errors into their Error class (microsoft_graph_client.rb:233, gmail_mailbox_client.rb:172) so error.cause is the raw Faraday class; and the adapter (vendor/bundle/.../faraday-net_http-3.4.4/lib/faraday/adapter/net_http.rb:15-36,63-75) maps Errno::ECONNRESET, EPIPE, IOError/EOFError, and Net::HTTPBadResponse to Faraday::ConnectionFailed (SSL errors to Faraday::SSLError), never TimeoutError. Concrete failing input: the socket resets while reading the response to an already-transmitted POST /sendMail (Graph) or /users/me/messages/send (Gmail) -> ConnectionFailed -> claim cleared -> next 2-minute sweep re-claims and re-sends a non-idempotent send endpoint -> duplicate email to the recipient. The job's own comment (lines 230-233) states the ambiguity principle; the implementation under-covers it. Downgraded high->medium because two facts I verified narrow the trigger window: the adapter opens a fresh connection per request (http.start block, no keep-alive reuse, so no stale-connection RST race) and sets http.max_retries=0, so only a genuine mid-flight reset in the post-write/pre-response window on a fresh socket triggers it. Real, but rare; impact (duplicate approved client-facing email, defeating the exact invariant the claim machinery protects) keeps it above low.
verdict.ship_risk: Low-to-moderate. No client-email re-enablement: this path sends only Brian-approved drafts (sanctioned outbound), and the fix touches no sponsor-portal/reminder mailers. No /api/v1 field or DB schema changes; new error subclasses are additive and remain rescuable via the existing MicrosoftGraphClient::Error/GmailMailboxClient::Error rescues if subclassed. Main ship risk is over-correction: Faraday::ConnectionFailed also covers provably-pre-send failures (ECONNREFUSED, SocketError/DNS, Net::OpenTimeout, EHOSTUNREACH) that today auto-retry silently; a blanket 'hold all transport errors' would bounce approved cards back to Brian's phone queue as send_unconfirmed holds on every transient network blip, delaying legitimate approved sends and adding noise for a non-technical operator. Mitigate by distinguishing the underlying cause (error.cause.cause is the original Errno; hold on ECONNRESET/EPIPE/IOError/HTTPBadResponse/SSLError, keep retrying ECONNREFUSED/SocketError/OpenTimeout) and by adding specs for both branches so the green suite stays green.

title: resolve_mailbox misses 'From: Name <addr>' headers, silently sending from the wrong mailbox
description: resolve_mailbox extracts an explicit From address with body[/^\s*From:\s*([^\s<>]+@[^\s<>]+)/i, 1], which only matches a bare address ('From: brian@hardwarefyi.com'). A display-name form ('From: Brian D'Erario <brian@hardwarefyi.com>') never matches because the token after 'From:' contains no '@'. The job then falls through to TaskNotes' fuzzy sender (/from:\s*brian/i matches the same line, giving :brian) and SENDER_MAILBOX maps 'brian' => brian@kerrihq.com (line 23), a different mailbox on a different domain and provider (Gmail instead of Graph).
failure_or_value: A card whose draft header reads 'From: Brian <brian@hardwarefyi.com>' is approved; the email goes out from brian@kerrihq.com instead of brian@hardwarefyi.com. The sign-off check cannot catch it (both mailboxes sign 'Brian' per Outbound::PreSendCheck::EXPECTED_SIGNERS), so a client receives Hardware FYI business mail from the wrong company domain, and the reply lands in the wrong inbox/thread history.
fix_sketch: In resolve_mailbox, after the bare-address attempt, also try body[/^\s*From:[^\n<]*<([^\s<>]+@[^\s<>]+)>/i, 1] and use whichever hits (still validated against GRAPH_MAILBOXES/GMAIL_MAILBOXES, still routing standardandworks to nil). Add a spec for the display-name form. One method, no schema/API change.

verdict.reason: Mechanically reproduced on the real code: ran the exact regex at app/jobs/send_approved_drafts_job.rb:174 against a body containing "From: Brian D'Erario <brian@hardwarefyi.com>" — explicit extraction returns nil (the char class [^\s<>] excludes '<' so a bracketed address is unreachable, and the display-name token has no '@'). The job then falls to TaskNotes#parse_sender (app/services/task_notes.rb:74), whose /from:\s*brian/i branch matches the same line and returns :brian, and SENDER_MAILBOX["brian"] (job line 23) is brian@kerrihq.com (Gmail) — not the explicitly named brian@hardwarefyi.com, which IS in MicrosoftGraphClient::ALLOWED_MAILBOXES (microsoft_graph_client.rb:20) and would have been chosen had the regex matched. Outbound::PreSendCheck::EXPECTED_SIGNERS maps both mailboxes to "Brian" (pre_send_check.rb:24-25), so the sign-off hold cannot catch it; the client email sends from the wrong domain/provider with no hold, event, or warning, and replies land in the wrong inbox. Card bodies are LLM/human-written with no code-enforced From format (the canonical prompt at ask_savant/tools.rb:1524 asks for a bare address but nothing validates it), and the job itself documents that agents drift from exact formats (the SEND_VERB_VARIANT comment at lines 79-81 records a prior production incident of exactly this kind). Also found while verifying: "From: <addr>" (angle-only) fails BOTH the explicit regex and the fuzzy sender, silently stalling an approved non-S&W card unsent. Severity stays medium: real, silent, client-facing wrong-domain sends, but requires a non-canonical (though highly natural) header form.
verdict.ship_risk: Low blast radius. The fix adds a second additive regex attempt in one private method (resolve_mailbox); extracted addresses are still validated against GRAPH_MAILBOXES/GMAIL_MAILBOXES and the standardandworks→nil routing must be kept for the bracketed form too. No API field or DB schema change, so agent pollers are unaffected. Client-email note: this job already sends Brian-approved client mail — the change does NOT re-enable any banned sponsor-facing mailer (SponsorPortalMailer/SponsorAssetReminderService untouched); it only makes the sending mailbox honor the From address Brian saw when approving. Behavior only changes where the explicit bracketed address disagrees with the fuzzy fallback (the bug case) — verified that "From: Kerri <kerri@hardwarefyi.com>" and "From: Brian <brian@kerrihq.com>" resolve to the same mailbox before and after. Ship with specs for display-name, angle-only, S&W-bracketed, and non-allowlisted-bracketed forms, and run the full suite (main is green).

title: Gmail sweep/list is a sequential N+1 fetching full MIME payloads it discards
description: search_messages and messages_since call full_message(id) — GET /messages/{id}?format=full — once per message, sequentially, then normalize with include_body: false, discarding the body they just downloaded. A messages_since(max: 200) sweep issues up to 201 sequential HTTPS round-trips, each returning the complete MIME payload, and each format=full messages.get costs 5 Gmail quota units.
failure_or_value: Concrete value: the brian@kerrihq.com inbox sweep (which runs on a schedule and blocks the agent turn) currently spends roughly 100-250ms per message — 20-50 seconds and ~1000 quota units for a busy 200-message window — to build previews it could get from headers+snippet. Switching listings to format=metadata cuts payload size by orders of magnitude and quota to 1-2 units per get, making sweeps several times faster and far less likely to hit per-user rate limits.
fix_sketch: Add full_message(message_id, format: "full") and have search_messages/messages_since request format: "metadata", metadataHeaders: MESSAGE_HEADERS. normalize_message already works from headers/snippet/labelIds, all present in metadata format; has_attachments (derived from payload parts, absent in metadata) should be omitted from listing rows or defaulted false — read_message/read_thread keep format=full and full attachment data, and agents already fetch those for detail. Read-only internal change; API response fields stay additive-compatible (has_attachments simply absent on listings, matching the .compact behavior for other nil fields).

verdict.reason: Re-read confirms the core claim on the real code path. gmail_mailbox_client.rb:33-35 (search_messages) and :58 (messages_since) call full_message(id) once per message, sequentially, and full_message at :231-233 hardcodes format: "full", so each listing row downloads the complete MIME payload. normalize_message(include_body: false) at :294-313 then uses only headers, snippet, labelIds, and internalDate — all available from format=metadata with metadataHeaders — plus has_attachments derived from payload parts. The body is downloaded and discarded. Live callers confirm impact: ask_savant/tool_executor.rb:1529 (search_mail, up to 50 sequential full fetches inside an interactive agent turn) and :1583 (begin_mail_sweep via messages_since, up to 200 fetches when brian@kerrihq.com is in the sweep's mailboxes). The sibling MicrosoftGraphClient (microsoft_graph_client.rb:76-99) pages 50 messages per request with $select and no per-message fetch, so the Gmail client is a genuine outlier N+1 and the fix is a straight parity upgrade. Downstream check: upsert_sweep_item (tool_executor.rb:1727) uses only conversation_id/from/subject/received_at, so losing has_attachments on listing rows breaks nothing. Two overstatements in the finding: (1) the quota arithmetic is unverified — Gmail charges messages.get at 5 units regardless of format per current docs, so the win is payload size/latency, not documented quota units; (2) SWEEP_DEFAULT_MAILBOXES are the three @hardwarefyi.com Graph mailboxes, so the 200-message Gmail worst case only occurs when brian@kerrihq.com is explicitly in the schedule's mailboxes and the watermark window is large (catch-up after a failed run). Also note the metadata switch keeps the sequential round trips — it shrinks each one; batching would be a further win. None of this changes the verdict: real, feasible, does not already exist.
verdict.ship_risk: Low. Read-only internal change to listing calls; read_message/read_thread/download_attachment/reply_message keep format=full so bodies and attachment IDs are unaffected, and no send path is touched (touches_client_email=false). Two things to guard: (1) has_attachments on listing rows — safest is to default it false rather than omit, since agent prompts or future code may pattern-match on the key; either way it is a listing-row-only change, not a /api/v1 field rename. (2) metadataHeaders must include the full MESSAGE_HEADERS list (it already has both Message-ID and Message-Id spellings) or reply threading built from a listing-sourced id would still work since reply_message re-fetches format=full itself. Verify with a capture-fixture spec plus one live sweep against brian@kerrihq.com before calling it done.

title: Outreach send path bypasses the em-dash scrub and GroundTruthGuard that every other send path has
description: SendOutreachEmailJob delivers LLM-generated sponsor outreach (OutreachMailer renders outbound_email.body_plain verbatim) without OutboundText.without_em_dashes and without Outbound::GroundTruthGuard. Both protections run on the Ask Savant tool path (tool_executor.rb:1895-1896) and the approved-drafts path (send_approved_drafts_job.rb:127,167), so this is the one externally-facing send route where an em dash or a wrong dollar figure sails through in code.
failure_or_value: Concrete value: closes the last gap in two of Brian's hard rules. An outreach body generated with '$15,000 — our top package' currently goes to a sponsor with the em dash intact and, if the CRM deal says $12,000, with the wrong figure unchecked. After the fix, the same guarantees hold on every automated send path. This adds zero new email — it only filters/holds sends that were already queued by the existing human-initiated outreach flow, keeping client email posture unchanged.
fix_sketch: In OutreachMailer#outreach_email set @body = OutboundText.without_em_dashes(outbound_email.body_plain) and pass subject through the same scrub. In SendOutreachEmailJob#perform, after claim_for_sending and before deliver_now, run Outbound::GroundTruthGuard.check(organization: outbound_email.organization, body: outbound_email.body_plain, to: outbound_email.to_email, subject: outbound_email.subject); if result.blocked?, mark_failed with the guard summary (or a new held-style delivery_error) instead of sending — warn mode (the current default) stays log-only, so behavior only changes when the guard is flipped to enforce.

verdict.reason: Every cited claim survives re-reading. (1) OutreachMailer#outreach_email (app/mailers/outreach_mailer.rb:15-16) sets @body = outbound_email.body_plain verbatim; no OutboundText.without_em_dashes anywhere on the path. (2) SendOutreachEmailJob#perform (app/jobs/send_outreach_email_job.rb:11-13) goes claim_for_sending -> deliver_now with no Outbound::GroundTruthGuard call. (3) The two comparison paths really do have both protections: ask_savant/tool_executor.rb:1883-1896 runs GroundTruthGuard.check then without_em_dashes on subject+body, and send_approved_drafts_job.rb:127-133 and :167 do the same even on human-approved cards. (4) The outreach body is LLM-generated: SponsorOutreachGenerator (Ollama, app/services/sponsor_outreach_generator.rb) fills deal.parsed_outreach_email, and OutreachGenerator fills TicketSearchResult#email_outreach_body; both prefill the send form (outreach_emails_controller.rb:12-16, ticket_search_result_outreach_emails_controller.rb:14) and neither generator prompt even mentions the no-em-dash rule (the sponsor prompt's own instructions contain em dashes). (5) OutboundText's header comment claims to be "the guarantee: an em dash that slips through is replaced ... before the email leaves" (app/services/outbound_text.rb:4-6), a guarantee this route silently voids. (6) It is genuinely the last gap: the only other mailers are account_management, invitation (non-LLM system mail), and sponsor_portal (internal-only). Concrete input: Ollama emits "our top package is $15,000 — happy to walk you through it" into the prefilled form; a user taps Send unedited; the sponsor receives the em dash intact, and if the CRM deal says $12,000 the mismatch is never even logged. Human review on the form is not a refutation, since the approved-drafts path enforces both checks after human approval by design. Kept medium (not raised): the path is human-initiated with a visible preview, and the guard's default warn mode means the dollar-figure half is log-only until enforce is flipped.
verdict.ship_risk: Low. No new email is created and no banned client-facing mail is re-enabled; the change only scrubs/filters sends already initiated by a human through the existing outreach form, so the client-email ban posture is unchanged (touches_client_email=true only because the recipients are sponsors). Em-dash scrub is a pure text transform (also apply to subject); the guard call in warn mode (current prod default) is log-only, and it fails open by design, so behavior changes only if OUTBOUND_GROUND_TRUTH_GUARD is flipped to enforce, at which point a blocked send should use mark_failed with the guard summary so it surfaces via the existing failed status + Turbo broadcast rather than a new state. API/schema compat is clean: no fields renamed, delivery_status enum values reused. Residual risks: (a) in enforce mode a legitimate multi-deal or renewal email quoting a new price could be held, so keep the guard's warn-first rollout discipline; (b) any spec asserting OutreachMailer renders body_plain verbatim will need updating alongside the change; (c) the scrub converts em dashes to commas, so a body a human just previewed will differ slightly from what sends, matching the already-accepted behavior of the approved-drafts path.

title: SendApprovedDraftsJob strips em dashes from the body but not the subject
description: claim_for_send returns body: OutboundText.without_em_dashes(body.to_s) (line 167) but subject: subject unfiltered (line 166; subject comes from the draft's Subject header or task title at line 125). The Ask Savant tool path scrubs both subject and body (tool_executor.rb:1895-1896), so this path is inconsistent with the coded guarantee.
failure_or_value: An approved draft whose subject line is 'Q3 partnership — next steps' sends with the em dash intact, violating Brian's hard no-em-dash rule in the most visible part of the email (the recipient's inbox list) despite the rule being 'code-enforced'.
fix_sketch: Change line 166 to subject: OutboundText.without_em_dashes(subject.to_s). Note OutboundText replaces an em dash with ', ' which reads fine in subjects ('Q3 partnership, next steps'). Add a one-line spec beside the existing body-scrub spec.

verdict.reason: Re-read confirms the asymmetry: send_approved_drafts_job.rb:166 returns subject unfiltered while :167 scrubs the body with OutboundText.without_em_dashes, and the Ask Savant send path (tool_executor.rb:1895-1896) scrubs both, so the subject gap breaks the coded guarantee at this boundary. The refutation attempt failed: OutboundText is used nowhere upstream of this job for API-created cards (Api::V1::TasksController#create applies no scrubbing), so a card filed by the Slack agent with 'Subject: Q3 partnership — next steps' in its draft headers sends with the em dash intact after Brian approves it. Concrete input, real path. Severity stays low: it violates Brian's hard style rule in the recipient's inbox line but is not a correctness or data-integrity failure, and agent prompts already discourage em dashes so frequency is low.
verdict.ship_risk: Low. The fix is a one-line text transform at send time on an already-approved internal send path; it does not enable any new client-facing email (touches_client_email only in the sense that it edits text of mail Brian already approved) and changes no API field, so agent compatibility is unaffected. Two small risks to note: (1) the sent subject can differ slightly from the subject Brian saw on the approval card (em dash rendered as a comma), same as the existing body behavior; (2) if a draft replies to an inbound thread whose subject contained an em dash, rewriting the subject could split subject-based threading in some recipients' clients (the job sends via send_message with no In-Reply-To headers, so this is the only threading mechanism at play). Both are rare and cosmetic; add the suggested spec beside the body-scrub spec and run the full suite.

title: OutboundEmail.message_id is a phantom; real Graph/Gmail message ids are discarded at delivery
description: OutboundEmail#generate_message_id stores a locally-minted '<uuid@hardwarefyi.com>' that never reaches the wire — MailboxMailDelivery's header note (lines 19-21) documents that Graph/Gmail generate their own Message-ID and custom headers are not transmitted. Meanwhile deliver! (line 44-48) receives the client's result hash containing the real provider id (and Gmail threadId) and throws it away, so no outreach record can ever be matched to the actual sent message or its reply thread.
failure_or_value: Concrete value: reply detection and thread correlation for sponsor outreach become possible (today, answering 'did Acme reply to our outreach?' requires a manual mailbox search because the stored message_id matches nothing in the mailbox). Also powers the check-email-before-cold rule: an agent can look up the provider conversation_id and read the actual thread. Purely additive plumbing on the existing send; no new client email.
fix_sketch: In MailboxMailDelivery#deliver!, capture result = client.send_message(...) and stash it on the in-memory mail object after the send (e.g. mail.header['X-Savant-Provider-Message-Id'] = result[:id].to_s and 'X-Savant-Provider-Thread-Id' = result[:conversation_id].to_s — set post-send, so never transmitted). In SendOutreachEmailJob, mail = OutreachMailer.outreach_email(outbound_email).deliver_now, then persist the two values into NEW nullable columns provider_message_id/provider_thread_id (additive migration; leave the existing message_id column untouched for API compatibility).

verdict.reason: Every structural claim survives re-reading: OutboundEmail#generate_message_id (outbound_email.rb:58-59) mints a local '<uuid@hardwarefyi.com>' that MailboxMailDelivery's own header note (mailbox_mail_delivery.rb:19-21) and OutreachMailer's comment (outreach_mailer.rb:8-14) confirm never reaches the wire; deliver! (lines 44-48) returns the client result but Mail#deliver returns the mail object, so SendOutreachEmailJob:13 genuinely cannot see it. The finding actually UNDERSTATES the value: process_inbound_email_job.rb:96-98 matches inbound In-Reply-To against OutboundEmail.message_id, a lookup that can never succeed post-SendGrid — so reply-to-org threading is silently dead code today. One correction to the sketch: only GmailMailboxClient returns id/conversation_id (gmail_mailbox_client.rb:134); MicrosoftGraphClient#send_message uses /sendMail which returns 202 empty-body, so its result hash (microsoft_graph_client.rb:196) has no id at all — and the default outreach sender kerri@hardwarefyi.com is a Graph mailbox, i.e. the dominant path. Capturing Graph ids requires switching the no-attachment send to the draft-create+send flow already used at microsoft_graph_client.rb:189-192 (ideally with Prefer: IdType=ImmutableId), or a post-send Sent Items lookup. With that amendment the upgrade is real, feasible, additive, and does not already exist.
verdict.ship_risk: No client-email re-enablement: zero new sends, metadata capture only, and the ban stays intact. But the full fix touches the LIVE sponsor-outreach send path: for Graph mailboxes it must change /sendMail to draft-create+send to obtain the id, which alters how every Graph outreach email is transmitted (deliverability/formatting regression risk; mitigated because the attachment path already uses that exact flow in production). If shipped only as sketched (capture result hash), Graph sends store nil provider ids and the feature underdelivers on its main use case. Graph message ids are mutable across folder moves unless ImmutableId is requested — without it, stored ids can go stale. API/DB compat is clean: two new nullable columns, existing message_id field and /api/v1 payloads untouched. Do NOT retro-populate or change generate_message_id — message_id has a uniqueness validation and a live (if dead-lettered) lookup consumer.

title: Failed outreach emails keep a populated sent_at (stamped at claim time, never cleared)
description: claim_for_sending stamps sent_at: Time.current when transitioning queued -> sending (line 47), before any delivery happens. mark_failed (line 54) sets delivery_status: :failed but leaves sent_at populated, so every failed outreach row permanently carries a sent_at as if it went out.
failure_or_value: Concrete failure: OutreachMailer raises (template bug or Graph/Gmail error) after the claim; the record ends delivery_status: failed with sent_at set. Any query, CSV export, or agent reading /api/v1 data that treats sent_at presence as 'this email was sent' (a natural reading) counts failed sends as delivered — inflating outreach activity in exactly the reporting Brian can't verify by reading code.
fix_sketch: Move the sent_at stamp to the success update (outbound_email.update!(delivery_status: :sent, sent_at: Time.current) at line 15) and have claim_for_sending set only delivery_status: :sending; in mark_failed also clear it (sent_at: nil) for rows failing after a claim. Additive behavior change on existing columns' values only — no field renames, and :sending rows keep their investigable state.

verdict.reason: Verified on the real code: send_outreach_email_job.rb:47 stamps sent_at at claim time (queued -> sending) before delivery, and mark_failed (lines 54-55) sets delivery_status: :failed without clearing sent_at, so every post-claim failure (Graph/Gmail client error or any StandardError from the mailer) permanently keeps a populated sent_at. Concrete downstream effect exists: email_tracking_controller.rb:83 adds a :sent timeline event whenever sent_at is present with no failed-status exclusion, so failed emails render as sent in the tracking timeline; ticket_search_result.rb:155 also seeds first_email_at from minimum(:sent_at) including failed rows. However, the finding's /api/v1 impact claim is overstated: no API serializer exposes OutboundEmail.sent_at, and the tracking stats count by delivery_status (failed counted separately), so headline metrics are unaffected. Real bug, small blast radius, severity stays low.
verdict.ship_risk: Low. The fix only changes when internal column values are written (stamp sent_at on the success update, clear it in mark_failed); no API fields renamed or removed, no schema change, no client-email surface touched (OutreachMailer is the existing approved outreach path and the fix enables no new sends, touches_client_email=false). Two watch-items: (1) existing failed rows in prod keep their stale sent_at unless a one-off backfill nulls them, so historical timelines stay slightly wrong; (2) a process crash between deliver_now and the success update! would leave a :sending row with sent_at nil even though mail went out, but that ambiguity already exists today (the row is stuck in :sending either way) so it is no worse. Any specs asserting sent_at is set during :sending will need updating.

title: FlowExecutor holds a DB transaction + row lock across entire step execution, so a crash mid-step rolls back the ledger after external sends already happened (duplicate-send risk)
description: Agents::FlowExecutor#step! wraps the ENTIRE step execution in `@flow.with_lock` (flow_executor.rb:54), which opens a Postgres transaction and holds a SELECT FOR UPDATE on the agent_flows row for the whole step. A step includes multi-minute nested LLM runs (run_agent_prompt -> AskSavant::Agent#respond over Ollama HTTP), external tool calls (send_mail, Slack posts via Graph/Slack HTTP), and even `sleep(1-2s)` transient-retry pauses (transient_retry_sleep) - all inside that open transaction. Two consequences: (1) if the process dies mid-step (deploy restart, OOM), the transaction rolls back - step.run!/succeed!, appended task events, and every DB row the nested tools created are erased, but the external side effects (mail actually sent, Slack message actually posted) are NOT undone; (2) any concurrent AgentFlowStepJob for the same flow (the 30-minute stale sweeper in AgentScheduleDispatcherJob, an approval-decision resume, a redundant enqueue) BLOCKS on the row lock for up to the full step duration, silently tying up a second Solid Queue worker (which runs inside Puma).
failure_or_value: Concrete failure: flow = [approval step (succeeded), tool step send_mail]. The tool step executes: Graph API sends the mail, step.succeed! is written inside the still-open transaction, then Render restarts the dyno mid-commit window. The transaction rolls back, the step is back to queued/running in the DB, Solid Queue re-dispatches (or the 30-min stale sweeper re-enqueues), step! re-runs the tool step - the approval before it is still `succeeded`, so confirm:true is auto-set and the mail is sent a SECOND time to the same recipient. Separately, while any step's nested LLM run is in flight (10+ minutes on Ollama), every redundant AgentFlowStepJob blocks on the FOR UPDATE instead of no-oping, starving the in-Puma worker pool.
fix_sketch: Split step! into claim/execute/record phases: (1) short `with_lock` transaction that finds the next actionable step, transitions it to running with a lease token (e.g. `executor_lease` + `lease_expires_at` columns, additive migration) and COMMITS; (2) execute the step (LLM/tool call, retries, sleeps) with NO transaction open; (3) short `with_lock` transaction that verifies the lease still matches, then persists succeed!/fail!/wait_for_approval! and advances the pointer. Idempotency moves from the row lock to the lease: a duplicate job that cannot claim the lease returns :noop immediately instead of blocking. For consequential tools, additionally write a durable 'tool attempt started' marker (committed before the external call) so a crash between send and record is detected as 'attempted, outcome unknown' and surfaced as a card instead of silently re-sent.

verdict.reason: Re-read confirms every element on the real code path. flow_executor.rb:54 wraps the entire step in @flow.with_lock (one Postgres transaction + FOR UPDATE row lock held to block end), and inside it run_step performs multi-minute external work: nested AskSavant::Agent#respond over Ollama HTTP (line 166), synchronous Graph/Gmail HTTP in tool_executor.rb:1891 for send_mail, plus 1-2s sleeps (line 500). All nested AR writes (step.run!/succeed!, audit!, mark_executed!, task events, flow.updated_at) join that single transaction. Concrete duplicate-send input: flow = [succeeded approval step (committed earlier), tool step send_mail]; worker killed mid-step (Render deploy SIGKILL — steps can legally run up to AgentFlowStepJob's 15-minute cap, exceeding any shutdown grace) after the HTTP send but before commit. Rollback leaves the tool step queued, the approval still approved (mark_executed! rolled back), and flow.updated_at stale; Solid Queue releases the dead claim and AgentScheduleDispatcherJob:27 re-enqueues after 30 min; step! re-passes the approval guard (line 253), re-sets confirm:true (line 261), and sends the same mail again with no surviving marker of the first attempt. The lock-blocking half is also real: no lock_timeout is configured, so any redundant AgentFlowStepJob blocks on FOR UPDATE for the full step duration, occupying an in-Puma Solid Queue worker thread and a DB connection. No lease/advisory-lock/attempt-marker mechanism exists anywhere in the repo to refute this.
verdict.ship_risk: Medium. The fix does not touch client email (client sends stay behind the same approval gate; the change strictly reduces unintended duplicate external sends) and needs no API field or schema removals — lease columns are additive. Main risks: (1) lease logic bugs could wedge flows (lease never expiring means the sweeper's re-enqueue becomes a permanent :noop) or, if the lease check is wrong, allow two executors to run one step concurrently — needs lease_expires_at + tests for claim/expiry/duplicate-claim; (2) moving execution outside the transaction changes failure semantics: a mid-execute crash now leaves a durable running step with an attempt marker that must be surfaced as an 'attempted, outcome unknown' card rather than silently retried, so the recovery path (sweeper + AgentFlowStepJob) must be updated in the same PR to avoid regressing crash recovery into a stall; (3) the existing green test suite encodes the current single-transaction semantics, so several FlowExecutor specs will need rework, raising the review burden. Recommend shipping with the sweeper behavior change and a manual resume path verified end-to-end before deploy.

title: ScheduledAgentRunJob never advances agent.last_run_at, so schedule-driven agents with a report interval permanently trip 'Agent overdue' cards and drift signals
description: Agent.overdue keys on COALESCE(last_run_at, created_at) vs report_interval_hours (agent.rb:56-59). last_run_at is only written by Agent#record_run! (API-reported runs) and Slack::EventProcessor (event_processor.rb:416/437). ScheduledAgentRunJob creates and finishes AgentRun rows directly via `schedule.agent.runs.find_or_initialize_by ... run.update!` (scheduled_agent_run_job.rb:50, 73-82) and never touches agent.last_run_at. Since routines migrated from external POSTing to native AgentSchedules, any agent whose SKILL.md frontmatter sets report_interval_hours (synced by AgentPromptSyncJob:48) but whose runs now come exclusively through AgentSchedule will have a frozen last_run_at.
failure_or_value: An agent like kerri-inbox-sweep with report_interval_hours=24 runs green every hour via its AgentSchedule, yet once last_run_at (or created_at) ages past 24h it enters Agent.overdue forever: AgentHealthCheckJob files a fresh 'Agent overdue: ...' action_needed card on Brian's board every single day, and AgentDriftMonitor adds a permanent 'agent(s) overdue on reporting' warn signal to the 7:30am drift heartbeat and /api/v1 runtime health - alarm fatigue that trains Brian to ignore the drift channel, which exists precisely to catch real silent failures.
fix_sketch: In ScheduledAgentRunJob#perform, after the successful run.update! (line ~82), add `schedule.agent.update!(last_run_at: finished_at)` (and optionally in record_failure, mirroring event_processor which advances it on failures too so 'reported' means 'ran'). One-line additive change; overdue then means what it says for schedule-driven agents.

verdict.reason: Re-read confirms every link in the chain. Agent.overdue (app/models/agent.rb:56-59) keys on COALESCE(last_run_at, created_at) vs report_interval_hours. The only writers of last_run_at are Agent#record_run! (agent.rb:131-135, reached via POST /api/v1/agent_runs and the create_agent_run tool) and Slack::EventProcessor (event_processor.rb:416/437, which only advances the workspace's resolved Slack agent). ScheduledAgentRunJob (app/jobs/scheduled_agent_run_job.rb:50, 73-83, 435) writes AgentRun rows and schedule.last_finished_at directly and never touches agent.last_run_at. Concrete failing input already live in prod: Vaughn — Agents::OrgProvisioner hard-codes report_interval_hours: 24 and provisions a daily AgentSchedule as his only run source (live 2026-07-01, per project state); AgentPromptSyncJob cannot clear the interval because Vaughn is not repo-synced. ~24h after provisioning he permanently enters Agent.overdue despite green daily scheduled runs, so AgentHealthCheckJob (recurring.yml prod, 7am daily; per-day external_ref dedupe means a NEW card each day) files a daily false 'Agent overdue: Vaughn' action_needed card, and AgentDriftMonitor#overdue_agents (agent_drift_monitor.rb:105-107) adds a permanent warn signal to the 7:30am DriftHeartbeatJob, defeating that monitor's stated high-precision guarantee. Severity medium is right: no data loss, but persistent false alarms on the exact channel built to catch real silent agent failures.
verdict.ship_risk: Low. The fix (schedule.agent.update!(last_run_at: finished_at) after the successful run.update! in ScheduledAgentRunJob#perform, and mirrored in record_failure to match Slack::EventProcessor's advance-on-failure semantics) is an additive write to an existing column — no schema change, no field rename. API compatibility: last_run_at is already exposed read-only (list_agents_tool, brain_exporter); its value simply becomes fresh instead of stale, which is the field's intended meaning, so agent pollers only see more-correct data. Zero client-email surface (touches_client_email=false; nothing near SponsorPortalMailer/SponsorAssetReminderService). Residual risks to watch: (1) the extra update! adds a row-lock write on agents per scheduled run — negligible at current run volume; (2) advancing last_run_at on failed runs means 'reported' = 'ran, possibly failing', so a permanently-failing schedule would no longer trip 'overdue' — that gap is already covered by ScheduledRunFailureAlertJob and the drift monitor's failed-agent-tasks signal, but worth a sentence in the commit message; (3) add a spec asserting last_run_at advances so the green suite stays green and the behavior is pinned.

title: Rejecting an approval configured with on_reject=skip still fails the whole flow when the next step is a consequential tool
description: resolve_rejected_step honors on_reject='skip' by marking the approval step skipped and resuming (flow_executor.rb:91-95). But the primary reason an approval step exists is to authorize the consequential tool step right after it, and run_tool's policy gate requires the preceding step to be `approval_step? && succeeded?` (flow_executor.rb:253). A skipped approval is not succeeded, so the very next tool step returns the consequential-policy error and fail_flow! kills the entire flow - including all later unrelated steps. The approval card body even promises the opposite: approval_task_body appends '(this step is configured to skip on reject and continue)' (flow_executor.rb:385-386).
failure_or_value: Flow: [step1 approval(on_reject=skip) 'ok to email X?', step2 tool send_mail, step3 agent_prompt 'summarize + file report']. Brian rejects step1 expecting the send to be skipped and the summary to still run (as the card text told him). Instead: step1 skipped -> step2 policy-violation failure -> flow status failed, a red 'Agent flow failed' card is filed, and step3 never runs. Reject-and-continue is broken for exactly the approval-then-act pattern the executor is built around.
fix_sketch: In resolve_rejected_step, after skipping the approval step, cascade-skip the immediately following step when it is a tool step whose tool is in CONSEQUENTIAL_TOOLS (record output {'skipped_because' => 'authorizing approval was rejected'} and an agent_task event), then resume_pointer!. Alternatively, make run_tool treat 'preceding approval skipped via on_reject=skip' as skip-the-tool rather than fail-the-flow. Keep the hard-fail behavior for a tool step whose preceding approval is missing entirely.

verdict.reason: Verified on the real code path: resolve_rejected_step (flow_executor.rb:90-95) marks the approval step `skipped` and resumes, but run_tool's consequential gate (flow_executor.rb:251-254) requires the preceding step to be `approval_step? && succeeded?` — `skipped` is a distinct enum state (agent_flow_step.rb:17-25), so the very next consequential tool step returns the policy error and fail_flow! (flow_executor.rb:409-415) fails the entire flow, fails the AgentTask, files a red failure card, and kills all later steps. This directly contradicts the documented contract in tools.rb:383 ("then the step is skipped and the flow continues") and the approval card text at flow_executor.rb:385-386, while system_prompt.rb:54 mandates approval-immediately-before-consequential-tool as the canonical composition. The existing spec (flow_executor_spec.rb:137-158) only tests skip followed by agent_prompt, so the broken tool path is untested and the green suite doesn't refute the bug. Concrete failing input: [approval(on_reject=skip), tool send_mail, agent_prompt] with the approval rejected.
verdict.ship_risk: Low blast radius: the fix lives entirely in FlowExecutor#resolve_rejected_step (or run_tool), no schema changes, no /api/v1 field changes, so agent API compat is unaffected. touches_client_email=false and the fix strictly reduces sends: a rejected approval now suppresses the gated send instead of erroring — no client-email re-enablement risk. Care points: cascade-skip must apply only to the single tool step directly gated by the rejected approval (later consequential steps keep their own gates), must handle legacy "manual" steps which also count as approval_step?, must keep hard-fail for a consequential tool with no preceding approval at all, and should record a skipped_because output plus an agent_task event so the ledger/audit trail stays honest. Add a spec for approval(on_reject=skip)+consequential tool+trailing step.

title: Upgrade: stale-flow sweeper cannot recover flows wedged in waiting_approval after the approval was already decided
description: The only crash-recovery path for the flow engine is AgentScheduleDispatcherJob#resume_stale_agent_flows, which re-enqueues `AgentFlow.running` untouched for 30 minutes. Flows in waiting_approval are excluded on purpose (they legitimately wait for a human), but the ONLY thing that wakes them is the after_update_commit callback on ApprovalRequest (approval_request.rb:54, 110-117) enqueueing one AgentFlowStepJob. If that single enqueue is lost - Solid Queue insert error in the commit callback, job row deleted, deploy race, or the enqueued job's process dies before step! commits the resolution - the flow sits in waiting_approval forever with a decided approval and nothing ever retries it. Brian approves a card, nothing happens, and there is no signal.
failure_or_value: Concrete value: closes the one unrecoverable wedge state in an otherwise self-healing engine. Today the failure looks like 'I approved the flow step yesterday and the flow is still paused' with no card, no log, and no sweeper coverage; the flow silently never completes and its AgentTask stays running.
fix_sketch: Extend resume_stale_agent_flows with a second query: `AgentFlow.waiting_approval.where(updated_at: ..(now - 10.minutes)).joins(agent_flow_steps: :approval_request).where(agent_flow_steps: { status: :waiting_approval }).where.not(approval_requests: { status: :pending }).distinct.find_each { |flow| AgentFlowStepJob.perform_later(flow.id) }` (match the actual pending-status enum value). FlowExecutor#step! already handles decided approvals idempotently via resolve_waiting_step, so redundant enqueues are harmless.

verdict.reason: Re-read confirms every claim: the stale-flow sweeper (agent_schedule_dispatcher_job.rb:27) sweeps only AgentFlow.running, and the sole automatic wake for waiting_approval flows is a single perform_later in ApprovalRequest's after_update_commit (approval_request.rb:54, 110-117). ApplicationJob has no retry_on (all commented out) and AgentFlowStepJob declares none, so one failed resume job (e.g., lock deadlock during a deploy) or a lost enqueue permanently wedges the flow in waiting_approval with a decided approval — no card, no log, no health-check coverage (grep shows zero agent_flow references in health services). The proposed sweep extension is genuinely idempotent: FlowExecutor#step! is row-lock-guarded and resolve_waiting_step (flow_executor.rb:74-88) handles decided approvals, and agent_flow_step_job.rb:8-9 explicitly documents redundant enqueues as safe. A manual resume_agent_flow tool (tool_executor.rb:4145) covers this state, proving the wedge is real, but it requires someone to notice a silent stall. One fix-sketch refinement: filter to decided statuses [approved, rejected, skipped, executed] rather than .not(status: :pending), because needs_context and expired are treated as still-waiting by resolve_waiting_step and would cause pointless re-enqueues every tick.
verdict.ship_risk: Low. The change is a second read-only query plus enqueues of an already-idempotent, lock-guarded job inside an existing recurring dispatcher; no schema change, no API field change, no client-email surface (approvals/flows are internal board cards only). Worst realistic regression is enqueue churn if the status filter is too loose (needs_context/expired flows re-enqueued each tick as no-ops), avoided by filtering to decided approval statuses explicitly. Keep the query time-guarded (updated_at older than ~10 minutes) so it never races the legitimate callback enqueue, though even that race is harmless under the row lock.

title: Upgrade: no overlap guard on AgentSchedule - a run that outlasts its cadence gets a second concurrent run of the same routine
description: AgentSchedule#enqueue_due_run! advances next_run_at and enqueues unconditionally; ScheduledAgentRunJob's only dedup is per-scheduled_for external_id (agent-schedule:<id>:<timestamp>). Nothing checks whether the PREVIOUS run of the same schedule is still in flight. Ollama-backed sweep runs routinely take tens of minutes; an hourly or custom-interval schedule (e.g. a 30-minute inbox sweep) whose run exceeds the interval gets a second concurrent run with a different timestamp, so both execute fully in parallel.
failure_or_value: Two overlapping inbox-sweep runs both compute the same 'since last successful run' watermark (previous_run_line reads only succeeded runs, and neither in-flight run has finished), so both process the identical mail window and both deliver: duplicate Slack DMs to Brian, duplicate action_needed cards, and doubled Ollama load - exactly the duplicate-drafting noise class that keeps recurring (duplicate inbox-sweep systems, PR #223). Preventing overlap also protects the watermark semantics.
fix_sketch: In ScheduledAgentRunJob#perform, after loading the schedule, add a skip-if-running guard: `in_flight = schedule.agent.runs.where('external_id LIKE ?', "agent-schedule:#{schedule.id}:%").where(status: :running).where(started_at: 2.hours.ago..).where.not(external_id: external_id).exists?` - if true, mark this run's AgentRun row as skipped-for-overlap (or simply return before creating it, logging '[ScheduledRun] overlap: previous run still in flight'). The 2-hour floor prevents a crashed never-finished run from muting the schedule forever. Optionally make it opt-out per schedule via delivery_config['allow_overlap'] (additive).

verdict.reason: Re-read confirms every load-bearing claim. agent_schedule.rb:43-57 advances next_run_at and enqueues unconditionally (with_lock only stops double-enqueue of the same tick); scheduled_agent_run_job.rb:49-51 dedups only by per-timestamp external_id, so a later tick always runs; no limits_concurrency or other guard exists anywhere (ApplicationJob is bare, rg finds nothing). config/queue.yml gives the wildcard worker threads: 2 and recurring.yml ticks the dispatcher every minute in production, so two runs genuinely execute in parallel. Concrete input: a custom schedule with interval_minutes=30 whose Ollama run takes 40 minutes gets run B enqueued at t+30 with a distinct external_id while run A is still status=running. The watermark harm is real: previous_run_line (lines 127-137) takes maximum(finished_at) over succeeded runs and the job nils finished_at at start (line 60), so both concurrent runs compute the identical since-last-run cutoff, sweep the same mail window, and both deliver Slack DMs / action_needed cards - the exact duplicate-drafting class already fought in PRs #223/#274. Minor caveat: harm needs actual parallelism (serial back-to-back execution would self-correct the watermark), but 2 worker threads is the deployed default, so that is not a refutation.
verdict.ship_risk: Low. The guard is job-internal: no API field changes, no schema changes beyond optional additive delivery_config key, and zero client-email surface (scheduled delivery is Slack DM + internal task cards; nothing near SponsorPortalMailer). Two real risks to handle in the fix: (1) a SIGKILLed worker leaves a status=running row with finished_at nil - without the 2-hour started_at floor the skip guard would mute the schedule indefinitely (a Ruby exception is covered by record_failure, process death is not); (2) skip semantics silently drop a tick, so log it and/or consider Solid Queue limits_concurrency(to: 1, key: schedule_id) instead, which serializes runs so the follow-on run sees the prior finish time and the watermark self-corrects - arguably better than skipping. Note the LIKE pattern also matches enqueue_run_now! manual runs, so a manual run in flight will suppress the next scheduled tick; that is probably desired but should be a conscious choice in tests.

title: NO_UPDATES quiet sentinel is ignored for task-delivery schedules - an all-quiet run still files an action_needed card
description: deliver_result returns `file_result_task(schedule, run) if schedule.task?` BEFORE the no_updates_verdict? check (scheduled_agent_run_job.rb:166-170). The sentinel's contract ('nothing is DM'd or filed', per the class comment at lines 30-41) is therefore only honored for agent_run/Slack schedules. A schedule with delivery=task whose prompt uses the NO_UPDATES convention files an 'action_needed' card titled 'Scheduled agent result: <name>' whose body is just the NO_UPDATES verdict, every run.
failure_or_value: Any task-delivery routine adopting the prod-prompt NO_UPDATES convention (live per the inbox-sweep run-scoping work) generates a recurring do-nothing card on Brian's approval board - e.g. an hourly schedule adds up to 24 junk cards/day he has to swipe away on his phone, exactly the noise the sentinel was built to eliminate ('if no changes were made, no need to message me').
fix_sketch: Move the sentinel check first in deliver_result: `return true if no_updates_verdict?(run.output)` before the `schedule.task?` branch. The AgentRun row still records the NO_UPDATES output for audit, and returning true keeps surface_unfiled_output from filing it. One-line reorder; agent_run behavior unchanged.

verdict.reason: Re-read confirms it exactly: app/jobs/scheduled_agent_run_job.rb:166 returns file_result_task for schedule.task? before the no_updates_verdict? check at line 170, so a task-delivery schedule whose run output ends with NO_UPDATES files a fresh action_needed card every run (per-run external_ref at line 194, so no dedup across runs), directly contradicting the sentinel's documented contract at lines 31-34 ("nothing is DM'd or filed"). Concrete input: AgentSchedule with delivery: :task + a prompt using the prod NO_UPDATES convention; every all-quiet run produces a junk "Scheduled agent result: <name>" card whose body ends in the sentinel. The spec suite tests the sentinel only on Slack-delivery schedules (scoping_spec:96-151) and task delivery only with real output (job_spec:33-49), so the interaction is unpinned and the fix breaks no green test. Severity stays low: no known prod schedule combines delivery=task with NO_UPDATES today (inbox sweep is Slack-delivery), so it is a deterministic latent trap rather than active noise.
verdict.ship_risk: Low. Server-side job logic only: no client-facing email (touches_client_email=false), no /api/v1 field changes, no schema changes. Two caveats: (1) the proposed bare reorder would also suppress the card for a FAILED task run whose output ends in NO_UPDATES, hiding the failure from the approval board — guard the early return with run.succeeded? (ScheduledRunFailureAlertJob still fires either way); (2) behavior change: task-delivery schedules lose their card-per-run heartbeat on quiet runs, so anything treating the card cadence as proof-of-run would see gaps (the AgentRun row still records every run, so /api/v1 agent-run audit is unaffected). Add a spec pinning task+NO_UPDATES quiet behavior when shipping.

title: Upgrade: VoiceCalibration.gather_edits loads every org task from the last 30 days and samples an arbitrary (not newest) 25 edits
description: gather_edits runs `organization.tasks.where("updated_at > ?", window_days.days.ago)` with no order and no SQL filter, then Ruby-iterates the ENTIRE result set - instantiating every task and running TaskNotes.parse on each - before `.first(limit)`. Two problems: (a) on a busy org this materializes thousands of task rows (bodies included) and parses them all weekly for at most 25 usable pairs; (b) with no ORDER BY, Postgres returns rows in effectively arbitrary order, so the 25 pairs the calibration learns from are not Brian's most recent edits - the freshest voice feedback (the whole point of the weekly loop) can be crowded out by month-old edits that appear first, run after run.
failure_or_value: Concrete value: the weekly voice loop reliably trains on Brian's LATEST 25 edits instead of a stale arbitrary sample, and the job stops loading/parsing the full 30-day task table (memory + latency win on the Render worker running inside Puma).
fix_sketch: Push filtering and ordering into SQL: `organization.tasks.where("updated_at > ?", window_days.days.ago).where("COALESCE(resolution_payload ->> 'edited_body', '') <> ''").order(updated_at: :desc).limit(limit * 4).filter_map { ... }.first(limit)` (the 4x headroom absorbs pairs dropped by the normalize-equal check). Purely internal to the service; output shape unchanged.

verdict.reason: Re-read app/services/voice_calibration.rb:59-69: the relation has no ORDER BY and no SQL filter, filter_map materializes every org task in the 30-day window (text body included), and .first(25) takes an arbitrary physical-order sample rather than Brian's newest edits. Because the weekly job (config/recurring.yml:106, VoiceCalibrationJob) uses an overlapping 30-day window, stale edits can persistently crowd out the freshest voice signal, which is the loop's whole point. Minor overstatement in the finding: TaskNotes.parse runs only for tasks with a non-blank edited_body, not literally every row, and window volume is likely hundreds not thousands; still, full materialization inside Puma is real. Fix is valid: resolution_payload is jsonb (db/schema.rb:1719) so the ->> predicate plus order(updated_at: :desc) works, output shape unchanged, nothing equivalent already exists.
verdict.ship_risk: Low. Purely internal service change: no /api/v1 field changes, no migrations, and zero client-email surface (the service only reads Graph sent mail, never sends). Two residual risks: (1) the limit*4 SQL cap could return fewer usable pairs than today's exhaustive scan in a week dominated by no-op edits — prefer pushing only the filter+order into SQL without a tight LIMIT; (2) existing voice_calibration specs may assume insertion-order sampling and need updating, and the learned profile will legitimately shift toward newest edits (intended, and revertible via rake voice:revert).

title: Upgrade: AgentRuntimeHealth snapshot has no visibility into AgentFlows (wedged/waiting/failed flows are invisible to the health endpoint and QUEUE badge)
description: AgentRuntimeHealth#snapshot covers slack, model, sessions, tasks, schedules, workspace_runs, and drift - but not the flow engine at all. AgentFlow is now a first-class execution surface (approval-gated multi-step work), and its two known bad states - running-but-stale (lost executor) and waiting_approval on a long-undecided or already-decided approval - never appear in the runtime health payload agents and the QUEUE badge poll. Today the only signal for a stuck flow is Brian noticing a card never arrived.
failure_or_value: Concrete value: `GET /api/v1` runtime health (and anything built on it, like the Savant QUEUE badge diagnosis flow) can name a wedged flow the same way it names a lagging schedule. A flow stuck 45 minutes in running, or waiting_approval for 3 days, becomes a visible counter instead of a silent gap - directly extending the observability posture the snapshot already established for schedules (due count + lag_seconds).
fix_sketch: Add a `flows:` key to #snapshot (additive - API consumers only gain a field): counts of running / waiting_approval / failed_last_24h, plus `stale_running` (running with updated_at older than AgentScheduleDispatcherJob::STALE_FLOW_AFTER) and `oldest_waiting_approval_age_seconds`. Implement with an `agent_flows` scoped-relation helper mirroring the existing agent_tasks/agent_schedules helpers (agent_runtime_health.rb:128-142).

verdict.reason: Re-read confirms AgentRuntimeHealth#snapshot (agent_runtime_health.rb:12-23) has no flows key, AgentDriftMonitor has no flow signals, and no /api/v1 flow health surface exists, while AgentFlow (agent_flow.rb:15-22) is a real org-scoped execution record with running/waiting_approval/failed states and the snapshot is polled by agents via api/v1/agent_runtime_health_controller.rb and the tool_executor. The proposed additive flows counter mirroring the existing agent_tasks/agent_schedules scoped-helper pattern (organization.rb:27 has has_many :agent_flows) is feasible and does not already exist. One overstatement: stale running flows are NOT purely invisible-until-Brian-notices — AgentScheduleDispatcherJob#resume_stale_agent_flows (agent_schedule_dispatcher_job.rb:26-31) auto-re-enqueues them, and ApprovalRequest#resume_waiting_agent_flow (approval_request.rb:110-116) resumes decided approvals. But real gaps remain: waiting_approval flows whose resume enqueue was lost are covered by no sweeper (the sweeper scans only AgentFlow.running), repeated step failures and terminal failed flows appear in no counter (failed_last_24h exists for tasks/workspace_runs but not flows), and long-undecided approval age has no visibility. So the upgrade is confirmed at low severity, not raised.
verdict.ship_risk: Very low. The change is a new additive top-level key in the runtime-health JSON, so agents that poll /api/v1 only gain a field; no existing field is renamed or removed and no DB migration is needed. Zero client-email exposure (touches_client_email=false is correct — pure read-only observability). Main care points: keep the new queries cheap (indexed status counts, one minimum() on waiting_approval) since the endpoint is polled around the clock, and reference AgentScheduleDispatcherJob::STALE_FLOW_AFTER rather than duplicating the 30-minute constant so the two stay in sync.

title: AgentScopeResolver merge() widens an agent's scope to its owner's grants (privilege escalation)
description: AgentScopeResolver#readable_knowledge_scope computes the agent/owner intersection with ActiveRecord `merge`: `agent_resolver.readable_knowledge_scope(base).merge(owner_resolver.readable_knowledge_scope(base))`. Rails merge REPLACES conditions on the same column instead of ANDing them. I verified this empirically in this app: merging `where(sensitivity: ..1, domain_id: X)` with `where(sensitivity: ..3)` produces SQL `domain_id = X AND sensitivity <= 3` — the agent's sensitivity ceiling (1) is silently replaced by the owner's (3). Same replacement applies to domain_id/kind/property_id when both sides carry them. The bug only manifests when each side's scope is a single un-OR'd branch (exactly one read grant each — the common single-purpose-agent shape) and the owner is a non-master user; a master owner returns bare `base` (no predicates) so today's Brian-owned agents are unaffected, which is why the suite is green. The same `merge` hazard exists at api/v1/knowledge_records_controller.rb:78 (`base.merge(agent_scope_resolver.readable_knowledge_scope(base))`, where `base` may carry a brand-wall property_id predicate).
failure_or_value: Agent owned by a non-master user (e.g. Benji once brand-wall memberships land, or Ari without master_access): agent grant = read pipeline domain up to normal_internal; owner grant = read all domains up to finance_sensitive. GET /api/v1/knowledge_records?agent_slug=... returns pipeline records at confidential/finance_sensitive — above the agent's explicit ceiling. If the owner's single grant is domain-scoped to a different domain, the merged scope returns the OWNER's domain — records the agent has no grant for at all.
fix_sketch: Stop using merge for intersection. In AgentScopeResolver#readable_knowledge_scope: `agent_scope = agent_resolver.readable_knowledge_scope(base); owner_scope = owner_resolver.readable_knowledge_scope(base); scoped = agent_scope.where(id: owner_scope.select(:id))` (id-subquery intersection is replacement-proof), then keep the existing source_system gate. In the API controller, replace `base.merge(...)` with `base.where(id: agent_scope_resolver.readable_knowledge_scope(base).select(:id))`. Add a regression spec: agent with one low-ceiling grant + non-master owner with one high-ceiling grant must NOT see high-sensitivity records, and must see nothing when owner grant is a different domain.

verdict.reason: Reproduced end-to-end on the real code path, not just in isolation. Running the actual AgentScopeResolver (RAILS_ENV=test, real factories) with agent grant = pipeline domain / max normal_internal and non-master owner grant = all domains / max confidential: `allowed?(action: :read, domain: pipeline, sensitivity: :confidential)` correctly returns false, but `readable_knowledge_scope` returns BOTH the normal_internal and the confidential pipeline records. The generated SQL shows the agent's `sensitivity <= 1` predicate silently replaced by the owner's `sensitivity <= 2` (Rails merge at app/services/agent_scope_resolver.rb:31-32 drops receiver predicates on columns the merged relation references, including range/lteq predicates). Worse, with the owner's single grant scoped to a different domain, the scope returned ONLY the owner's-domain record ("finance rec") — a domain the agent has zero grants for — while `allowed?` denies pipeline reads entirely. So the list path (which backs GET /api/v1/knowledge_records?agent_slug=... via knowledge_records_controller.rb:78) contradicts the single-record check and inverts the documented intersection invariant. The existing spec at spec/services/agent_scope_resolver_spec.rb:60-73 uses EQUAL sensitivity ceilings on both sides, which is exactly the shape where replacement is invisible — that is why the suite is green. Severity adjusted critical→high because it is latent in current production data: a master-access owner (Brian, or Ari via master_access) makes owner_scope a bare base relation whose only predicates (organization_id) match the agent side, so no replacement damage occurs; exploitation requires a non-master owner with a single un-OR'd read grant. That shape is precisely what the in-flight brand-wall work (Benji HFYI-only, enforcement flipping in PR8) will create, so it must be fixed before that lands. The outer merge at knowledge_records_controller.rb:78 is benign today only because agent scope derives from the same base, but the id-subquery fix should be applied there too for the same reason.
verdict.ship_risk: Low. The fix (agent_scope.where(id: owner_scope.select(:id)) instead of merge) only ever narrows results toward the documented intersection, so it is a tightening, never a widening. No touches_client_email: this is the brain read path, nothing near sponsor sends. API backward-compat is safe: no field renames/removals, response shape unchanged; for every agent whose owner has master access (all known current prod agents) the returned rows are identical, so round-the-clock agent pollers see no diff. Two residual risks to check before ship: (1) minor query-plan change from the id-subquery on the hot /api/v1/knowledge_records path — trivial at current data volume, and can be skipped for master owners by returning agent_scope directly; (2) any hypothetical prod agent already owned by a non-master user would see its (wrongly widened) results shrink to its true grants — that is the intended correction but worth a one-line prod query to confirm which agents have non-master owners before deploying. Regression spec must use DIFFERING ceilings and a different-domain owner grant, since the existing equal-ceiling spec masks the bug.

title: BrainExporter (download_brain MCP tool + brain resource) bypasses the brand wall entirely
description: BrainExporter#readable_records returns the full `organization.knowledge_records` unless an agent_slug is passed, and never consults BrandScope/api_brand_restriction. The REST endpoint (Api::V1::KnowledgeRecordsController#readable_scope, line 77) brand-scopes with `brand_scoped(...)`, but the MCP `download_brain` tool and the `kerrihq:///brain` resource — the exact same data via a different door — hand any key with `brain:read` the entire brain including full bodies. Additionally #counts (lines 89-103) reports org-wide record + CRM totals even in agent mode, and agent_slug is caller-chosen (a brand-restricted key can simply omit it). Today enforcement is dark (brand_enforcement flag off, flips in the brand-wall PR8), so this is a hole that must close before the flip, not a live leak.
failure_or_value: Once brand_enforcement flips: Benji's HFYI-restricted API key calls the download_brain MCP tool (requires only brain:read) and receives every S&W-boundary-adjacent, finance, and executive knowledge record with bodies — the entire wall defeated by one tool call, while /api/v1/knowledge_records correctly walls him.
fix_sketch: Give BrainExporter a `restricted_to_property:` kwarg. In DownloadBrainTool and BrainResource, resolve the caller's restriction the same way BaseController does (Current.api_key -> ApiPolicyContext#brand_restriction_in(Current.organization)) and pass it in. In #readable_records apply `base = base.where(property_id: restriction.id) if restriction` before the agent branch; make #counts and #serialize_domains count from the same walled base instead of raw organization.* when a restriction or agent scope is active. Add specs: property-bound key exports only its brand's records and counts.

verdict.reason: Re-read confirms every load-bearing claim. BrainExporter#readable_records (app/services/brain_exporter.rb:56-61) returns organization.knowledge_records with no brand/property filter; the only narrowing is caller-chosen agent_slug. Brain::DownloadBrainTool requires only brain:read and BrainResource passes no restriction; both are auto-registered (config/initializers/mcp.rb:16-17). rg confirms ZERO occurrences of brand_scoped/BrandScope/brand_restriction in app/tools or app/resources. The REST twin (Api::V1::KnowledgeRecordsController#readable_scope:77) DOES apply brand_scoped, so identical data diverges by transport. The MCP transport (lib/mcp/api_key_authenticated_transport.rb) authenticates brand-restricted credentials (ApiKey belongs_to :property; OAuth tokens bound to restricted users) and nothing downstream consults the restriction. knowledge_records.property_id exists and is indexed (db/schema.rb:1026,1046). Secondary claim also true: #counts (lines 89-103) and serialize_domains/sources/agents report org-wide totals even in agent mode. Concrete failing input: brand_enforcement=true, HFYI-restricted key with brain:read calls download_brain with no agent_slug and receives every record with bodies, while /api/v1/knowledge_records walls the same key. One nuance strengthens it: ApiPolicyContext gates only the key-property path on BrandScope.enforced?; the bound-user path (User#brand_restriction_in, user.rb:97-106) has no flag check, so if any membership already carries restricted_to_property the REST/MCP divergence is live pre-flip. No spec covers exporter brand behavior. Kept high (not critical) because on main today enforcement is dark and restricted memberships land with the wall PR stack, so it is a must-close-before-flip hole rather than a currently exploited leak.
verdict.ship_risk: Low blast radius and no client-email surface (pure read-path filtering; touches_client_email=false). The fix is additive: a restricted_to_property kwarg on BrainExporter plus a where(property_id:) filter; no API fields renamed or removed, so agent pollers are unaffected. Main risks: (1) the unbound org-wide KERRIHQ_AGENT_API_KEY must keep returning nil restriction (ApiPolicyContext already guarantees this; preserve that path in the tool/resource resolution and add a spec); (2) walling #counts changes reported totals for restricted/agent callers — intended, but any automation asserting org-wide counts would see smaller numbers; (3) coordination risk with the in-flight brand-wall worktree (~/Projects/kerrihq-rails-brand-wall) — MCP scoping may be planned in a later PR of that stack, so land this fix inside the stack before PR8 flips enforcement to avoid duplicate/conflicting implementations; (4) OAuth-token MCP callers (in-app copilot users) resolve restriction via the resource owner's membership — verify Brian/owner memberships stay unrestricted so their exports do not shrink.

title: API knowledge_records#update enforces no agent write grants and lets agents rewrite provenance
description: The `create` action checks `agent_scope_resolver.allowed?(action: :create, ...)` for an acting agent, but `update` performs no grant check at all: any key with brain:write can mutate title/body/summary/tags of every record its read scope covers (candidate, imported, AND stale — only canonical/superseded are blocked). Since read and update are separate verbs in PermissionGrant::ACTIONS, a read-only agent grant currently confers write. Worse, `record_params` permits `source_path`, `source_url`, and `citation`, and update only excludes status/kind/sensitivity — so an agent can rewrite an imported record's provenance (or change source_path and break the importer's (org, source_system, source_path) idempotency key, causing the next import push to create a duplicate record instead of refreshing the original). Also minor: with an acting agent, an invalid `sensitivity` param raises KeyError in SensitivityLevels.value → unrescued 500 instead of 400.
failure_or_value: Kerri's agent, granted read+create only, PATCHes /api/v1/knowledge_records/:id with agent_slug=kerri and body='<hallucinated fact>' on a stale imported record: succeeds, silently corrupting brain history with no grant covering update. Setting source_path='brain/wiki/other.md' detaches the record from its import identity; the next brain push re-creates the original path as a new record — duplicate truth.
fix_sketch: In #update: (1) mirror create's gate — `if acting_agent && !agent_scope_resolver.allowed?(action: :update, domain: record.domain, sensitivity: record.sensitivity, kind: record.kind, source_system: record.source_system, property: record.property)` render 403; (2) extend the except-list to provenance fields: `record_params.except(:status, :kind, :sensitivity, :source_path, :source_url, :content_hash)` (citation is arguably editable; source_path is not); (3) rescue KeyError in BaseController alongside ArgumentError → 400. All additive/restrictive, no field renames.

verdict.reason: Re-read confirms every claim. (1) knowledge_records_controller.rb#update (lines 58-70) has no agent_scope_resolver.allowed? gate, while #create (45-50) does; readable_scope narrows agents via PermissionResolver#readable_knowledge_scope which selects grants by the :read action only (permission_resolver.rb:53), and read/create/update are separate verbs in PermissionGrant::ACTIONS — so a read-only agent grant confers update on every candidate/imported/stale record its read scope covers (only canonical/superseded are blocked). (2) record_params permits source_path/source_url/citation and update excepts only status/kind/sensitivity (line 68), so an agent can move an imported record's source_path to any unused value; Kerrios::ImportService keys refresh on find_by(source_system:, source_path:) (import_service.rb:89-90), so the next push creates a duplicate record at the old path — duplicate truth in the brain. (3) Minor 500 confirmed: with acting_agent, an invalid sensitivity string hits SensitivityLevels.value → LEVELS.fetch → KeyError, which BaseController does not rescue (it rescues ArgumentError; KeyError < IndexError). Severity stays high: canonical records are protected, but the unguarded write path lets a hallucinating agent silently corrupt non-canonical brain content and break import idempotency — precisely what the grant architecture exists to prevent.
verdict.ship_risk: Low-to-moderate and purely restrictive. No client email involvement (touches_client_email=false) and no API field renames — response shapes are unchanged; only some previously-200 agent PATCHes become 403/400. The real risk: any existing agent flow (scheduled routine, Slack agent, importer glue) that currently PATCHes records via agent_slug without an explicit update-action PermissionGrant will start 403ing — audit prod PermissionGrants for Kerri/Oliver/Vaughn and add update grants where legitimately needed before deploying, or ship the grant gate behind a warn-then-enforce log first (matching the guard-warn pattern already used elsewhere). Excluding source_path from update-params could break a caller that legitimately re-paths records over the API — grep found none (the importer writes via the model, not the API), but verify agent-side scripts. Plain-key callers (no agent_slug) are unaffected by the grant gate; if source_path is also stripped for them, confirm no sync glue depends on it. The KeyError→400 rescue is strictly an improvement.

title: Agent-filed brain records are never brand-tagged (property_id always nil via the API)
description: KnowledgeRecord's own comment says property is 'nil only until the brand backfill runs; brand-restricted readers never see nil' — the fail-closed wall assumes every new record gets tagged. But the API create path (the main write path now that KerriOS is retired: Kerri/Oliver/Vaughn file candidates here around the clock) has no property param, no default, and no inference: every agent-filed record lands property_id nil forever. The backfill is a one-shot; the nil population regrows daily.
failure_or_value: Concrete value: when brand enforcement flips (PR8), every candidate Kerri filed since the backfill — including plainly Hardware-FYI facts — is invisible to Benji (HFYI-restricted), so the person meant to review HFYI brain candidates can't see them; meanwhile the promotion queue for Brian silently accumulates untagged rows. Fixing it keeps the wall's fail-closed invariant true continuously instead of only at backfill time.
