fix_sketch: Additive only: (1) permit an optional `property` slug in record_params, resolve via `Property.find_by!(slug:)`, and include it in the create attrs; (2) include `property:` in the agent grant check at line 45 so a property-scoped grant is honored; (3) default when absent: the key's api_brand_restriction if present, else the org's KMG/default property (same default the backfill used); (4) add `"property" => record.property&.slug` to serialize_record (additive field); (5) small recurring guard: a weekly job or QueueHealth check that counts property_id-nil knowledge_records created in the last 7 days and surfaces it, so regressions are visible.

verdict.reason: Re-read confirms every load-bearing claim. The API create path (api/v1/knowledge_records_controller.rb:52-55, record_params 99-101) has no property param, no default, no inference; KnowledgeRecord has no property-defaulting callback, unlike Event and Task which both have before_validation defaults — so BrandScope's own documented invariant ("new records default to KMG when brand can't be inferred", brand_scope.rb:17-19) is violated specifically on this model's main agent write path. brand_scoped (api/v1/base_controller.rb:91-94) does where(property_id => restriction.id), so nil rows are invisible to restricted readers once PlatformSetting.brand_enforcement flips. The backfill (lib/tasks/brand_backfill.rake) is a one-shot manual rake; its brand:enforce guard checks only nil-property DEALS, not knowledge_records, so the regrown nil population would not block the flip. Additionally there is NO remediation surface: neither the web form record_params (knowledge_records_controller.rb:233) nor API update permits property, and the only tagging path (AskSavant tool_executor ~873) tags only brand-restricted users' saves — Brian's master saves stay nil by design with no review tool to fix them. Fix is feasible and small: AgentScopeResolver#allowed? already accepts property: (agent_scope_resolver.rb:18), and serializer/param additions are purely additive. Kept high because enforcement flip is imminent (PR8 of the active brand-wall stack), agents file candidates around the clock, and the person meant to review HFYI candidates (Benji) would silently lose them all.
verdict.ship_risk: Low blast radius, no client-email involvement (touches_client_email=false), and fully additive API changes (new optional property param + new serialized "property" field; nothing renamed or removed, so 24/7 agent pollers are safe). Three real risks: (1) default choice — auto-tagging KMG on absent property matches the backfill rule and keeps fail-closed semantics, but KMG-tagged rows are equally invisible to restricted members, so genuinely-HFYI candidates still need the agent to pass the slug or a review surface to retag; the fix should include prompt/skill updates telling agents to send property. (2) Sketch correction: default via api_key.property directly, not api_brand_restriction — ApiPolicyContext only surfaces the key property when enforcement is already on, which would make the default silently vanish pre-flip. (3) Coordination: the brand-wall stacked PRs (#255+, worktree ~/Projects/kerrihq-rails-brand-wall) may already implement part of this; land it in that stack or rebase against it to avoid conflicting migrations/params. Passing property: into the agent grant check at controller line 45 could newly 403 a property-scoped grant that previously passed — verify existing agent grants before shipping.

title: Archived agent memories keep surfacing through the QMD index (and lookup is unscoped by org/active)
description: export_memory writes `entries/<id>.md` but nothing ever deletes a file: AgentMemory#archive! sets archived_at yet the markdown stays on disk and stays in the QMD index (export_organization only re-exports active memories; it never prunes). search() prefers the QMD result whenever it's non-empty, so an archived memory keeps ranking in results. serialize_qmd_row then does `AgentMemory.find_by(id: id)` with no organization scope and no active scope — it happily re-serializes the archived record (and, if a second org ever exists, another org's record, since @entries_dir is a single shared directory).
failure_or_value: Brian tells Kerri to forget a wrong operating rule; the copilot archives the AgentMemory row. Next `search_agent_memory` call still returns the archived rule via QMD (backend 'qmd'), and Kerri keeps following guidance that was explicitly retracted — the exact memory-poisoning failure MemoryPolicy exists to prevent.
fix_sketch: (1) In serialize_qmd_row, scope the lookup: `AgentMemory.active.find_by(id: id, organization_id: organization.id)` (pass organization into search_qmd) and return nil when not found so .compact drops it. (2) Add a forget!/archive path in the store that deletes entries/<id>.md and re-runs `qmd update`; call it wherever archive! is invoked. (3) In export_organization, prune files whose basename is not in the active id set. (4) Namespace entries per org (`entries/<org_id>/<id>.md`) for future multi-org safety.

verdict.reason: Every mechanical claim survives re-reading. (1) `export_memory` (app/services/agent_memory_store.rb:108-114) writes `entries/<id>.md` and nothing in the entire codebase deletes those files — no unlink/prune in the store, no cleanup job or rake task. (2) `export_organization` (:103-106) only re-exports `active` memories; it never removes files for archived/deleted ones. (3) `search` (:82-88) returns the QMD result whenever `memories` is non-empty, so the DB `.active` fallback never runs for hits that exist in the file corpus. (4) `serialize_qmd_row` (:235-247) does a bare `AgentMemory.find_by(id: id)` with no `active` scope and no organization scope, so an archived row is happily re-serialized; and if the row was hard-deleted (org `dependent: :destroy`, app/models/organization.rb:42) the fallback branch returns the stale file's title/snippet anyway — content survives even deletion. Concrete repro on the real path: archive any memory (`AgentMemory#archive!`, app/models/agent_memory.rb:41-43 — the model's sanctioned retraction mechanism, which every DB read path respects via `.active` at :75, :86, :93), then call the live `search_agent_memory` tool (app/services/ask_savant/tool_executor.rb:927-934) with matching keywords: the archived memory comes back with backend "qmd". One honest caveat that keeps this at medium rather than high: `archive!` currently has zero callers in app/lib — there is no agent "forget" tool or UI, so archiving today only happens via Rails console maintenance. The finding's narrative ("the copilot archives the row") overstates the trigger, but the inconsistency is real: the system's own retraction primitive is silently defeated by the QMD mirror, which is exactly the memory-poisoning failure the `.active` scoping elsewhere exists to prevent. The cross-org leak is also real code (shared `entries/` dir, unscoped lookup) but latent — single-org in practice, and the brand-walled path (:74-79) already bypasses QMD.
verdict.ship_risk: Low blast radius: AgentMemoryStore is internal-only — no client email anywhere near it (touches_client_email=false), no /api/v1 field renames (search result rows keep the same keys; archived rows simply stop appearing, which is the intended semantics). Two real risks in the sketched fix: (a) fix item 3 as written is dangerous multi-org — `export_organization(orgA)` pruning files not in org A's active id set would delete other orgs' files from the shared entries/ dir, so pruning must be org-aware (do item 4's per-org namespacing first, or prune only files whose frontmatter/DB row belongs to the pruning org); (b) scoping `find_by` to active+org means QMD hits for archived files return the file-based fallback hash (title/snippet, no id) instead of nil until the file is actually pruned — return nil explicitly so `.compact` drops them, and re-run `qmd update` after any deletion or stale index entries will error/miss. Also note `search` never runs `qmd update` today (only `remember!` does), so index refresh timing should be considered when adding the prune step.

title: AgentMemoryStore rewrites the entire markdown corpus on every search (O(N) disk writes per query)
description: search() (and status()) call export_organization, which `find_each`-loads every active AgentMemory and rewrites every `entries/<id>.md` plus the .qmd config file on EVERY call — even when nothing changed. export_memory also redundantly rewrites the config once per memory. AskSavant::ActiveMemoryPreflight runs a memory search before copilot turns, so each Ask Savant interaction pays N file writes + a full corpus rewrite on Render's disk before the actual QMD search even starts.
failure_or_value: Concrete value: with a few hundred memories this is hundreds of synchronous File.write calls per copilot turn / Slack agent memory lookup — pure latency and disk churn ahead of a phone-facing response. Making export incremental turns every agent memory search from O(N) writes to O(0), a direct speedup on the hottest agent path.
fix_sketch: Track an export watermark: store the max(updated_at)+count of active memories in a stamp file (e.g. `.qmd/export_stamp`); in export_organization, return early when the stamp matches the DB (`organization.agent_memories.active.pick(Arel.sql('max(updated_at), count(*)'))`). Only rewrite files for memories with updated_at > stamp (plus prune archived, per the other finding), then run `qmd update` once. Also lift write_qmd_config out of export_memory's per-record loop. remember! already exports the new record inline, so correctness is preserved.

verdict.reason: Re-read agent_memory_store.rb: search (line 82) and status (line 91) unconditionally call export_organization (lines 103-106), which find_each-loads every active AgentMemory and File.writes every entries/<id>.md; export_memory (line 112) additionally calls write_qmd_config per record, so .qmd/index.yml is rewritten N+1 times per search with zero dirty-checking. The path is hot: AskSavant::ActiveMemoryPreflight (line 24) runs this before every copilot turn (enabled by default per line 47), and ToolExecutor's memory_search (line 930) hits it too. Worse than claimed: the full export runs even when qmd is unavailable, then the result is discarded for the DB fallback. remember! already exports new records inline (line 56), so the incremental watermark fix preserves correctness. Not a correctness bug, but a real, feasible, low-blast-radius perf upgrade on the hottest agent path; actual latency today is likely tens of ms with a small corpus, growing linearly, so medium (not high) is right.
verdict.ship_risk: Low. Internal service only: no /api/v1 field changes, no DB schema changes (stamp lives in a file), and nothing near client email (touches_client_email=false). Main risks in the fix itself: (1) pruning archived memories' entry files could delete wrong files if not keyed strictly by id within entries/; (2) a stamp miss if any writer bypasses updated_at (update_column) — mitigate with a force-export fallback and full export on stamp-parse failure; (3) concurrent searches racing on the stamp file are benign (worst case one redundant export). Per-instance disk on Render keeps stamp and corpus co-located, so multi-instance is safe.

title: Add updated_since delta polling + property/last_verified_at fields to GET /api/v1/knowledge_records
description: Agents poll this endpoint around the clock (it is the canonical brain read per the session-startup contract), but the index supports only kind/status/domain/q/active filters — every sync pass re-pages the whole corpus with full bodies at 25-100/page under a 100 req/min rate limit. The serializer also omits three fields agents need: the brand tag (property), last_verified_at (verification recency for trust decisions), and the domain's human name.
failure_or_value: Concrete value: a `?updated_since=` filter lets Kerri/Oliver/Vaughn fetch only records changed since their last sync — typically one page instead of the full corpus — cutting scheduled-routine latency, rate-limit pressure, and Ollama context waste. Exposing `property` and `last_verified_at` lets agents answer 'is this HFYI or S&W?' and 'how fresh is this canonical fact?' without a per-record Savant UI lookup. All additive, safe under the never-rename rule.
fix_sketch: In #index add `scope = scope.where(updated_at: Time.iso8601(params[:updated_since])..) if params[:updated_since].present?` (Time.iso8601 raises ArgumentError → existing 400 rescue). In serialize_record, merge additive keys: `"property" => record.property&.slug, "last_verified_at" => record.last_verified_at, "active" => record.active?`. Optionally add a `fields=summary` param that drops body from the payload for cheap polling. Composite index on (organization_id, updated_at) if the corpus grows.

verdict.reason: Re-read the controller: #index (lines 19-28) supports only kind/status/domain/q/active — no updated_since anywhere in app/controllers — and serialize_record (lines 104-114) omits property, last_verified_at, and active even though the schema has property_id and last_verified_at and the model has active?/Property#slug. Agents genuinely poll this endpoint as the canonical brain read under a 100 req/min limit with 25-100/page pagination (base_controller lines 6, 127-135), so delta polling is a real, feasible, not-already-existing upgrade. The fix sketch works as written: rescue_from ArgumentError at base_controller line 30 turns bad Time.iso8601 input into the existing 400, and readable_scope already brand-scopes results so exposing the property slug leaks nothing.
verdict.ship_risk: Low. All changes are additive (new query param + new JSON keys), so no API backward-compat break for round-the-clock agent pollers, and nothing touches client email (touches_client_email=false). Two things to watch: (1) timestamp watermark sync can miss long-transaction writes whose updated_at predates the watermark — document an overlap-window convention for agents; (2) the broad rescue_from ArgumentError means any other ArgumentError in the action also 400s, which is pre-existing behavior but worth a targeted parse (Time.iso8601 in a begin/rescue) if precision matters. The (organization_id, updated_at) index is optional at current corpus size and safe to add concurrently later.

title: No dedup on agent candidate writes — repeated runs pile duplicate candidates into the promotion queue
description: POST /api/v1/knowledge_records creates unconditionally: content_hash is never computed for API writes and the (org, source_system, source_path) unique index doesn't apply because agents send no source_path. Scheduled agents (inbox sweep, Vaughn, memory mirroring via MemoryPolicy honor+mirror) re-derive the same durable fact across runs and file it again each time. The sibling store already solved this — AgentMemory has a content_hash unique constraint with a find-existing rescue, and create_task got dedup in PR #223 — but the brain candidate lane, which is the one a human must manually review, has none.
failure_or_value: Concrete value: Brian's /brain promotion queue is the human bottleneck (4 candidates already awaiting promotion per the ops notes; the June cleanup deduped operations 128→59 by hand). Hash-dedup at write time keeps the queue one-row-per-fact permanently, making 'promote candidates' a 30-second phone task instead of a periodic cleanup project.
fix_sketch: In #create, before create!: compute `hash = Digest::SHA256.hexdigest([title, body, kind].to_json)`; look up `current_organization.knowledge_records.where(content_hash: hash, status: ALLOWED_CREATE_STATUSES).first` and, when found, return it with 200 and an additive `"deduplicated": true` flag instead of creating (mirrors AgentMemoryStore#remember!'s RecordNotUnique path). Set content_hash on the created record otherwise. No schema change needed (column exists); optionally add a partial index on (organization_id, content_hash) WHERE status IN (0,1) — additive migration only.

verdict.reason: Every load-bearing claim re-checked and true. (1) app/controllers/api/v1/knowledge_records_controller.rb:52-55 calls create! unconditionally — no content_hash computed, no duplicate lookup; record_params (lines 99-101) doesn't even permit content_hash. (2) KnowledgeRecord (app/models/knowledge_record.rb) has NO content_hash callback and its only uniqueness validation is source_path scoped to (org, source_system) with allow_nil (line 61); the DB index (db/schema.rb:1044) is partial WHERE source_path IS NOT NULL, so agent writes that omit source_path are never deduped. (3) The content_hash column exists and is nullable (schema.rb:1016), so the sketched fix needs no destructive schema change. (4) The sibling AgentMemory store really did solve this: unique index on (organization_id, content_hash) (schema.rb:218), before_validation assign_content_hash (agent_memory.rb:51-53), and AgentMemoryStore#remember! rescues RecordNotUnique and returns the existing row (agent_memory_store.rb:60-63). (5) The finding actually understates the gap: the in-app copilot's remember_brain path (ask_savant/tool_executor.rb:873-891) sets source_path to a timestamp+SecureRandom.hex(4) value (line 2789-2792), so even the source-identity unique index can never fire there — every re-derived fact from Ask Savant/Slack files a fresh candidate too. Both the API lane and the copilot lane pile duplicates into the human-reviewed promotion queue, which matches the ops reality (manual 128→59 brain cleanup, candidates awaiting promotion). Confirmed as a real, feasible, not-already-existing upgrade.
verdict.ship_risk: Low, with three design nuances to get right. (a) API behavior change: a duplicate POST would return 200 + existing record instead of 201 + new record — agents polling /api/v1 get a valid record with an id either way, and the "deduplicated": true flag is purely additive; no field renames, no column drops. (b) Hash scope: hashing only [title, body, kind] would collapse identical content filed under two different domains — include domain_id (or scope the lookup by domain) to avoid cross-domain false dedup; also #update (controller line 68) lets agents change body, so content_hash must be recomputed on update (a before_validation callback like AgentMemory's is safer than controller-only assignment) or lookups will match stale hashes. (c) Race safety: a pure check-then-create is racy under concurrent agent runs; the proposed partial unique index on (organization_id, content_hash) WHERE status IN (0,1) plus a RecordNotUnique rescue (mirroring AgentMemoryStore) closes it — additive migration only, but backfill must handle existing NULL content_hash rows and any pre-existing duplicate candidates before the index will apply. No client-email surface touched (touches_client_email=false is correct). Existing test suite risk is minimal: controller create specs asserting 201 for repeat posts, if any, would need updating intentionally.

title: SafeHttp SSRF guard bypassed by IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses (metadata endpoint reachable)
description: BLOCKED_RANGES contains IPv4 CIDRs (127.0.0.0/8, 169.254.0.0/16, 10.0.0.0/8, ...) and IPv6 CIDRs (::1, fc00::/7), but nothing matches IPv4-mapped IPv6 literals like ::ffff:169.254.169.254. IPAddr range.include? does NOT match a mapped address against the plain IPv4 range, so blocked?() returns false and check!/validation_error pass. resolve() happily builds an IPAddr from such a host literal. This guard is the SSRF wall for agent-registered connectors (RestApiClient, GenericMcpClient) and Kerri can be steered by untrusted email/Slack content into registering/calling a URL.
failure_or_value: An agent-registered rest_api or MCP connector with endpoint https://[::ffff:169.254.169.254]/latest/meta-data/ (or https://[::ffff:127.0.0.1]:6379/) passes SafeHttp.check!, then Faraday/OS routes ::ffff:169.254.169.254 to the IPv4 cloud metadata service (169.254.169.254 on AWS/GCP/Render) or ::ffff:127.0.0.1 to loopback services. Verified in Ruby: all blocked IPv4 ranges return include?==false for the ::ffff:* forms, so the guard admits them.
fix_sketch: In blocked?(ip) normalize first: ip = ip.ipv4_mapped? ? ip.native : ip (also guard ipv4_compat?) before the range check; additionally add IPAddr.new("::ffff:0:0/96") to BLOCKED_RANGES as defense in depth. Verified: after ip.ipv4_mapped? ? ip.native : ip, ::ffff:169.254.169.254 -> 169.254.169.254 and matches 169.254.0.0/16. Apply the same normalization in resolve() output so hostnames resolving to mapped AAAA are caught too.

verdict.reason: Re-ran the exact resolve()/blocked?/BLOCKED_RANGES logic from app/services/safe_http.rb. IPAddr.new("::ffff:169.254.169.254") parses (ipv4_mapped?==true); IPAddr.new("169.254.0.0/16").include?(mapped)==false and 127.0.0.0/8.include?(::ffff:127.0.0.1)==false, so blocked? returns false and validation_error/check! pass. Confirmed end-to-end: for endpoint_url https://[::ffff:169.254.169.254]/latest/meta-data/ and https://[::ffff:127.0.0.1]:6379/, resolve(uri.host) yields the mapped IPAddr and 'any blocked?' is false. The finding's aside that bracketed uri.host might fail to parse is wrong (IPAddr strips brackets and parses), but that error only reinforces the bypass. SafeHttp.check! is the live guard on RestApiClient#call (rest_api_client.rb:32, Faraday then connects to the same URL) and GenericMcpClient (generic_mcp_client.rb:52), and validation_error guards registration (agent_connector.rb:66) — exactly the modeled agent-steered-SSRF threat. Fix verified: ip.ipv4_mapped? ? ip.native : ip converts to 169.254.169.254 which matches 169.254.0.0/16.
verdict.ship_risk: Low. Fix is additive defense inside blocked?() (normalize ipv4_mapped/compat to native before range check) — no API field renamed/removed, no DB schema change, no sponsor/client-email surface touched (touches_client_email=false). Prefer normalize-then-check over only adding ::ffff:0:0/96 as a blanket block, so a legitimately public host expressed in mapped form is evaluated against real ranges rather than hard-denied; also apply the same normalization to each address from resolve() so hostnames resolving to mapped AAAA are caught. No backward-compat risk to agents polling /api/v1.

title: SafeHttp validates a resolved IP but Faraday re-resolves and connects (DNS-rebinding TOCTOU)
description: SafeHttp.check! resolves the host and validates the IP, then RestApiClient/GenericMcpClient hand the original hostname URL to Faraday, which resolves DNS again at connect time. An attacker who controls the connector's DNS can return a public IP for the validation lookup and a private IP (127.0.0.1 / 169.254.169.254) for the actual connection. The file comment acknowledges this only 'closes most of the gap.' Connectors are attacker-influenced (email/Slack steer).
failure_or_value: A malicious connector host with 1s TTL DNS answers public on the validation resolve, then flips to 169.254.169.254 before Faraday connects, reaching internal/metadata services despite the guard. Closing this removes the residual SSRF path that the mapped-IPv6 fix alone doesn't cover.
fix_sketch: Have SafeHttp.check! return the validated IP, then connect to that IP directly while sending the original Host header (and SNI) — e.g. resolve once, build the Faraday URL against the pinned IP, or install a custom resolver/socket that pins the checked address. Alternatively re-validate inside a Faraday middleware using the socket's actual peer address.

verdict.reason: Re-reading the real code confirms the TOCTOU exists: SafeHttp.check! (safe_http.rb:38-43) resolves+validates via Resolv.getaddresses then returns the original hostname URL (line 42); RestApiClient#call (rest_api_client.rb:31-34) and GenericMcpClient#raw (generic_mcp_client.rb:52-53) hand that hostname to Faraday, which re-resolves via Net::HTTP at connect with no shared cache and no pinned IP. Concrete exploit: authoritative DNS with ~1s TTL answers a public IP on the validation lookup and 169.254.169.254/127.0.0.1 on the connect lookup. The file comment at safe_http.rb:9-10 already concedes it only 'closes most of the gap.' It's real and not already fixed. Downgraded from confirmed to plausible because the finding understates a strong mitigation: per agent_connector.rb:6-7,63-68 a connector is validated at registration and is unusable until Brian (a human) approves it (scope :usable -> approved), and registration is gated in AskSavant — so the primary SSRF control is human approval, making this residual TOCTOU defense-in-depth with low exploit likelihood (requires Brian to approve an attacker-DNS-controlled domain, then rebind).
verdict.ship_risk: No client-email exposure and no API/schema backward-compat concern (touches_client_email=false; purely internal SSRF hardening). The real risk is agent reliability: the fix_sketch's 'pin the validated IP' approach can break legitimate connectors, since most SaaS MCP/REST endpoints sit behind CDNs/load balancers with rotating IP sets and Host/SNI-based virtual routing — connecting to a single stale or rotated-out pinned IP causes intermittent connection/TLS-cert failures for agents that poll around the clock. Lower-risk implementation is a Faraday/Net::HTTP middleware that re-checks the socket's actual peer IP against BLOCKED_RANGES after connect (fail-closed) rather than statically pinning one resolved address. Must preserve https+SNI and reuse the same BLOCKED_RANGES so behavior stays consistent with registration-time validation.

title: CompanyEnrichmentJob calls Apollo find_sponsor_contacts uncached, spending up to ~30 email-reveal credits per company every run
description: The AskSavant tool path wraps Apollo in Apollo::Cache (tool_executor.rb:2229/2243), but CompanyEnrichmentJob.find_contacts calls ApolloClient.find_sponsor_contacts directly with no cache. find_sponsor_contacts fans out across all 6 SPONSOR_CONTACT_STRATEGIES, each revealing up to 5 matches via bulk_match with reveal_personal_emails: true (apollo_client.rb:353) — up to ~30 metered personal-email reveals per company. Every re-enrich (perform(reenrich: true)) and every batched enqueue re-spends the full credit cost, and there is no per-run credit ceiling or spend telemetry.
failure_or_value: Re-enriching a sponsor pipeline of N companies burns ~N x (company enrich + up to 30 contact reveals) Apollo credits each pass, with no dedupe against a recent identical pull. Wiring the existing Apollo::Cache in (as the tool path already does) makes re-enrich and near-duplicate enqueues free within the TTL window, and a spend counter gives Brian visibility the memory note ('do not loop Apollo across many companies') currently relies on prompt discipline to enforce.
fix_sketch: In company_enrichment_job.rb wrap both calls in Apollo::Cache.fetch (company + sponsor_contacts:limit keys, same as tool_executor.rb:2229/2243). Add a lightweight per-job/day credit budget check before find_sponsor_contacts and emit a metric/log of reveal count so batch runs are observable.

verdict.reason: Every cited line checks out. company_enrichment_job.rb:76/:90 call ApolloClient.enrich_company_info and find_sponsor_contacts directly with no Apollo::Cache, while the AskSavant tool path wraps the identical calls (tool_executor.rb:2229-2231 and 2243-2245) using a cache module (app/services/apollo/cache.rb) built exactly for this metered-API dedupe. find_sponsor_contacts runs all 6 SPONSOR_CONTACT_STRATEGIES unconditionally (apollo_client.rb:43-74, 218), each revealing up to 5 email-bearing matches via bulk_match with reveal_personal_emails: true (apollo_client.rb:323-325, 353) — up to ~30 reveal requests plus 6 searches per run, and since dedup happens after per-strategy reveals, the same person can even be revealed twice in one run. The job fires uncached on every Company creation (Enrichable after_create_commit) and every reenrich! (company.rb:86-92, DealsController#reenrich), with no recency guard, credit budget, or spend telemetry. Severity trimmed from high to medium because volume is low (manual re-enrich, small team, lookalikes create suggestions not Companies) and Apollo generally does not re-charge for already-unlocked contacts, so repeat runs waste requests/quota more than guaranteed credits. Still a real, feasible, not-yet-existing upgrade with the pattern already proven in tool_executor.
verdict.ship_risk: Low blast radius, but two implementation traps: (1) caching find_sponsor_contacts on the reenrich: true path would make the Re-enrich button (whose documented purpose is "find additional contacts") a silent no-op for the 14-day TTL — the fix must bypass or refresh the contacts cache on reenrich while still writing the fresh result for cross-path reuse; (2) cache keys embed the limit ("sponsor_contacts:#{limit}") and the job uses limit 10 while the tool defaults to 5, so cross-path hits require key normalization or caching the un-truncated pool. No client-email exposure: Apollo enrichment is internal, the generated outreach_sequence is stored on deals, never sent. No /api/v1 field or DB schema changes needed — caching and a spend log are purely internal and additive. Slightly-stale contact rosters within the TTL are already the accepted tradeoff on the tool path, and cached contact payloads (personal emails) land in the same Solid Cache store the tool path already uses.

title: Apollo 429 retry ignores Retry-After and blocks a Puma thread with a fixed sleep
description: make_request rescues RateLimitError and retries up to 2 times with a hard-coded sleep(1), ignoring Apollo's Retry-After header, using no backoff/jitter, and holding the thread. Apollo tools run synchronously inside AskSavant request handling (apollo_find_contacts/apollo_find_sponsor_contacts), so this blocks a web worker thread and typically under-waits a real rate-limit window, causing the retry to 429 again and surface as a failed lookup.
failure_or_value: Under Apollo rate limiting, a single apollo_find_sponsor_contacts fans out to 6+ requests; each 429 sleeps exactly 1s x2 then fails, tying up the Puma thread for seconds and returning 'Rate limit exceeded' to Brian on his phone even though a slightly longer wait would have succeeded. On a shared key, concurrent agent runs amplify this.
fix_sketch: Read response.headers['retry-after'] (seconds or HTTP-date), clamp to a sane max (e.g. 10s), add exponential backoff + jitter across the retries, and raise attempts modestly. Longer-term, run Apollo lookups in a background job rather than inline in the request path.

verdict.reason: Re-read confirms every element: apollo_client.rb:449-461 retries RateLimitError with a hard-coded sleep(1) x2 and no backoff/jitter; the 429 branch (lines 500-502) raises without capturing response.headers, so Retry-After / Apollo's x-minute-requests-left can never inform the wait; Apollo limits are per-minute so a 1s wait inside an exhausted window predictably 429s again. The synchronous-path claim holds: ask_savant_controller.rb:22 runs AskSavant::Agent#respond inline, and tool_executor.rb:2205/2222 call ApolloClient directly, so sleeps land on a Puma thread during Brian's copilot request. Fan-out is real and slightly worse than stated: find_sponsor_contacts runs 6 strategies x (search + bulk_match reveal) = up to 12 requests, worst case ~12s of pure sleep in-request. Minor wording correction: the sponsor tool degrades silently to empty results (execute_sponsor_contact_search rescues Error and returns [] per strategy), while apollo_find_contacts is the path that surfaces the literal "Rate limit exceeded" error string to Brian. Apollo::Cache mitigates frequency but not cache-miss behavior, and shared-key background jobs (prospect discovery, ticket search) can push the interactive path into the limit. Concrete failing input: Apollo key at its per-minute cap + one apollo_find_contacts call → 429, sleep 1, 429, sleep 1, 429 → tool error to Brian with ~2s+3 round trips of held web thread.
verdict.ship_risk: Low. The fix is client-side retry policy only: no /api/v1 field changes, no schema changes, and zero proximity to sponsor/client email (Apollo tools are read/enrich only; the client-email ban is untouched, touches_client_email=false). Two real hazards in the fix itself: (1) honoring a large Retry-After inline would hold the Puma thread LONGER than today, so the in-request clamp must stay small (~3-5s total budget on the web path; longer backoff only in background-job contexts, or move Apollo lookups to a job); (2) the existing spec at spec/services/apollo_client_spec.rb:307 exercises the 429 path and currently absorbs the two fixed sleeps — retry-logic changes must stub sleep and update that spec or the suite slows/breaks. Behavior change is strictly additive reliability: worst case is slightly longer tool latency under rate limiting in exchange for fewer failed lookups.

title: Render rollback (the canary dead-man lever) is a single POST with no retry — a transient blip strands bad code live
description: RenderClient#rollback! issues one Net::HTTP POST (30s read timeout, no retry). SelfUpgradeCanaryJob#roll_back! invokes it when the agent degrades after a self-upgrade; on any RenderClient::Error it records 'rollback_failed' and freezes the pipeline but does NOT retry. Because rollback is the safety mechanism that restores the pre-upgrade image, a single transient network error / Render 5xx at exactly the moment degradation is detected leaves the bad deploy serving on both web and worker.
failure_or_value: Canary detects a degraded agent, calls rollback!, the Render API returns a transient 502 or the connection times out once -> result is 'rollback_failed', self-upgrades freeze, but the broken code stays live on all services until a human intervenes. A couple of retries would have recovered automatically.
fix_sketch: Wrap rollback! (and ideally deploys reads it depends on) in a small retry loop: 3 attempts with exponential backoff on Net::OpenTimeout/Net::ReadTimeout/5xx before raising. Consider verifying the resulting live deploy afterward (poll live_deploy) so a silent no-op rollback is caught.

verdict.reason: Re-read confirms every claim: RenderClient#request (app/services/render_client.rb:77-86) is one Net::HTTP call with no retry, and SelfUpgradeCanaryJob#roll_back! (app/jobs/self_upgrade_canary_job.rb:100-120) treats a single RenderClient::Error as terminal "rollback_failed" — a transient Render 5xx at the degradation moment strands the bad deploy live (though an urgent owner task IS filed, so it's alarmed, not silent). The code is worse than the finding states: raw Net::OpenTimeout/ReadTimeout/ECONNRESET are never wrapped in RenderClient::Error, so a plain connection timeout during roll_back! escapes both the line-110 rescue and perform's rescues, kills the job (ApplicationJob has no retry_on; Solid Queue doesn't auto-retry), and leaves NO rollback, NO pipeline freeze, NO owner notification, and the upgrade stuck in canary with no requeue. The same hole strands the ordinary canary loop via deploy_for_commit at perform line 27, defeating the explicit "hiccups must not strand the canary" rescue at line 67. The GitHub watchdog only covers total app death, not this. Upgrade is real, feasible, high-value, does not exist.
verdict.ship_risk: Low. Fix is confined to RenderClient (wrap network exceptions in RenderClient::Error + 3-attempt backoff on timeout/5xx), referenced only by the canary job and its spec — no /api/v1 field changes, no DB schema change, no client-email surface (touches_client_email=false). Two watch items: (1) retrying the rollback POST after a response-read timeout could issue a duplicate rollback request; Render rollback-to-deployId is effectively idempotent (worst case a redundant deploy of the same image), acceptable for a dead-man lever; (2) wrapping timeouts changes perform's behavior so timeouts requeue instead of killing the job — desired, but spec/jobs/self_upgrade_canary_job_spec.rb must be updated and the green suite re-run to prove no regression.

title: MCP token pre-refresh fails open when expires_at is missing/malformed, defeating proactive refresh
description: token_expiring?(credentials) parses Time.iso8601(credentials['expires_at']) and rescues ArgumentError by returning false — i.e. treats a token with a blank or unparseable expires_at as 'not expiring', so bearer_token/access_token never proactively refresh it. The clients then rely solely on the reactive 401-retry path. If token_payload stored no expires_at (OAuth response omitted expires_in) the client always sends a stale/expired token first, doubling every call into a guaranteed 401 + refresh + retry.
failure_or_value: When Superhuman/Reclaim returns a token without expires_in (so expires_at is nil), every MCP call issues one doomed request, refreshes, and retries — extra latency on Brian-facing Superhuman/Reclaim tool calls and needless refresh churn; and if the reactive refresh path ever regresses, calls fail outright with no proactive safety net.
fix_sketch: In token_expiring? rescue ArgumentError -> return true (treat unknown expiry as expiring, forcing a refresh) rather than false; missing-expiry should refresh, not skip.

verdict.reason: The code does exactly what the finding says: token_expiring? in superhuman_mcp_client.rb:144-149 and reclaim_mcp_client.rb:135-140 rescues ArgumentError to false, so a nil/malformed expires_at disables proactive refresh; and the nil state is reachable because both OAuth clients (superhuman_oauth_client.rb:103, reclaim_oauth_client.rb:86) deliberately store expires_at: nil when the token response omits expires_in. However, the impact is overstated: the reactive 401-refresh-retry path fully preserves correctness, and the penalty is one extra round-trip per token-expiry window (the refreshed token is persisted and reused), not a doubling of every call. The triggering condition — Superhuman/Reclaim omitting expires_in — is hypothetical with no evidence it occurs, so this is a low-value resilience gap rather than a confirmed bug.
verdict.ship_risk: The proposed fix (rescue ArgumentError → true) is riskier than the bug: when expires_at is persistently nil (refresh re-stores nil), every MCP request would trigger a token refresh before the call — a refresh storm that adds latency to every Brian-facing Superhuman/Reclaim tool call, and if either provider rotates refresh tokens, concurrent per-call refreshes could invalidate the stored refresh token and mark the IntegrationConnection errored, hard-breaking the integration until Brian re-does OAuth. Safer fix: synthesize a default expires_at (e.g. 55 minutes from now) in token_payload when expires_in is absent. No client-email exposure (these are internal MCP tool clients, no sends) and no /api/v1 field or DB schema changes needed.

title: Contract flow 500s end-to-end for deals without an event (newsletter deals)
description: Contract.rb:7-9 explicitly documents that newsletter-sponsorship contracts have no event (belongs_to :event, optional: true), and Deal.belongs_to :event is also optional. But every step of the native contract flow dereferences the event unconditionally: ContractsController#new calls ContractTemplate.for_event(@event) whose scope does event.id (contract_template.rb:15) and builds the title with @event.name (contracts_controller.rb:26); ContractRenderer#variables calls @deal.event.name/.location_display/.end_date (contract_renderer.rb:23-30); AccountManagementMailer#contract_signing_request puts @event.name in the subject (line 14) and contract_from_options calls @event.contract_from_email (line 123).
failure_or_value: Open 'New contract' on any deal that has no event (the newsletter pipeline, an increasing share of HWFYI revenue): NoMethodError on nil at contract_template.rb:15 -> 500 page. Even a contract created another way and sent for signing crashes SendContractForSigningJob inside the mailer (nil.name / nil.contract_from_email), so the send silently never leaves and the contract is reverted to draft by the job's rescue. The only working path today for newsletter deals is upload_external. Native e-sign is dead for a whole deal class.
fix_sketch: Nil-safe the event everywhere: (1) contract_template.rb for_event -> ->(event) { event ? where(event_id: [event.id, nil]) : where(event_id: nil) }; (2) contracts_controller.rb#new title fallback "#{@deal.company.name} - #{@deal.name} Sponsorship Agreement" when @event.nil?; (3) contract_renderer.rb guard @deal.event with a safe navigation + 'TBD' fallbacks (format_date_range already handles missing dates; add event_name fallback to @deal.name); (4) mailer: subject falls back to contract.title when @event.nil?, and contract_from_options returns {} when @event.nil? (MailboxMailDelivery already falls back to info@hardwarefyi.com). Add a request spec creating+sending a contract on an event-less deal.

verdict.reason: Every cited deref verified on re-read. ContractTemplate.for_event does event.id unguarded (contract_template.rb:15) and ContractsController#new passes @deal.event (nil for newsletter deals) at contracts_controller.rb:19-20, so clicking any "+ NEW CONTRACT" link on an event-less sponsorship deal 500s; the deal show view (deals/show.html.erb:4,464) proves the event-less case is UI-reachable and even nil-guards the same scope itself, confirming the gap is real, not hypothetical. ContractRenderer dereferences @deal.event.name/.location_display/.end_date (contract_renderer.rb:23,25,30), and AccountManagementMailer uses @event.name in the subject (line 14) plus @event.contract_from_email in contract_from_options (line 123), which is called by ALL six mailer actions, so send_for_signing, signed-confirmation, and fully-executed mails all crash for event-less contracts; SendContractForSigningJob's rescue then reverts to draft and re-raises. Contract.rb:7-10 explicitly documents newsletter contracts have no event. Only minor overstatement: the job failure is visible in the job backend, not fully silent, but the user-facing flash still falsely says the contract is being sent. Native e-sign is genuinely dead for the newsletter deal class; only upload_external works.
verdict.ship_risk: Low blast radius: fix is nil-guards plus fallbacks, purely additive, no API fields or schema touched, and event-ful deals keep identical behavior. touches_client_email=true in the sense that AccountManagementMailer is a client-facing signing email, but it is the sanctioned contract e-sign path (not the banned SponsorPortalMailer/asset surface) and the fix adds no new send trigger; sends stay gated behind the explicit send_for_signing action, draft guard, and company-email presence check. Residual risks to verify before ship: (1) subject falls back sensibly (contract.title) so newsletter sponsors do not get a malformed subject; (2) contract_from_options returning {} must actually fall through to a sane default from-address in MailboxMailDelivery, confirm the info@hardwarefyi.com fallback claim in that class; (3) fixing the crash converts previously-failing sends into real outbound client emails, so any queued/retried SendContractForSigningJob for an event-less contract could fire after deploy, check the queue for stuck jobs first. Add the request spec for create+send on an event-less deal as proposed.

title: Persist the fully-executed PDF in Postgres and stop regenerating it with headless Chrome on every download
description: Contract.rb:21-26 admits the signed_document ActiveStorage blob is wiped on every Render deploy (local disk, no volume), so the legally-executed PDF exists only as a regenerable Ferrum render plus whatever landed in the email. Both download endpoints (contracts_controller.rb:118-134 and the sponsor-facing contract_signing_controller.rb:113-136, linked from the fully-executed email) boot a full headless Chrome per request: 2-6s latency and hundreds of MB of RSS on the web instance, worst on Brian's phone. Meanwhile ContractDocument already solves durable Postgres PDF storage for externally-signed contracts, but validates contract_id uniqueness so it can't hold the natively-executed artifact today.
failure_or_value: Value: (1) a byte-stable, sha256-stamped legal artifact that is guaranteed identical to what was emailed to the sponsor and survives deploys; (2) instant PDF downloads (send_data from Postgres) instead of a Chrome cold-start per tap, removing the single heaviest request on the web dyno; (3) removes the current audit gap where a code/CSS change to contracts/_pdf.html.erb silently changes the 'signed' PDF that later downloads produce.
fix_sketch: Additive migration: add kind (string, default 'external_upload') to contract_documents and replace the model's contract_id uniqueness validation with uniqueness scoped to kind (validation change only, no column drop). In SendFullyExecutedContractEmailJob#perform after generate_and_attach!, upsert ContractDocument.from_bytes(pdf_data, filename: ..., content_type: 'application/pdf') with kind: 'executed_render', and stamp contract.document_hash-adjacent sha256 there. Both download_pdf actions: if a ContractDocument exists for the contract, send_data its bytes; fall back to ContractPdfGenerator only when absent. Keeps API additive; no client-email behavior change (same attachment, now byte-stable).

verdict.reason: Every cited fact checks out on re-read: contract.rb:21-26 admits signed_document is an ephemeral regenerable cache wiped on deploy; both download endpoints (contracts_controller.rb:118-134, contract_signing_controller.rb:113-136) boot a fresh Ferrum headless Chrome per request via ContractPdfGenerator (contract_pdf_generator.rb:12-29) with no durable-copy check; the sponsor fully-executed email links to the token download URL so sponsor taps hit the Chrome path; document_hash covers only the body (contract.rb:89-91) so a contracts/_pdf.html.erb change silently alters the "signed" PDF later downloads produce; and ContractDocument (contract_document.rb:23 plus unique DB index at schema.rb:652) already solves durable Postgres PDF storage but its contract_id uniqueness blocks holding the natively-executed render. The upgrade is real, does not already exist (external_document at contracts_controller.rb:275-289 only covers externally-uploaded contracts), and the fix sketch is feasible and additive. High severity is justified: legal-artifact durability plus removing the heaviest request on the web dyno.
verdict.ship_risk: Medium, manageable. (1) API compat: the agent-polled "uploaded_document" field (api/v1/deals/contracts_controller.rb:141-149) and every existing lookup (Contract#uploaded_document?/uploaded_document_metadata, has_one :uploaded_document, contracts_controller.rb:278, deals_controller.rb:93, api contracts_controller.rb:67) currently mean "external upload"; without scoping them to kind='external_upload' in the same PR, new executed_render rows silently change that field's semantics for agents. No field renames needed. (2) Migration must also swap the unique DB index on contract_documents.contract_id (schema.rb:652) to unique(contract_id, kind) alongside the validation change; additive, no column drops. (3) Client email: no new sends are introduced; the fully-executed sponsor email is an existing signing-triggered transactional send (not the banned asset/chase/portal class). Keep attach_signed_pdf behavior untouched in the first pass so email content and triggers are byte-for-byte unchanged; only downloads switch to send_data-from-Postgres with the ContractPdfGenerator fallback retained for pre-execution previews.

title: Nil-deal crash across the post-signing pipeline for event_sponsor-only contracts
description: Contract validates deal OR event_sponsor (contract.rb:119-123), so contract.deal can legitimately be nil during the EventSponsor migration window. But the whole post-signing pipeline assumes a deal: GenerateDeliverablesJob does contract.deal.deliverables (line 8-10, enqueued unconditionally at contract_signing_controller.rb:73), SendFullyExecutedContractEmailJob does contract.deal.move_to_stage!(:closed_won) (line 27), and both admin-notification mailers build organization_deal_contract_url(org, contract.deal, contract) which raises UrlGenerationError when deal is nil (mailer lines 48-51 and 83-86).
failure_or_value: A sponsor signs a legacy event_sponsor contract: GenerateDeliverablesJob raises NoMethodError forever; contract_signed_notification (admin email) fails in the mailer job so the team is never told; on countersign, SendFullyExecutedContractEmailJob crashes at line 27 AFTER the sponsor/internal emails are enqueued, landing in the scary 'do NOT re-run this job' rescue branch (lines 28-43) and leaving a permanently failed job whose repair message references a deal that does not exist.
fix_sketch: Guard each: GenerateDeliverablesJob#perform: return if contract.deal.nil? (there are no sponsorship_selections without a deal anyway). SendFullyExecutedContractEmailJob:27: contract.deal&.move_to_stage!(:closed_won). Mailer: build @contract_url only when contract.deal.present?, else link the deal-less contract via the event_sponsor page or omit the button in the view (views already render @contract_url unconditionally, so wrap in if @contract_url). Add a spec signing a contract whose deal is nil.

verdict.reason: The cited code would crash on a nil deal exactly as described (generate_deliverables_job.rb:8, send_fully_executed_contract_email_job.rb:27, account_management_mailer.rb:48/83), but the finding's premise that deal-nil contracts 'legitimately exist during the migration window' no longer holds. The Phase 3 backfill (db/migrate/20260610100300_backfill_deals_from_event_sponsors.rb) re-pointed every event_sponsor contract to a deal with a raise-on-mismatch parity check, all current creation paths (contracts_controller.rb and api/v1/deals/contracts_controller.rb) build contracts via @deal.contracts.new, no app code creates EventSponsors or event_sponsor-only contracts anymore, and Deal has_many :contracts dependent: :destroy prevents orphaning. No concrete input on a real code path reaches the crash; it requires console-crafted data or a migration rollback. Downgraded to a latent-inconsistency hardening item (guard the four sites or tighten the requires_pipeline_record validation to require deal now that the window is closed), not a confirmed bug.
verdict.ship_risk: Low. The sketched fixes are nil-guards plus skipping the admin-notification URL when deal is absent: no client-facing email is added or re-enabled (contract_signed_notification and contract_fully_executed_notification go to org admins only; the sponsor emails are transactional signing confirmations already permitted), no /api/v1 field changes, no schema changes. Main watch-outs: (1) contract.deal&.move_to_stage! silently skips closed_won for a deal-less contract, acceptable since none should exist; (2) if the fix instead tightens the validation to require deal, confirm zero deal-nil contract rows in prod first, or existing rows would fail future saves; (3) wrapping @contract_url in the mailer views must not accidentally suppress the button for normal deal-backed contracts.

title: document_hash stamped at signing does not match the body actually stored (sign-date substitution happens after hashing)
description: In ContractSigningController#create the update! at lines 48-59 passes document_hash: @contract.compute_document_hash (SHA256 of the CURRENT body, still containing '[Signing Date]') and, in the same hash, body: @contract.body.gsub(SIGN_DATE_PLACEHOLDER, date). Both arguments are evaluated before assignment, so the persisted document_hash is the digest of the pre-substitution body while the persisted body is the substituted one. The hash is the tamper-evidence record for the signing ceremony, and it provably does not verify against the stored document. Countersigning later recomputes the hash over the substituted body (contracts_controller.rb:167), silently overwriting the signer-ceremony hash, so the mismatch self-heals in a way that destroys the original evidence.
failure_or_value: For any contract signed but not yet countersigned (or where countersign happens days later), Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(contract.body) != contract.document_hash. If Don or a counterparty ever audits 'this hash proves what the sponsor signed', the verification fails; after countersign the hash matches a body the sponsor technically never saw hashed. Legal-audit integrity defect, zero-cost to hit.
fix_sketch: Compute the final body first, hash that, and consider preserving both ceremony hashes: signed_body = @contract.body.gsub(ContractRenderer::SIGN_DATE_PLACEHOLDER, signed_at.strftime('%-m/%-d/%y')); @contract.update!(..., body: signed_body, document_hash: Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(signed_body)). Optionally also write the hash into the contract_signed activity metadata so the countersign overwrite at contracts_controller.rb:167 no longer erases the signing-time evidence. Backfill note: existing signed-not-countersigned rows can be re-stamped with a data migration.

verdict.reason: Re-read confirms every element. In ContractSigningController#create (lines 48-59), document_hash is computed via compute_document_hash (SHA256 of the current, with_lock-reloaded body still containing the literal '[Signing Date]' placeholder) while the body argument in the same update! is the sign-date-substituted string; Ruby evaluates both before assignment, so the persisted hash digests a body that is never stored. The placeholder genuinely reaches production bodies: ContractRenderer maps the {{ contract_sign_date }} merge field (advertised in the template-editor UI at contract_templates/_form.html.erb:31) to '[Signing Date]', and contracts_controller.rb:33-37/54-58 persist the rendered output as contract.body. Worse than the finding states, the signed PDF footer prints this hash (app/views/contracts/_pdf.html.erb:148), so the sponsor's tamper-evidence PDF contains a hash that fails verification against its own document text. Countersign (contracts_controller.rb:159-168) then recomputes the hash over the substituted body, silently overwriting the ceremony hash and destroying the original evidence. Concrete failing input: any contract created from a template using {{ contract_sign_date }} and signed by the sponsor; Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(contract.body) != contract.document_hash until countersign. Specs only assert hash presence (contract_signing_spec.rb:75), so the green suite does not contradict this. Kept at medium: no functional breakage or data loss, but it defeats the sole purpose of the field (legal-audit tamper evidence) on every placeholder-using contract at zero cost to hit.
verdict.ship_risk: Low for the forward fix: compute the substituted body first, hash it, persist both in the same update! inside the existing with_lock. touches_client_email=false — the signing flow's mailers (contract_signed_confirmation etc.) already fire and are unchanged; the fix adds no sends. API-compat is safe: document_hash already exists in the /api/v1 serializer and only its value semantics improve; no field rename/removal, no migration needed. Two cautions: (1) do NOT blanket-backfill existing signed contracts — PDFs already delivered to sponsors have the old (mismatched) hash printed in their footer, so re-stamping the DB would create a new mismatch against documents in counterparties' hands; prefer fixing forward and, if remediation is wanted, record the corrected hash in activity metadata rather than overwriting. (2) The countersign path (contracts_controller.rb:167) still overwrites the signing-ceremony hash; preserving it in the contract_signed activity metadata (additive) closes the evidence-destruction hole without schema changes. The external-upload paths that set document_hash from the PDF sha256 (contracts_controller.rb:258, api/v1/deals/contracts_controller.rb:57) use different semantics intentionally and must be left alone.

title: Public /contracts/:token/forward is an unthrottled outbound-mail relay from a real HWFYI mailbox
description: The unauthenticated forward action (contract_signing_controller.rb:90-111, routed at routes.rb:141) lets anyone holding a signing token POST any recipient address and trigger AccountManagementMailer.contract_forwarded, with no rate limit, no per-contract cap, and no confirmation. Delivery goes out via MailboxMailDelivery from the event's contract_from_email or the DEFAULT_FALLBACK_MAILBOX info@hardwarefyi.com — a real, monitored Graph mailbox (mailbox_mail_delivery.rb:25-28). Each forwarded mail also contains the live signing link, and the signature form is fully self-attested (any name/email passes), so every forward recipient can execute the contract.
failure_or_value: Anyone who receives (or leaks) a signing link can script POST /contracts/<token>/forward in a loop to spam arbitrary addresses from info@hardwarefyi.com, torching the domain's sender reputation that all of HWFYI's sponsor outreach depends on. It also silently widens who can legally sign: unlimited forwards x self-attested signature form.
fix_sketch: Add Rails 8 controller rate limiting: rate_limit to: 3, within: 1.hour, only: :forward, with: -> { redirect_to sign_contract_path(token: @contract.signing_token), alert: 'Too many forwards; try later.' } plus a hard per-contract lifetime cap (count 'contract_forwarded' activities, refuse past e.g. 5). Both are server-side only; no change to what the email says or when the sanctioned signing/forward emails send, and client email stays opt-in as today.

verdict.reason: Re-reading the real code confirms every load-bearing claim. routes.rb:135-141 exposes POST /contracts/:token/forward with no authentication (ApplicationController and ContractSigningController add no authenticate_user!). The forward action (contract_signing_controller.rb:90-111) gates only on @contract.can_be_signed? (contract.rb:66-67 = unexpired token, not signed, sent/viewed) plus an email-format regexp — no rate limit, no per-contract cap, no confirmation. AccountManagementMailer.contract_forwarded (account_management_mailer.rb:19-30) sends to the arbitrary recipient and embeds the live signing_url. From address resolves via MailboxMailDelivery to the real monitored info@hardwarefyi.com fallback (mailbox_mail_delivery.rb:28,66-78). The signature form is fully self-attested (create, lines 20-88), so each forward recipient can execute. rate_limit is already used elsewhere in-repo (api/v1/base_controller.rb:6), so the fix is a proven, native Rails 8.1 pattern. No spec covers forward, so regression surface is small. One caveat vs the finding's framing: the attacker must already hold a valid unexpired token for an unsigned contract, so it is not literally 'anyone' — it is anyone who received or leaked a signing link, or a malicious legitimate recipient. That precondition keeps it at medium, not higher.
verdict.ship_risk: Low. The fix (Rails rate_limit + a lifetime forward cap counting contract_forwarded activities) is server-side only, needs no schema change, and relies on an already-configured cache store. It does not alter any email body, does not change when sanctioned signing/forward mail sends, and does not re-enable any banned client-facing send — it only throttles an existing sponsor-facing forward, so no client-email re-enablement risk. No API field renamed/removed. touches_client_email is true only because forward is itself a sponsor-facing send that already exists; the change restricts it. Only real care point: pick a per-contract cap (e.g. 5) high enough not to block a legitimate sponsor re-forwarding to legal/procurement, and fail closed with a friendly redirect rather than an error.

title: Signing links are generated as http:// and fall back to localhost:3000 when APP_HOST is unset
description: Both the mailer (account_management_mailer.rb:127-137) and Contract#signing_url (contract.rb:53-56, 138-140) build sponsor-facing URLs with Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.sign_contract_url(token:, host: ENV.fetch('APP_HOST', 'localhost:3000')) — no :protocol, so url_helpers default to http://, and if the APP_HOST env var is ever missing/renamed on Render the sponsor email silently ships http://localhost:3000/contracts/... links. This hand-rolled host also bypasses config.action_mailer.default_url_options (production.rb:74 sets host kerrihq.com), so there are two competing sources of truth for the mail host.
failure_or_value: Concrete failure modes: (a) every signing/download link in client email is http:// today, relying on the force_ssl redirect and tripping corporate link scanners that downgrade-flag http links in contracts; (b) one env-var slip on a new Render service = sponsors receive dead localhost links and the send is unrecoverable (the contract is already 'sent'). Both hit the single most revenue-critical email the system sends.
fix_sketch: In one shared helper (e.g. Contract#default_host or a ContractUrls module): host = ENV['APP_HOST'].presence || Rails.application.config.action_mailer.default_url_options&.dig(:host); raise in production if blank instead of defaulting to localhost; pass protocol: 'https' (or protocol: Rails.env.production? ? 'https' : 'http') to every *_url call in account_management_mailer.rb:127-133 and contract.rb:55. Purely changes link construction in already-sanctioned emails; adds no sends.

verdict.reason: Re-read confirms every citation: account_management_mailer.rb:127-137 and contract.rb:53-56,138-140 build sponsor-facing signing/download URLs with host: ENV.fetch("APP_HOST", "localhost:3000") and no :protocol; Rails.application.routes.default_url_options is never set anywhere in the repo, so url_for emits http:// today on real send paths (URLs land in contract_signing_request/contract_forwarded HTML+text views and contracts/show copy-link). The dual-source-of-truth claim is also real: production.rb:74 sets action_mailer host kerrihq.com, and sponsor_portal_mailer.rb:63 already uses the better fallback pattern, proving the inconsistency. Mitigations keep this at medium rather than high: force_ssl/assume_ssl (production.rb:28,31) mean the http links 301 to https and work today, and the localhost fallback is latent (APP_HOST is evidently set in prod since cors.rb:11 depends on it). Net: a mitigated live defect (http scheme in the revenue-critical contract email) plus a genuine one-env-var-from-disaster trap that a non-technical owner could never detect until a sponsor reports a dead localhost link. Same weak fallback also exists at sponsor_commitment.rb:133 and company_resource.rb:47, so the shared-helper fix has extra leverage.
verdict.ship_risk: Low blast radius but flag touches_client_email=true: the fix edits link construction inside client-facing contract emails. AccountManagementMailer is the sanctioned approval-gated contract-signature flow, NOT the banned SponsorPortalMailer/SponsorAssetReminderService surface, and the change adds zero sends — keep it strictly to URL building and do not touch the banned mailers. Specific risks: (1) if APP_HOST is ever set with a scheme prefix (cors.rb origin_for_host tolerates "https://..."), naively adding protocol: "https" yields a malformed double-scheme URL — normalize/strip the scheme in the shared helper like cors.rb does; (2) raising in production on blank host converts a silent bad link into a failed mailer job — desirable, but confirm the raise happens before the contract is marked sent so the flow is retryable; (3) no API/DB surface is touched (purely internal URL helpers, no /api/v1 field changes); (4) no spec asserts these URLs' scheme, so the green suite should stay green — verify with a mailer preview and full rspec run before ship.

title: Contract 'viewed' status and activity log are polluted by email link-scanner GETs
description: ContractSigningController#show (lines 9-18) mutates state on a plain GET: it flips status sent -> viewed and appends a contract_viewed activity on EVERY page load. Corporate mail security (Outlook SafeLinks, Mimecast, Google link prefetch) fetches URLs in inbound mail within seconds of delivery, so nearly every contract will show 'viewed by sponsor' moments after sending regardless of whether a human opened it, and each sponsor refresh appends another activity row.
failure_or_value: The viewed signal is one of the few pipeline tells Brian gets on his phone ('they opened the contract, chase now'), and today it is effectively always-on noise: a scanner GET makes an unopened contract indistinguishable from an engaged sponsor, and the activity feed accumulates duplicate contract_viewed rows on every reload.
fix_sketch: Make the GET side-effect-free and record the view from a browser beacon: add a tiny Stimulus controller on the signing page that POSTs to a new mark_viewed member route (post :viewed under the existing token-scoped routes at routes.rb:135-142) after DOMContentLoaded; scanners do not execute JS, humans do. In the action, transition sent->viewed and log activity only if no prior contract_viewed activity exists (or only on the first transition). Keep the existing status flip as a fallback on the POST /sign submit so nothing regresses if JS is off.

verdict.reason: Re-read confirms every load-bearing claim: contract_signing_controller.rb:9-18 mutates on GET (sent→viewed plus an activity row per page load), Trackable#track_activity! (trackable.rb:13-23) has no dedup so duplicate contract_viewed rows accumulate on every human reload unconditionally, the signing URL is emailed to sponsors via AccountManagementMailer#contract_signing_request/#contract_forwarded so mail-security link prefetchers hit the mutating GET with a valid token, and the viewed badge is surfaced in contracts/show.html.erb:17,48 plus the deal timeline, so it is a signal Brian actually reads. No beacon exists today and the fix is feasible as sketched: sponsor layout already loads Stimulus and csrf_meta_tags, and routes.rb:135-141 accepts an additive post :viewed. Only soft spot: 'nearly every contract' overstates it (SafeLinks scans mostly at click; Mimecast/Proofpoint pre-fetch at delivery; some sandboxes execute JS), but the always-on activity-row pollution and idempotency-violating GET stand on their own.
verdict.ship_risk: Low. touches_client_email=false: no new sponsor-facing sends; the existing signing-request mail is untouched, only when state flips changes. Route change is purely additive (new POST :viewed), no DB schema change, no /api/v1 field rename, so agent pollers are unaffected. Residual risks: (1) spec/requests/contract_signing_spec.rb:20-25 asserts viewed-on-GET and must be intentionally rewritten, (2) JS-blocked sponsors will not register viewed until they sign (the fallback flip on POST /sign covers final state, but the early-engagement tell is lost for that minority), (3) JS-executing detonation sandboxes can still fire the beacon occasionally, so pair it with log-once/first-transition dedup and optionally a short delay or interaction gate.

title: Template-defined variables silently override built-in contract data in ContractRenderer
description: ContractRenderer#variables ends with .merge(custom_variables) (line 31), and custom_variables (lines 63-67) returns the template's stored variable defaults. Because custom variables merge LAST, a contract template that declares a variable whose key collides with a built-in (e.g. someone adds 'company_name' or 'total_value' with a sample default like 'ACME Corp' while authoring a template) silently replaces the real deal data with the static default in every contract rendered from that template.
failure_or_value: One innocuous template edit produces legal contracts carrying the wrong company name or wrong total value, and nothing errors — the wrong value is rendered, sent, signed, and hashed. Non-technical Brian would not catch it until a sponsor does.
fix_sketch: Flip precedence so live deal data always wins: custom_variables.merge(built_ins) i.e. change line 31 to start from custom_variables and merge the built-in hash over it (or use built_ins.reverse_merge only for keys not already built-in). Add a ContractTemplate validation rejecting variable keys that collide with ContractRenderer's reserved keys, so template authors get an error instead of silent behavior. Covered by extending spec/services/contract_renderer_spec.rb.

verdict.reason: The code matches the claim: contract_renderer.rb:31 does built_ins.merge(custom_variables), so a template variable named e.g. "company_name" would silently override live deal data in the rendered legal body and stored merged_variables. However, no reachable input path can create the collision today: ContractTemplatesController strong params permit only name/body/status/event_id (no :variables), the template form has no variables field, there is no API/seed/agent writer for ContractTemplate, and the column defaults to {}. custom_variables is therefore always empty on every real code path; the collision requires a Rails console write. Real latent footgun and worthwhile hardening (flip precedence + reserved-key validation), but not a confirmed bug producible through the product.
verdict.ship_risk: Very low. No client email involved (rendering only; sends stay behind existing approval gates). No API field renames: merged_variables keys/values are unchanged in practice because custom_variables is empty everywhere today, so flipping precedence alters no existing output. Adding a ContractTemplate validation on reserved keys can't invalidate existing rows (all have {} variables). Only caveat: if a future variables-editing feature intends per-template overrides of built-ins, the flipped precedence would need an explicit override mechanism instead.

title: Completion proof gate bypassed via idempotent create replay on tasks
description: The proof-gating shipped in PR #115 (a task can only move to done through the API with completion_proof or an applied_at stamp) is enforced only in #update via completion_write_allowed?. The idempotent-replay branch of #create (POST /api/v1/tasks with an external_ref that already exists) calls existing.update!(refresh_attrs) with no proof check at all. The replay also logs the event as 'refreshed' instead of 'completed', and skips the applied->archive/on_complete handling that #update performs, so the proof trail and QUEUE-badge health checks see a done card with no proof.
failure_or_value: Any key with tasks:write POSTs { task: { external_ref: "job-123", status: "done" } } for an existing card -> the card flips to done with zero completion proof, exactly what the done-without-proof queue-health check exists to prevent. An agent that hits a 422 on PATCH can (and eventually will) discover this side door.
fix_sketch: In the replay branch, before existing.update!, run the same guard as #update: return unless completion_write_allowed?(existing.status) (generalize the method to take the task, since it currently reads @task implicitly via params only — it already only inspects params, so just pass original_status = existing.status). Also reuse api_update_event_type/api_update_note so a replay that completes a task records a 'completed'/'applied' event instead of 'refreshed'. Add a request spec: create-replay with status=done and no proof returns 422.

verdict.reason: Re-read confirms every element. In app/controllers/api/v1/tasks_controller.rb the idempotent-replay branch of #create (lines 39-53) calls existing.update!(task_params.except(:external_ref)) with :status permitted (line 157) and never invokes completion_write_allowed?, which is called only from #update (line 74). Concrete repro: POST /api/v1/tasks with a tasks:write key and { task: { external_ref: "<existing>", status: "done" } } returns 200 idempotent_replay and flips the card to done with completed_at stamped (Task before_save, task.rb:79), zero proof, and a "refreshed" event. The tasks:resolve scope check (line 35) doesn't fire because no resolution keys are sent. There is no model-level validation backstop (completion_proof_present? at task.rb:115 is only a query helper), and TaskQueueHealth#agent_done_without_proof_count (task_queue_health.rb:199-202) counts exactly this state since "refreshed" is not in the completed/applied/sent/executed event list — so the bypass directly creates the QUEUE-badge failure the PR #115 gate exists to prevent. No request spec covers replay with status=done (specs only test title refresh and assignee re-homing). Additionally, the same unguarded replay pattern exists in the MCP tool at app/tools/tasks/create_task_tool.rb:68-77, so the fix should cover both entry points. Severity stays high: every around-the-clock agent holds tasks:write, and an LLM agent that 422s on PATCH retrying via POST is a realistic path to silently corrupting the proof trail Brian audits.
verdict.ship_risk: Low. The fix is a controller-side guard addition: no API fields are renamed or removed (only a new 422 on a previously-accepted degenerate request), no schema change, and zero client-email surface (touches_client_email=false). Proof-carrying replays keep working because completion_write_allowed? passes when completion_proof or applied_at is present in the payload. The one compat consideration: any existing automation that completes tasks via POST-replay WITHOUT proof would start receiving 422 — which is the intended enforcement, but worth a pre-ship scan of task_events for "refreshed" events whose changes include a status flip to done, to confirm no legitimate glue relies on the side door. Also patch the parallel hole in app/tools/tasks/create_task_tool.rb or the fix is incomplete. Add the missing request spec (create-replay with status=done and no proof returns 422) and run the full suite, which is currently green on main.

title: Brand wall not enforced on nested deal endpoints, account signals, company deal payloads, and approval decide/execute
description: DealsController#set_deal correctly applies brand_scoped (deals_controller.rb:87), but every nested deal surface resolves the deal with plain current_organization.deals.find: case file entries, stakeholders (person emails), SOW deliverables, and contracts including GET .../contracts/:id/document which streams the signed contract PDF. AccountSignalsController#index and the top-level DeliverablesController have no brand scoping at all. CompaniesController#serialize_with_deals returns ALL of a company's deals (values, stages, health) even when the key is brand-restricted and the company is tagged with both brands. ApprovalRequests #index/#show are brand_scoped but #decide/#execute are not. Note: for a key bound to a brand-restricted user, ApiPolicyContext#brand_restriction_in applies the user's restriction UNCONDITIONALLY (api_policy_context.rb:19), so this is live today for user-bound keys like Benji's, not just after the PR8 enforcement flip.
failure_or_value: A Benji HFYI-restricted key that gets 404 on GET /api/v1/deals/<sw-deal-id> can still GET /api/v1/deals/<sw-deal-id>/contracts/<id>/document and download the other brand's signed contract PDF, list its stakeholders' emails, and read its case file; GET /api/v1/companies/<id> leaks the other brand's deal values. This defeats the entire brand-data-wall build on the API side.
fix_sketch: In each nested set_deal, use brand_scoped(current_organization.deals).find(params[:deal_id]) exactly like DealsController#set_deal. Brand-scope ApprovalRequests#decide/#execute lookups the same way index/show already do. In serialize_with_deals, filter deals through brand_scoped(record.deals) and scope account_signals via their deal/company brand. For AccountSignals#index and the deliverables ledger, join through deals (brand_scoped(..., column: Deal.arel...property_id) or a where(deal_id: brand_scoped(deals))). All changes narrow restricted keys only; the unbound org-wide agent key (api_brand_restriction nil) is a no-op, so existing agents are unaffected.

verdict.reason: Every cited line checks out on re-read. The four nested deal controllers (case_file_entries_controller.rb:24, deal_stakeholders_controller.rb:36, deals/deliverables_controller.rb:38, deals/contracts_controller.rb:77) resolve deals with plain current_organization.deals.find while DealsController#set_deal (deals_controller.rb:87) uses brand_scoped — concrete divergence: an HFYI-restricted user-bound key gets 404 on GET /api/v1/deals/<sw-deal> but 200 (with signed-PDF bytes) on GET /api/v1/deals/<sw-deal>/contracts/<id>/document. The apparent mitigation in ContractsController (authorize @deal, :show? → BrandScope.record_visible?) is a no-op for API callers because BrandScope.restrictions_for returns {} unless the subject is a User (brand_scope.rb:54), and pundit_user is an ApiPolicyContext. The 'live today' claim also holds: ApiPolicyContext#brand_restriction_in (api_policy_context.rb:19) applies a bound user's membership restriction with no BrandScope.enforced? gate (only the key's-own-property fallback is gated), and spec/requests/api/v1/brand_wall_spec.rb asserts exactly that behavior — but tests only deals/companies/people, never the nested endpoints. AccountSignals#index (line 6) and the top-level DeliverablesController have no brand scoping at all; CompaniesController#serialize_with_deals (line 80) dumps all deals of a dual-tagged company (leaking cross-brand deal ids/values/stages, which then feed the unscoped nested endpoints); ApprovalRequests#decide/#execute (lines 65/87) skip the brand_scoped that index/show (lines 20/29) apply. deals.property_id and approval_requests.property_id both exist in schema.rb. Held at high rather than critical: exploitation requires an internal brand-restricted user-bound key, the org boundary is intact, and prod exposure before the PR8 enforcement flip depends on restricted memberships already existing.
verdict.ship_risk: Low-to-medium. No client email anywhere on these paths (touches_client_email=false is correct). API backward-compat is safe by construction: for the unbound org-wide agent key api_brand_restriction is nil and brand_scoped/brand_scoped_companies return the relation unchanged, so 24/7 agent polling sees zero behavior change; no fields are renamed or removed (restricted keys just get 404s/filtered rows, the same semantics deals#show already has). Residual risks: (1) AccountSignals scoping is the fiddliest — signals attach via company OR deal OR person with different brand derivations, so an over-aggressive join could hide legitimate same-brand signals from a restricted key; scope via deal property_id and company taggings, and extend brand_wall_spec.rb to cover it. (2) serialize_with_deals filtering shrinks the deals array for restricted keys viewing dual-tagged companies — intended, but worth a spec asserting unbound keys still get the full array. (3) ApprovalRequests#decide brand-scoping only narrows which requests a restricted key can act on; it does not fix the separate (pre-existing, by-design 'trusted bridge') fact that decide trusts the caller-supplied decided_by_email — don't conflate the two in the fix.

title: Invalid-API-key requests are never rate limited (auth halts before the limiter)
description: before_action :authenticate_api_key! is declared on line 4; rate_limit (line 6) inserts its throttle callback AFTER it. A request with a missing/invalid token renders 401 and halts the chain before the limiter ever runs, so the by: -> { @api_key&.token_prefix || request.remote_ip } IP fallback is dead code. Unauthenticated traffic gets unlimited attempts, each costing a SHA256 + indexed DB lookup. There is also no Rack::Attack or edge throttle in config/initializers.
